question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch Tool indicate at least a 25% probability of a 50+ basis point rate cut at the January 2026 FOMC meeting by October 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The CME FedWatch Tool tracks market expectations for Federal Reserve rate decisions based on futures pricing. Currently, following the September 17, 2025 rate cut of 25 basis points (to 4.00%-4.25%), market expectations are focused on gradual cuts. The CME FedWatch Tool showed a 93.2% probability of a 25bps cut at the October 2025 meeting and 92.7% for December 2025, but no specific probability was reported for a 50+ bps cut in January 2026. Market sentiment shifting toward expecting a larger cut (50+ bps) in January 2026 would be a strong indicator that economic conditions are deteriorating faster than anticipated, potentially prompting more aggressive Fed action.

Sources:
- CME Group FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
- Current Fed Funds Rate (4.00%-4.25%): https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the CME FedWatch Tool's 'Probability of 50+ bps Rate Cut' for the January 27-28, 2026 FOMC meeting reaches or exceeds 25% at any time between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-17 (inclusive), as recorded on the official CME FedWatch Tool page (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html). The probability must be clearly displayed for the January 2026 meeting. If the tool does not explicitly show probabilities for 50+ bps cuts, but shows probabilities for target rate ranges (e.g., 3.50-3.75% if current is 4.00-4.25%), then a probability ≥25% for a target range that implies a 50+ bps cut (e.g., 3.50-3.75% or lower) will also count as Yes. If the FedWatch Tool is unavailable or does not update during the resolution window, the question resolves based on the last available data before October 18, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: Market expectations for Fed rate cuts, as reflected in the CME FedWatch Tool, are a leading indicator of actual Fed policy decisions. A significant increase in the probability of a large (50+ bps) cut in January 2026 would signal that traders anticipate deteriorating economic conditions (e.g., rising unemployment or falling inflation) that could compel the Fed to act more aggressively. This subquestion provides early insight into whether the conditions for a large rate cut are emerging, which is directly relevant to the ultimate question about the Fed's action in January 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: CME FedWatch Tool must show ≥25% probability of 50+ bps rate cut at the January 27-28, 2026 FOMC meeting at any point between September 18 and October 17, 2025. The current rate was 4.00-4.25% after September 2025 cut. A 50+ bps cut at January 2026 would imply a rate of 3.50-3.75% or lower at that meeting specifically. Observable evidence: explicit citation of CME FedWatch probabilities for the January 2026 FOMC meeting showing ≥25% for 50+ bps cumulative cut at that meeting.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Multiple queries: 'CME FedWatch January 2026 FOMC rate cut probability', 'Federal Reserve rate cut expectations January 2026 basis points probability', 'FedWatch January 2026 meeting rate cut probability 50bps 3.25 3.50', 'Fed rate cut 2026 market pricing January FOMC 50 basis points', 'FedWatch tool probability rate cut January 27 28 2026 FOMC 50 basis points'
evidence.step3_event_detection: No article in the search results explicitly cited CME FedWatch probabilities for the January 2026 FOMC meeting. Articles discussed: October 2025 meeting (25bps, ~95% probability), December 2025 meeting (25bps, ~78-80% probability), and general 2026 rate path. One article (Fox Business/LPL) explicitly mentioned 'a pause in rate cuts at the January 2026 meeting.' The Moneycontrol article mentioned >50% probability the rate will be 2.75-3.0% or lower by end-2026, but this is for end-2026 (multiple meetings) not January 2026 specifically.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No articles explicitly stated CME FedWatch showed ≥25% probability of a 50+ bps cut AT the January 2026 meeting. The LPL economist quote in Fox Business article from October 8, 2025 explicitly notes 'a pause in rate cuts at the January 2026 meeting,' suggesting markets expected NO cut at January 2026, let alone a 50+ bps cut. For the 50+ bps threshold to be met at January 2026, markets would need to price a large cut at that specific meeting, which conflicts with 'pause' expectations. The Moneycontrol reference to CME FedWatch showing >50% probability for 2.75-3.0% or lower by end-2026 refers to cumulative cuts across all 2026 meetings, not specifically the January 2026 meeting.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp could be extracted for the specific event (January 2026 FedWatch showing ≥25% for 50+ bps). No article directly reports this specific metric.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found in the available evidence. Could not find any direct citation of FedWatch showing ≥25% for 50+ bps at the January 2026 meeting.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked multiple angles. The Federal Reserve's own dot-plot projected only 1 additional cut for all of 2026, and LPL economist expected a pause at January 2026. Markets were focused on Oct and Dec 2025 cuts. Even if cumulative cuts by end-2025 brought rate to 3.50-3.75%, a further 50+ bps cut AT January 2026 alone (implying 3.00-3.25% or lower) was not widely expected. No contradictory evidence showing ≥25% probability for this specific scenario at the January 2026 meeting was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria requires explicit evidence that the CME FedWatch Tool showed ≥25% probability of 50+ bps rate cut at the January 2026 meeting during the resolution window. No such explicit evidence was found. The available evidence suggests markets expected a pause at January 2026, not a 50+ bps cut. Therefore, the question resolves No, with the resolution datetime being the end of the resolution window.

question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

subquestions.question: Will the US Initial Jobless Claims 4-week moving average exceed 250,000 at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Initial Jobless Claims are a leading indicator of labor market health and potential economic distress. A sustained increase in claims often precedes recessions as layoffs rise. The 4-week moving average smooths out weekly volatility and provides a clearer trend. As of August 2025, the 4-week moving average of Initial Jobless Claims was approximately 220,000 (based on recent trends). The 250,000 threshold represents a significant deterioration from current levels and would indicate worsening labor market conditions. Historically, claims above this level have often coincided with or preceded recessions.

Sources:
- U.S. Department of Labor: https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/UI/claims-data
- Federal Reserve Economic Data: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/IC4WSA
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the seasonally adjusted 4-week moving average of US Initial Jobless Claims, as reported by the U.S. Department of Labor in its weekly Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report, equals or exceeds 250,000 at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The official source is the Department of Labor's weekly report at https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/UI/claims-data. If multiple reports show claims above this threshold during this period, the question resolves Yes. If the Department of Labor stops publishing this data during this period, the question will resolve based on the last available report. If the reporting methodology changes significantly, resolution will be based on the most comparable available metric.
subquestions.rationale: Rising jobless claims are a reliable leading indicator of economic distress and often precede recessions. A sharp increase to 250,000+ would signal deteriorating labor market conditions that could lead to reduced consumer spending and potentially trigger or confirm a recession. This provides an early warning signal for the 2025 recession question while being resolvable within the required timeframe.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The seasonally adjusted 4-week moving average of US Initial Jobless Claims must equal or exceed 250,000 at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), as reported by the U.S. Department of Labor. Observable evidence: DOL weekly reports published during this window showing the 4-week moving average value. Key threshold: 250,000.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'US Initial Jobless Claims 4-week moving average September 2025' — to find all weekly DOL reports published Sept 1–Oct 1. Query 2: 'Department of Labor unemployment insurance weekly claims report September 2025' — to find official report data. Query 3: 'initial jobless claims 4-week moving average 250000 exceeded September October 2025' — to check if threshold was breached. Query 4: 'US weekly jobless claims September 25 2025 moving average Department of Labor' — to find the final report in the window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Four weekly DOL reports were published between Sep 1 and Oct 1, 2025: (1) Sep 4 report (week ending Aug 30): 4-week MA = 231,000. (2) Sep 11 report (week ending Sep 6): 4-week MA = 240,500 (some sources cite 241,000). (3) Sep 18 report (week ending Sep 13): 4-week MA = 240,000 (revised to 240,750). (4) Sep 25 report (week ending Sep 20): 4-week MA = 237,500. No report showed the 4-week MA reaching 250,000.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Comparing all reported 4-week moving averages against the threshold of 250,000: Sep 4 = 231,000 [CalculatedRisk](http://www.calculatedriskblog.com/2025/09/weekly-initial-unemployment-claims.html); Sep 11 = 240,500 [CalculatedRisk](http://www.calculatedriskblog.com/2025/09/weekly-initial-unemployment-claims_11.html); Sep 18 = 240,000 [NASDAQ](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/us-weekly-jobless-claims-pull-back-more-expected); Sep 25 = 237,500 [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/09/25/unemployment-claims/1541758813102/). None of these values equal or exceed 250,000. The criteria for Yes resolution are NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event (4-week MA ≥ 250,000) occurred during the window. The highest value observed was 240,500–241,000 in the Sep 11 report. The window closes at 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No occurrence of 4-week MA ≥ 250,000 was found at any point during the window. The search also covered Sep 25, the last report within the window, confirming the threshold was never breached.
evidence.step7_verification: The Sep 11 spike in weekly claims to 263,000 was attributed to Texas-specific fraud (identity theft in unemployment claims post-Labor Day), which explains why the 4-week MA remained well below 250,000 at 240,500. The subsequent weeks showed clear reversal: 231,000 (Sep 13 week), 218,000 (Sep 20 week). Multiple high-quality sources (CalculatedRisk, NASDAQ, UPI, ActionForex, Yahoo Finance) all confirm the same 4-week MA values — none approaching 250,000. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All four DOL weekly reports published between Sep 1 and Oct 1, 2025 showed 4-week moving averages well below the 250,000 threshold (highest was ~240,500-241,000 on Sep 11). The question resolves No. The window closed at 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z without the threshold being met.

subquestions.question: Will Max Verstappen finish on the podium at the 2025 Singapore Grand Prix?
subquestions.background_information: The Singapore Grand Prix (October 3-5, 2025) is a crucial indicator of Red Bull's performance in high-downforce, hot conditions where they historically struggle. Verstappen has had mixed results at Singapore: he won in 2022 and 2023 but had a non-podium finish in 2023 due to car issues. Red Bull's recent performance improvements (winning Monza and Baku) suggest they may be competitive, but Singapore's high-downforce nature remains a challenge. Verstappen's current championship position (3rd, 69 points behind Piastri) means podium finishes are essential to keep his title hopes alive. A podium here would signal Red Bull's car is competitive across diverse circuits, while a non-podium would suggest persistent weaknesses. Sources: Motorsport.com analysis of Singapore as a benchmark (https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/after-baku-brilliance-here-s-why-singapore-gp-is-key-for-max-verstappen-s-f1-title-hopes/10645689/), Verstappen's Singapore history (F1 official stats: https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2023/races/1222/singapore/race-result.html).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Max Verstappen finishes in 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place in the 2025 Singapore Grand Prix race (October 5, 2025). The race result must be confirmed by the official FIA race classification published on Formula 1's official website (https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2025/races/). If the race is canceled, postponed beyond October 31, 2025, or results are not officially published, the question resolves to 'No' (as Verstappen cannot score podium points). Resolution window: October 1, 2025 (start) to October 5, 2025 (end, race date).
subquestions.rationale: Singapore is a high-downforce, hot circuit where Red Bull has historically struggled (Verstappen had a non-podium here in 2023). A podium finish would indicate Red Bull's recent improvements are genuine across all circuit types, boosting Verstappen's title chances. A non-podium suggests Red Bull's car remains inconsistent, making a 2025 title win less likely given Verstappen's 69-point deficit. This is a crux because forecasters disagree on whether Red Bull's recent wins are temporary or signal a true resurgence.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Max Verstappen must finish 1st, 2nd, or 3rd in the 2025 Singapore Grand Prix on October 5, 2025. Observable evidence: Official FIA/F1 race classification showing Verstappen in top 3. Key entities: Max Verstappen, 2025 Singapore GP. Timing: October 5, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: '2025 Singapore Grand Prix race result podium' (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-05) — to find the race outcome. Query 2: 'Max Verstappen Singapore GP 2025 finish position' (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-05) — to find Verstappen's specific result. Query 3: 'Singapore Grand Prix 2025 race winner result October 5' — to confirm race outcome on race day. Query 4: 'Verstappen Russell Piastri Norris Singapore GP race 2025 winner' (2025-10-05 to 2025-10-06) — to confirm podium finishers.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found on October 5, 2025: All sources consistently report the race result as: 1st George Russell, 2nd Max Verstappen, 3rd Lando Norris, 4th Oscar Piastri. No conflicting results detected. Qualifying data from October 4 was also found but is irrelevant to resolution (race result matters). The Formula 1 official website published race highlights confirming the result.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple sources explicitly confirm Verstappen finished 2nd: [India Today](https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/formula-one/story/george-russell-wins-singapore-gp-mclaren-clinches-constructors-title-2024-2798112-2025-10-05): 'Red Bull's Max Verstappen finished second.' [Formula 1 Official Website](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/highlights-relive-russells-singapore-gp-victory-as-mclaren-clinch-teams.14hQGs9PmCdD9KtYARgyy2): 'Verstappen finished second, with Lando Norris completing the podium ahead of Oscar Piastri.' [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/george-russell-takes-commanding-win-at-singapore-grand-prix-verstappen-and-norris-complete-podium-496865-2025-10-05): 'finishing 5.4 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen of Red Bull, with Lando Norris of McLaren securing third.' [Irish Times](https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/2025/10/05/george-russell-wins-in-singapore-gp-as-lando-norris-nibbles-at-angry-oscar-piastris-lead/): Final positions explicitly listed as Russell (1), Verstappen (2), Norris (3), Piastri (4). Verstappen finishing 2nd satisfies the resolution criteria (podium = top 3).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: All confirming articles are dated October 5, 2025 (race date), within the resolution window. The Formula 1 official website published race highlights on October 5, 2025. Exact timestamp within the day is not provided, but the date is explicitly October 5, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: There is only one Singapore GP race in 2025 (October 5). No earlier qualifying occurrence exists — the race result is a single event. No conflicting earlier result exists.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: All 8+ sources (including the official F1 website) consistently agree on the same podium: Russell 1st, Verstappen 2nd, Norris 3rd. No source disputes Verstappen's 2nd-place finish. The race was not canceled or postponed. Results were officially published on October 5, 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Max Verstappen finished 2nd at the 2025 Singapore Grand Prix on October 5, 2025, which is within the resolution window (October 1–5, 2025). A 2nd-place finish satisfies the resolution criteria (top 3 = podium). Multiple high-quality sources including the official Formula 1 website confirm this result. Resolution: Yes.

question: US strikes Iran by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Iran launch at least 10 ballistic or cruise missiles (excluding short-range rockets) at Israeli territory between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22?
subquestions.background_information:
Iran has demonstrated ongoing missile capabilities and willingness to launch attacks against Israel. In June 2025, Iran launched Operation True Promise III involving hundreds of ballistic missiles and drones at Israeli targets. Recent military exercises in December 2025 showed continued missile testing with Qadr 110, Qadr 380, Qadr 360 cruise missiles and 303 ballistic missiles. Current tensions remain high following the June 2025 conflict where the US joined Israeli strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities. The threshold of 10 missiles represents a significant escalation beyond routine border skirmishes and would indicate Iran's continued willingness to directly attack Israeli territory despite previous retaliations.

Sources:
- Iran holds drills in Gulf, firing ballistic, cruise missiles at simulated targets: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf-firing-ballistic-cruise-missiles-at-simulated-targets
- Iranian MFA putting its cards on table over nation's stance before IAEA: https://en.trend.az/world/iran/3916295.html
- Video shows Iran firing missiles in warning to enemies: https://www.newsweek.com/iran-missile-test-warning-israel-us-1965432
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) or regular military forces launch at least 10 ballistic missiles or cruise missiles (excluding short-range rockets with range <70km) that impact Israeli territory (including airspace violations that result in missile impacts) between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22 (inclusive). Missiles that are intercepted but would have impacted Israeli territory if not intercepted count toward the total. Missiles that fail to launch or are destroyed before launch do not count. The primary resolution source will be official Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) statements and the Israeli Ministry of Defense missile attack reports. Secondary sources include confirmed reporting from major international news agencies (Reuters, AP, AFP) and the US Department of Defense. If conflicting reports exist, the most conservative (lowest) count from credible sources will be used. The question will resolve NO if fewer than 10 qualifying missiles impact Israeli territory during this period.

Resolution sources:
- IDF official website: https://www.idf.il/en/
- Israeli Ministry of Defense: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/ministry_of_defense
- US Department of Defense: https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/
- Reuters Middle East: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/
- Associated Press Middle East: https://apnews.com/hub/middle-east
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a crucial indicator for US-Iran escalation because significant Iranian missile attacks on Israel would likely provoke US military response. Historical precedent shows that when Iran directly attacks Israeli territory at scale (as in June 2025), the US has responded with direct military action against Iranian targets. A major missile attack would demonstrate Iran's continued aggression and willingness to escalate, increasing the probability of US retaliatory strikes. This provides an early warning signal about Iran's offensive posture and likelihood of provoking US military action within the ultimate question timeframe.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition: Iran's IRGC or regular military launches ≥10 ballistic or cruise missiles (range ≥70km) that would impact Israeli territory between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22. Observable evidence required: IDF or major international media reports of actual Iranian missile launches targeting Israel within the window. Key entities: Iran IRGC/military, Israel, ≥10 qualifying missiles. Threshold: 10 missiles minimum. Timing: must occur within the stated window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Iran missile attack Israel 2025 December January' — to find any actual attack reports. 2) 'Iran IRGC ballistic missile strike Israel January 2026' — to find specific IRGC missile launches. 3) 'Iran attack Israel missiles fired launched December 2025 January 2026' — to find direct attack reports. 4) 'IDF air defense intercept Iranian missile alert Israel 2026' — to find interception reports confirming attack. 5) 'Israel Iran war ceasefire no attack January 2026 de-escalation' — to confirm no attack occurred.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events of actual Iranian missile attacks on Israel found during the window. What was found: (1) Iran conducted missile drills in December 2025; (2) Iran threatened to strike Israel/US bases if the US attacked Iran; (3) Israel raised alert levels in January 2026; (4) Israeli cities opened shelters amid fears; (5) Iran and Israel exchanged non-attack pledges via Russia; (6) A Times of Israel blog explicitly stated 'the crisis ultimately subsided without an attack'; (7) IDF confirmed defensive alert posture but no offensive event. All events were preparatory, rhetorical, or diplomatic — not actual missile attacks on Israel.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence matches the resolution criteria. The criteria requires actual Iranian missile launches targeting Israeli territory. Sources reviewed: [Times of Israel blog](https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/when-panic-goes-viral/) explicitly states 'the crisis ultimately subsided without an attack.' [Zero Hedge/WaPo report](https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/iran-israel-secretly-agreed-not-attack-each-other-through-russian-backchannel-wapo) confirms Iran and Israel exchanged non-attack pledges. [IDF statements](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-its-on-alert-for-surprise-scenarios-calls-iran-protests-an-internal-matter/) confirm only alert/defensive posture, no attack occurred. No IDF missile attack report, no DoD report, no Reuters/AP/AFP report of actual Iranian missile launches targeting Israel in this period exists.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for qualifying attack event can be extracted because no qualifying attack occurred. The de-escalation/no-attack conclusion is supported by articles dated 2026-01-15 through 2026-01-17 confirming the crisis subsided without an attack, and by the absence of any attack reports through the end of the window (2026-01-22).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event was found at all during the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find any contradictory evidence: (1) No IDF missile attack report exists; (2) No DoD attack confirmation exists; (3) No Reuters/AP/AFP missile attack reporting exists; (4) Times of Israel explicitly states crisis subsided without attack; (5) Israel-Iran backchannel no-first-strike pledge confirmed by multiple sources (Washington Post, tfiglobalnews, Zero Hedge, NaturalNews); (6) IDF statements confirm only defensive alert — no offensive event confirmed. The previous Iranian missile attack on Israel occurred during the June 2025 12-day war, well outside this window. No contradictory evidence found supporting a Yes resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is NO. During the Dec 23, 2025 – Jan 22, 2026 window, Iran did not launch any ballistic or cruise missiles at Israeli territory. The period was characterized by severe tensions, threats, and preparatory actions, but actual military hostilities did not occur. A mutual non-attack understanding was exchanged through Russian backchannel diplomacy, and the crisis de-escalated around January 14-17, 2026 without any attack. Since no qualifying missiles were launched throughout the entire window, the resolution is definitively No, with the resolution_datetime set to the end of the window.

question: Will Artificial Intelligence be TIME's Person of the Year for 2025?
description:
If listed person/thing is named as TIME's Person of the Year for 2025, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "Yes" if listed person is named TIME's Person of the Year either alone or in conjunction with any other person or thing which is not named in this market, so long as the term is explicitly named. 

For example, if the Person of the Year is "Donald Trump and the MAGA movement", this would qualify to resolve this market to “Trump”. However if the Person of the Year is "The MAGA movement", this would not qualify to resolve this market to “Trump” regardless of whether Trump is depicted on the cover. 

If two or more people or things which are named in this market are named TIME's Person of the Year, this market will resolve in favor of whichever person or thing is listed first. For example if TIME's Person of the Year is “Joe Biden and Kamala Harris”, the market for Joe Biden would resolve to “Yes” and the market for Kamala Harris would resolve to “No”. 

This market will resolve based on Time's cover. Other Time webpages which differ from the cover will not be considered.

This market can resolve after the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is announced by TIME magazine. If for any reason the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is not announced by January 31, 2026 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: this event is mutually exclusive.

question: US x Venezuela military engagement by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. 

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Venezuela's Bolivarian Militia conduct an armed maritime patrol within 50 nautical miles of any US Navy vessel in the Caribbean Sea between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?

Venezuela has mobilized its 4.5 million-strong Bolivarian Militia in response to increased US naval presence in the Caribbean. The militia, created in 2009 and formally integrated into Venezuela's armed forces in 2020, includes civilian volunteers who can be deployed for territorial defense. Recent reports indicate Venezuela has deployed warships and drones to patrol its coastline as US Navy vessels including destroyers, cruisers, and amphibious ships operate in the region. The USS Lake Erie recently transited the Panama Canal into the Caribbean, joining other US vessels. Venezuela's Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino announced 'significant' drone deployments and naval patrols including 'larger vessels further north in our territorial waters.' Current US Navy deployments include approximately 4,500 personnel across multiple vessels including destroyers, amphibious ships, and a cruiser. The militia's potential involvement in maritime patrols represents an escalation risk as civilian-manned vessels could potentially provoke incidents with professional naval forces.

If no official reporting exists but multiple credible news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP) report the incident with specific coordinates, those reports may be used.

If Venezuela deploys armed militia vessels near US Navy ships, it demonstrates both capability and willingness to directly challenge US military presence, making actual military engagement more likely. This is particularly relevant given Venezuela's recent mobilization of 4.5 million militia members and their potential deployment to maritime areas where US vessels are operating.

evidence.step1_decompose: Requires: (1) Bolivarian Militia (civilian militia, not regular FANB) vessels; (2) armed maritime patrol on water; (3) within 50 nautical miles of US Navy vessel; (4) in Caribbean Sea; (5) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01; (6) confirmed by US Navy reporting, MarineTraffic data, or Venezuelan government reporting with coordinates.

All rejected because: (a) Exercises involved FANB and Special Naval Militia but no specific 50nm proximity to US vessels confirmed; (b) F-16s are military aircraft, not militia maritime patrol; (c) No US Navy official reporting of militia vessel proximity; (d) No coordinates provided confirming 50nm threshold.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla receive regulatory approval for fully driverless vehicle operation (Level 4/5 autonomy) in at least one major U.S. city or state by September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tesla's robotaxi launch depends critically on regulatory approval for fully driverless operation. Current Tesla pilot programs require human safety monitors (Austin has passenger-seat monitors, California has driver-seat monitors). Tesla has not yet applied for key permits needed for fully driverless operation in major markets like California. Mercedes-Benz has already received Level 3 approval in Nevada and California using a more conservative regulatory approach with lidar and redundancy systems. Tesla's regulatory strategy appears focused on expanding pilot programs rather than seeking full driverless permits. As of August 2025, Tesla has not filed applications for driverless taxi permits in Nevada despite discussions with regulators. Regulatory approval is a prerequisite for any public driverless taxi service launch.

- https://abc7news.com/mercedes-benz-level-3-autonomous-driving-tesla-robotaxi/ (Mercedes regulatory approval)
- https://nevadacurrent.com/2025/08/25/musk-hiring-for-robotaxi-in-nevada-comes-amid-scrutiny-of-driverless-cars/ (Tesla Nevada permit status)
- https://www.gurufocus.com/news/barclays-expects-long-approval-process-for-teslas-tsla-robotaxi (Barclays regulatory assessment)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if Tesla receives official regulatory approval from any U.S. state or major city (population > 500,000) permitting fully driverless vehicle operation (Level 4 or 5 autonomy as defined by SAE J3016) for commercial passenger service between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 (inclusive). Approval must be publicly announced by the regulatory body (e.g., California DMV, Nevada DMV, Texas DMV, NYC DOT) and specifically authorize Tesla vehicles to operate without any human safety driver present. Approval for testing with safety drivers, private owner use, or non-commercial applications does not count. If approval is announced but later revoked within the resolution window, it still counts as YES. The primary source for resolution will be official regulatory body announcements and press releases. Secondary sources include Tesla's official communications and major news outlets confirming the approval.

Primary resolution sources:
- California DMV Autonomous Vehicle Program: https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/
- Nevada DMV Autonomous Vehicles: https://dmvnv.com/autonomous.htm

- New York City DOT: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/home/home.shtml
subquestions.rationale: Regulatory approval is a critical gating factor for Tesla's driverless robotaxi service. If Tesla cannot secure regulatory approval in any major market by September 8th, it would indicate significant regulatory hurdles that make a public launch by October 31st highly unlikely. Conversely, receiving approval would demonstrate regulatory confidence in Tesla's technology and clear a major path toward launch. This subquestion provides an early indicator of whether Tesla is successfully navigating the regulatory landscape required for its ambitious October timeline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: An official regulatory body (California DMV, Nevada DMV, Texas DMV, NYC DOT, or equivalent for a city with population >500,000) must publicly announce approval of Tesla vehicles for fully driverless (Level 4 or 5 SAE J3016) commercial passenger service without any human safety driver present, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 inclusive. Observable evidence required: Official press release or announcement from regulatory body; must specifically authorize Tesla (not generic AV testing); must be Level 4/5 commercial operation; no safety driver required.

evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) abcmoney.co.uk article (Sep 5, 2025) claims Tesla announced FSD 'reached Level 4 autonomy' — REJECTED: This appears to be unreliable/speculative content, contradicted by multiple authoritative sources (TheStreet, Gizmodo, Mashable, IBD) published the same week. (D) NHTSA proposed easing rules (Sep 4) — future rulemaking, not a specific Tesla approval for Level 4/5.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event satisfies all criteria: (1) Tesla's FSD is explicitly confirmed as SAE Level 2 throughout the window by [TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/qualcomm-just-made-a-massive-leap-into-teslas-turf-), [Gizmodo](https://gizmodo.com/tesla-robotaxi-2000653821), [Mashable](https://mashable.com/article/tesla-robotaxi-human-safety-monitor-drivers-seat), and [Investor's Business Daily](https://www.investors.com/news/tesla-stock-bulls-driver-seat-robotaxi-safety-monitors/). (2) California DMV/CPUC explicitly had NOT granted Tesla driverless deployment permits per [SFist](https://sfist.com/2025/09/04/tesla-opens-up-robotoaxi-app-to-all-in-sf-but-can-they-even-do-this/). evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No valid timestamp exists for a qualifying event (Level 4/5 regulatory approval for Tesla commercial driverless operation) within the window Sep 1-8, 2025. evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality sources explicitly confirm no qualifying approval existed: TheStreet (Sep 7): 'Tesla's FSD technology remains classified at SAE Level 2'; Gizmodo (Sep 5): Tesla 'remains a Level 2 system that needs constant driver supervision'; Investor's Business Daily (Sep 3): 'California regulators will not allow driverless operation without extensive testing'; SFist (Sep 4): 'neither the CPUC nor the California DMV has granted Tesla permits for fully autonomous vehicles'; Barclays note (Aug 22): 'obtaining the necessary permits for a true Robotaxi service in California may take longer than expected.' The abcmoney.co.uk article's claim of 'Level 4 achievement' is a technology milestone claim by Tesla itself, not regulatory approval, and is directly contradicted by sources from the same date range.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is NO. Throughout the September 1-8, 2025 window, Tesla's FSD remained classified as SAE Level 2 by regulators and multiple independent sources. No U.S. state or major city regulatory body issued official approval for Tesla to operate fully driverless (Level 4/5) commercial passenger vehicles without a safety driver. California DMV/CPUC explicitly had not granted such permits; Tesla had not even applied for California's Driverless Deployment Permit. subquestions.question: Will the United Nations General Assembly adopt a resolution recognizing Palestine as a full member state with a vote margin of at least 50 votes before 2025-10-01?

A strong UN vote for Palestinian statehood would indicate international momentum toward meeting Saudi Arabia's conditions, making normalization more likely. Conversely, a weak vote margin or failure to pass would suggest continued obstacles to Palestinian statehood, reducing the likelihood of Saudi-Israeli normalization in 2025. This provides an early indicator of whether the diplomatic conditions Saudi Arabia requires are being met.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: UNGA adopts a resolution explicitly granting Palestine full UN membership (i.e., admitting Palestine as the 194th UN member state with voting rights), with Yes votes - No votes ≥ 50, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Observable evidence: official UN press release or major news organization reporting Palestine admitted as full UN member via UNGA vote. Parliamentary discussions about peace negotiations would indicate Ukraine's political readiness to engage in formal peace talks and could signal movement toward a potential peace deal. The session must be officially convened and recognized by the Ukrainian government.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful indicator because parliamentary authorization is likely required for Ukraine to formally engage in peace negotiations with Russia. If the Ukrainian parliament holds sessions specifically discussing peace talks, it signals political willingness to pursue a negotiated settlement. Conversely, if no such discussions occur by late October 2025, it suggests Ukraine remains focused on military resistance rather than diplomatic solutions, making a 2025 peace deal less likely. This question addresses a concrete political event that would precede any actual peace agreement signing.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Official Verkhovna Rada session between Oct 1–31, 2025 where the agenda explicitly includes discussion or voting on peace negotiations with Russia (authorization of negotiations, approval of negotiation frameworks, or voting on negotiation mandates). question: Ukraine recognizes Russian sovereignty over its territory by December 31, 2025?

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995, “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia, which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement, is an example of a qualifying agreement.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Andrew Cuomo publicly call for Eric Adams to drop out of the NYC mayoral race by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Multiple news reports indicate that political observers believe either Adams or Cuomo needs to drop out for the other to have a chance against Mamdani. Former Governor David Paterson, who initially supported Cuomo but recently endorsed Adams, had previously suggested that either Adams or Cuomo should drop out to prevent Mamdani from winning. Cuomo has already urged other candidates to drop out, and attorney Jim Walden has proposed a ranked-choice poll among the non-Democratic candidates to consolidate support. Current polling shows Mamdani with a significant lead, making strategic coordination between Cuomo and Adams potentially crucial for either to have a chance.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Andrew Cuomo makes a public statement (via press conference, official campaign release, or verified social media account) explicitly calling for Eric Adams to withdraw from the 2025 NYC mayoral race between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (11:59 PM ET). The statement must be unambiguous and directly address Adams' candidacy (e.g., 'Eric Adams should drop out,' 'I call on Mayor Adams to withdraw,' etc.). Statements merely suggesting consolidation against Mamdani without specifically naming Adams do NOT count. The primary resolution source will be Cuomo's official campaign website (https://cuomo2025.com) or verified Twitter/X account (@andrewcuomo). Secondary sources include major news outlets reporting on such a statement. If the event is postponed beyond October 1, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as an early indicator of strategic dynamics between Cuomo and Adams. If Cuomo publicly calls for Adams to drop out, it suggests he sees Adams as the weaker candidate and wants to consolidate the anti-Mamdani vote behind himself, making an Adams endorsement of Cuomo less likely. Conversely, if Cuomo doesn't make such a call, it could indicate either private coordination efforts or a willingness to coexist in the race, potentially leaving room for future endorsements. This captures a concrete action Cuomo might take that would reveal his assessment of the race and relationship with Adams.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Andrew Cuomo makes a public, unambiguous statement explicitly calling on Eric Adams to withdraw from the 2025 NYC mayoral race between September 1–October 1, 2025. evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest confirmed date with an explicit Cuomo quote calling on Adams to drop out is September 5, 2025 (from Indian Express, Yahoo News, NBC New York articles dated Sept 5, 2025). The amNewYork article from September 2, 2025 references this happening as of that date, suggesting the first occurrence may be September 2, 2025 at the latest. evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent major news sources (Indian Express, Yahoo News, NBC New York, amNewYork, Chosun.com, Daily News) corroborate Cuomo calling on Adams to drop out, with multiple articles citing his specific quote. evidence.step8_final_decision: Yes. subquestions.question: Will the monthly customs duties collected by the U.S. Treasury Department exceed $25 billion in September 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Customs duties collected by the U.S. Treasury have reached record levels in 2025, with monthly collections hitting $27.2 billion in June and $28 billion in July. These collections have contributed significantly to federal revenue, making tariffs the fourth-largest revenue source. For FY2025 through July, total customs duties reached approximately $150 billion. The ultimate question concerns whether FY2025 customs duties will exceed $250 billion. Monthly collections in September 2025 will provide a strong indicator of whether this target is achievable, as September is the final month of FY2025 (which ends September 30, 2025). Current monthly collections are running well above the ~$18.5 billion monthly average needed to reach $250 billion for the full fiscal year.

Sources:
- https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/files/reports-statements/financial-report/2024/notes-to-the-financial-statements19.pdf
- https://www.reuters.com/markets/us/us-customs-duties-top-100-billion-first-time-fiscal-year-2025-07-11/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement for September 2025 reports customs duties (also called 'customs duties and fees' or 'customs revenue') exceeding $25 billion USD. The data must be published on the Treasury Department's website (https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/276/MTS-2025-09.pdf) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). If the Treasury Department does not publish the September 2025 Monthly Treasury Statement by 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC, this question resolves to No. The resolution source is the Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement publication.
subquestions.rationale: September 2025 is the final month of FY2025. A monthly collection exceeding $25 billion would indicate strong ongoing tariff revenue momentum, making it more likely that the full fiscal year total exceeds $250 billion. Conversely, collections below this threshold would suggest a slowdown in tariff revenue, making the $250 billion target less likely. This subquestion provides an early and concrete indicator of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes: The U.S. Treasury Department's MTS-2025-09.pdf must be published on home.treasury.gov between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z AND report customs duties exceeding $25 billion. Critical: the resolution criteria state that if the September 2025 MTS is not published by 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC, the question resolves No.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: (1) Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement customs duties September 2025; (2) US customs duties revenue September 2025 billion Treasury; (3) Monthly Treasury Statement September 2025 MTS fiscal year end customs; (4) US budget deficit fiscal year 2025 September customs duties tariff revenue October; (5) US government shutdown October 2025 Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement delay; (6) Treasury Monthly Budget Statement MTS-2025-09 September fiscal year release schedule; (7) US September 2025 customs duties tariff revenue $30 billion monthly; (8) Monthly Treasury Statement September 2025 published release October shutdown delayed; (9) Treasury fiscal year 2025 final budget data official release customs September
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key findings: (1) U.S. government shutdown began October 1, 2025 after Congress failed to pass a continuing resolution. (2) Reuters/Investing.com (Oct 13) explicitly states Treasury Department's Monthly Budget Statement was marked 'TBD' due to the shutdown. (3) Fox10 article (Oct 7) references Treasury data showing September 2025 tariff revenue of $31.3 billion. (4) ArcaMax article states 'The CBO report was released amid a federal government shutdown, which may delay the official Treasury release of the September and 2025 fiscal-year data.' (5) Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed official Treasury economic data releases are delayed until the shutdown ends. (6) The August 2025 MTS was published September 11 — about 11 days after month-end. The September 2025 MTS would normally be published in mid-October.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require the September 2025 MTS to be published by 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z. The historical pattern shows MTS releases occur ~10-14 days after month-end. The September 2025 MTS covers data through September 30, 2025, so it cannot be published before September 30. The government shutdown starting October 1 further confirms no publication could occur by October 1. This could trigger internal party challenges, loss of parliamentary confidence, or pressure for leadership change. The July 2025 reports already show discontent within Labour ranks and collapsing public support, making polling performance a crucial near-term indicator of Starmer's political survival.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Any qualifying poll (YouGov, Ipsos, Survation, Opinium, Deltapoll, or Savanta) published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 shows Labour's lead over the second-place party dropping below 10 percentage points. Lead = Labour% minus second-place party%. Must appear in official polling firm website or specified major UK newspaper.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'UK opinion poll Labour lead September 2025' — to find relevant polls; 2. 'YouGov Ipsos Survation Opinium poll Labour Conservative September 2025' — to find qualifying polls from named firms; 3. 'UK voting intention poll Labour Reform Conservative percentage points September 2025' — to find exact vote share figures; 4. 'Labour trailing Reform UK second place opinion poll September 2025 voting intention' — to understand Labour's position; 5. 'Ipsos poll Labour Reform September 2025 voting intention percentage' — to find specific Ipsos data; 6. 'Labour first place poll September 2025 ahead Conservatives Reform UK' — to check if Labour was ever first in this period.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple qualifying polls identified: (1) Opinium (6 Sept 2025): Reform 30%, Labour 23%, Conservatives 17% — Labour is in SECOND place, trailing Reform; (2) Opinium (21 Sept 2025): Reform 31%, Labour 22%, Conservatives 17% — Labour is in SECOND place; (3) YouGov MRP (26 Sept 2025): Reform 27%, Labour 21%, Conservatives 17% — Labour is in SECOND place; (4) Ipsos (27 Sept 2025): Reform 34%, Labour 22%, Conservatives 14% — Labour is in SECOND place. In ALL September 2025 polls from qualifying firms, Reform UK leads with Labour in second place. CRITICAL ISSUE: Labour is not in first place in any poll during this period, so the notion of 'Labour's lead over the second-place party' is ambiguous — Labour IS the second-place party.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria assumes Labour is in first place (it asks about 'Labour's lead over the second-place party'). In reality, all September 2025 polls show Reform UK leading, with Labour in second place. If we interpret this strictly as Labour% minus the party immediately behind Labour (Conservatives), then: Opinium (6 Sept): 23%-17% = 6 points lead over Conservatives (below 10); Opinium (21 Sept): 22%-17% = 5 points lead over Conservatives (below 10); YouGov MRP (26 Sept): 21%-17% = 4 points lead over Conservatives (below 10); Ipsos (27 Sept): 22%-14% = 8 points lead over Conservatives (below 10). Under this interpretation, ALL qualifying polls show Labour's margin over the next party (Conservatives) below 10 points, satisfying the Yes condition. However, the more natural reading — that Labour is the leading party whose lead over second place is measured — fails because Labour is not in first place. This ambiguity creates a fundamental interpretation problem.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest qualifying poll from approved firms is Opinium (published 6 September 2025, a Saturday, covered by Wales Online and London Business News). If the question resolves Yes under the interpretation that Labour's margin over the party behind it (Conservatives) is below 10 points, the first qualifying instance is 2025-09-06. However, the timestamp from the Opinium poll is reported as 'released September 6, 2025' with no exact time.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: All qualifying September 2025 polls from approved firms show Reform UK leading with Labour in second place, with Labour maintaining only a small lead (4-8 points) over the Conservatives in third. The first such poll in the window appears to be the Opinium poll of 6 September 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: The evidence is consistent across multiple polls from qualifying firms: Reform UK overtook Labour before September 2025 and maintained a substantial lead throughout the entire September 1 - October 1, 2025 window. No poll from any qualifying firm shows Labour in first place during this period. The resolution criteria appears to have been written assuming Labour would be leading the polls, which contradicts the actual polling reality. This ambiguity — whether the question means (a) Labour leads over the next party behind it (below 10, resolves Yes) or (b) Labour's lead as first-place party (which doesn't apply as Labour isn't first) — makes resolution uncertain.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question is fundamentally ambiguous given the actual polling situation. The resolution criteria was written assuming Labour would be in first place (having a 'lead' over the second-place party). In September 2025, Labour is consistently in second place behind Reform UK in all qualifying polls. This could be interpreted two ways: (1) If 'Labour's lead over the second-place party' is taken as Labour's percentage minus the party immediately behind it (Conservatives in third place), then Labour's margin (approximately 4-8 points across all polls) is below 10, meaning the question resolves Yes — and the first qualifying poll is Opinium on 6 September 2025. (2) If the question is understood as Labour being the leading party and its lead over the party in second place being measured, then the premise fails because Labour isn't first, making the question unresolvable. Given this fundamental ambiguity in the resolution criteria versus the actual polling landscape (where Labour trails Reform, contrary to the question's assumption), the question is best deemed unresolvable (resolvable=false). The resolution criteria does not contemplate the scenario where Labour is not in first place.

question: NYSE marketwide circuit breaker in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a marketwide circuit breaker is triggered on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) at any time between January 1 and market close on December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A marketwide circuit breaker is defined as a trading halt that is initiated due to significant declines in the S&P 500 Index, specifically a Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3 halt as per NYSE rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the NYSE, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) close at or above 40 on at least one trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) is a real-time market index representing the market's expectations for volatility over the coming 30 days, derived from S&P 500 index options. It is often referred to as the 'fear gauge' as it tends to spike during periods of market stress and sharp declines. Historically, VIX levels above 40 are associated with extreme market turmoil and often precede or accompany significant market declines that could trigger circuit breakers. For example, during the March 2020 COVID-19 crash, the VIX reached 82.69, and marketwide circuit breakers were triggered multiple times. As of late August 2025, the VIX has been elevated due to trade tensions and tariff concerns, with recent closes around 25-30 (based on pre-September 2025 data from the provided articles). A VIX close of 40 or higher would indicate severe market stress, increasing the likelihood of large S&P 500 declines that could trigger NYSE circuit breakers in 2025.

Sources:
- Cboe Global Markets VIX Index: https://www.cboe.com/vix/
- Historical VIX data (Cboe): https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/vix_historical_data/
- Market volatility and circuit breakers (SEC): https://www.sec.gov/investor/alerts/circuitbreakers.pdf
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) closes at or above 40.0 on at least one trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), as reported by the official Cboe Global Markets VIX Index closing values published on their website. The resolution source is the historical data table at https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/vix_historical_data/. If the Cboe website is unavailable or does not publish data for a day, alternative reliable sources such as Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/quote/VIX:IND) or Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/) may be used, with preference given to Cboe data if discrepancies arise. If no official or reliable source provides VIX closing data for the period, the question resolves as 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: The VIX is a leading indicator of market stress and volatility. A close at or above 40 signifies extreme fear and potential for rapid market declines, which are necessary conditions for triggering NYSE circuit breakers. This subquestion provides an early warning signal for the ultimate question, as high VIX levels in September 2025 would suggest increased risk of a circuit breaker event in 2025 due to ongoing volatility. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question but a probabilistic indicator based on market sentiment.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The CBOE VIX index must CLOSE at or above 40.0 on at least one trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Observable evidence: Official closing price of VIX ≥ 40.0 reported by any reliable financial source. Key entities: CBOE Volatility Index (VIX spot index), not VXX or VIX futures. Threshold: 40.0 exactly or higher. Timing: at least one trading day's close within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'VIX volatility index closing value September 2025' - to find reported VIX closing values; 2) 'Cboe VIX index level high spike September October 2025' - to find any spike above 40; 3) 'VIX 32 September 18 19 2025 market volatility' - to investigate the anomalous 32.64 reference; 4) 'VIX closing value September 29 30 October 1 2025' - to check end of window; 5) 'S&P 500 VIX fear gauge September 29 2025 market close' - to check specific closing values; 6) 'market crash September 2025 stock sell-off VIX spike high' - to find any extreme events.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Sep 2 spike: VIX rose to 19.2 intraday, not a close above 40. (2) An Investing.com article from Sep 30 mentioned 'VIX peaked at 32.64 on September 18 and was 32.68 on Monday' - REJECTED as clearly inconsistent with all other sources showing VIX at 15.72 on Sep 18 (Yahoo Finance closing data), 15.70 on Sep 19, 16.18 on Sep 25, 15.29 on Sep 26. The Investing.com reference likely refers to VXX ETF price or another volatility derivative, not the spot VIX index. No event found with VIX closing at or above 40.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple explicit VIX closing values were reported throughout September 2025: Sep 9: 15.11 [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/stock-market-news-sep-9-132400918.html); Sep 18: 15.72 [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/stock-market-news-sep-18-131900325.html); Sep 19: 15.70 [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/stock-market-news-sep-19-132600670.html); Sep 25: 16.18 [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/stock-market-news-sep-25-075300739.html); Sep 26: 15.29 [Chosun.com](https://www.chosun.com/english/world-en/2025/09/27/WZZRTRXXSVEFJCTKA3NAPZKX6E/). Sep 29: WFMZ reports VIX 'fell from the previous week.' Sep 30: S&P 500 at record high - incompatible with VIX above 40. None of the criteria for Yes is met.

The questionable 32.64 reference in a single Investing.com article is inconsistent with all other sources and almost certainly refers to a different instrument.

Multiple explicit data points from Yahoo Finance, Benzinga, Chosun.com, MarketWatch, and others consistently show VIX between 14 and 20 throughout the September 1 to October 1, 2025 period. evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is overwhelming and consistent: the CBOE VIX index did not close at or above 40 on any trading day between September 1 and October 1, 2025. The market was near record highs with very low volatility throughout September 2025. question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.0% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 10-year yield reaches or is higher than the listed value for any date between April 9 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury 10-year yield close at or above 4.70% on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information: The 10-year Treasury yield is a key benchmark for interest rates globally, influenced by inflation expectations, Federal Reserve policy, and fiscal conditions. As of 2025-07-31, the 10-year yield was 4.360% (Morningstar). Recent market dynamics, including concerns over tariffs, fiscal deficits, and Fed policy uncertainty, have driven volatility. A yield surge to 4.70%—near the upper end of its 2025 range (52-week high: 4.802% on 2025-01-13)—would signal heightened inflation fears or bond market stress, potentially foreshadowing a move toward 5.0% later in 2025. Sources: https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/20250731178/10year-treasury-yield-rises-to-4360-this-month-data-talk, https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Treasury's 'Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates' for the '10 Yr' column (source: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025) reports a closing yield at or above 4.70% on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive). If the source is unavailable, the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) 10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate (DGS10) (source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10) may be used as a backup. The resolution window is strictly from 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-30; any event outside this period does not count.
subquestions.rationale: A rapid rise in the 10-year yield to 4.70% in September 2025—close to its 2025 high—would indicate accelerating inflation expectations, fiscal concerns, or reduced Fed dovishness, increasing the likelihood of the yield reaching 5.0% by year-end. This subquestion captures near-term momentum and market sentiment shifts that could drive the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: US 10-year Treasury yield must close at or above 4.70% on any trading day between Sept 1-30, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: Official Treasury yield data (treasury.gov) or reliable financial reporting showing a ≥4.70% close. Key threshold: 4.70%. Period: 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-30.

Query 2: '10-year Treasury yield 4.70% September 2025' (specific threshold search). Query 3: 'Treasury 10-year yield high September 2025 beginning month' (early September high yields). Query 4: '10-year Treasury yield close late September 2025' (late September yields).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The highest reported yield in September 2025 was approximately 4.28% on September 2, 2025 [InstaForex/MarketWatch Sept 2](https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2733646). This is 42 basis points below the 4.70% threshold. The yield then declined substantially for the rest of the month, reaching a 5-month low near 4.0% on Sept 17 [InstaForex Sept 17](https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2748245) and ending near 4.14-4.16% by late September [InstaForex Sept 29](https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2757309). No yield reading at or above 4.70% was reported.

evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at any point in September 2025.

The Morningstar/MarketWatch article from Sept 8 notes the yield fell from a peak of 4.8% on Jan. 13 to below 4.1%, confirming the yield was well below 4.70% for the entire month. No contradictory evidence was found. All sources consistently show yields below 4.3% at most.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The US 10-year Treasury yield remained well below the 4.70% threshold throughout September 2025, peaking around 4.28% on September 2 and declining substantially over the month.
