Trump has not yet made a bilateral visit to Germany (only attending the 2017 G20 summit there). Merz recently visited Washington in June 2025 to discuss trade and Ukraine, indicating ongoing diplomatic channels. The current relationship appears strained due to Trump's tariff threats and differing views on European defense. A meeting in October 2025 would signal improved relations and potential planning for a future visit. Sources: Council on Foreign Relations (https://www.cfr.org/), Statista (https://www.statista.com/chart/32717/countries-donald-trump-has-visited-as-president/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if an official bilateral meeting (in-person or via secure video conference) between U.S. President Donald Trump and German Chancellor Merz is confirmed to have occurred between 2025-10-01 00:00 UTC and 2025-10-22 23:59 UTC. Resolution will be based on official announcements from the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or German Federal Government (https://www.bundesregierung.de/), or reporting from at least two of the following major news agencies: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), Deutsche Presse-Agentur (https://www.dpa.de/). The meeting must be explicitly billed as a bilateral meeting between the two leaders (not part of a multilateral summit). If the meeting is postponed beyond 2025-10-22, it resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A bilateral meeting between Trump and Merz would indicate active diplomatic engagement and potential trip planning. If they meet (especially in person), it increases the likelihood of a future Germany visit. If no meeting occurs during this critical pre-election period, it suggests continued diplomatic distance, making a 2025 Germany visit less likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: official bilateral meeting (in-person OR secure video conference) between Trump and Merz, explicitly billed as bilateral (not part of multilateral summit), confirmed by White House/German Federal Government, or two of Reuters/AP/DPA, between 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z and 2025-10-22T23:59:59Z.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump Merz bilateral meeting October 2025' - to find direct bilateral; 2) 'Trump German Chancellor Merz meeting talks 2025' - general meetings; 3) 'Trump Merz meeting in person video conference bilateral October 2025' - looking for format; 4) 'Merz Trump bilateral sideline meeting Sharm el-Sheikh October 13' - specific summit bilateral; 5) 'Trump Merz White House meeting October 2025' - possible White House visit; 6) 'Trump Merz phone call telephone conversation October 2025' - to distinguish phone calls from video/in-person; 7) 'Merz Trump bilateral Egypt sideline Ukraine talks in person'; 8) 'Merz Washington visit US trip bilateral meeting October 2025'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate 1: October 5, 2025 - Trump-Merz telephone conversation (confirmed by multiple sources, explicitly described as 'telephone conversation' or 'phone call'). REJECTED: criteria requires in-person or secure video conference, not a phone call. Candidate 2: October 13, 2025 - Both Trump and Merz present at Sharm el-Sheikh multilateral summit. REJECTED: criteria explicitly excludes multilateral summits; no dedicated bilateral between Trump and Merz was reported from this event. Merz said he 'would like to seize the opportunity this afternoon to once again talk to US president' suggesting no formal bilateral was scheduled. No source reported a Trump-Merz dedicated bilateral meeting at this summit. No other candidates found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The October 5 phone call [Devdiscourse](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/law-order/3653341-diplomatic-dialogues-merz-and-trump-tackle-global-crises) and [charter97.org](https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/10/5/658203/) does NOT match criteria (phone call, not in-person/video conference). The October 13 Sharm el-Sheikh summit [KUTV](https://kutv.com/news/nation-world/trump-and-world-leaders-convene-in-egypt-to-discuss-the-future-of-gaza-ceasefire-palestine-hamas-benjamin-netanyahu-united-nations-abdel-fattah-elsisi-phase-one-hostages) and [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2029083) does NOT match criteria (multilateral summit, no dedicated Trump-Merz bilateral confirmed). No qualifying events found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp found within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence found - no in-person or video conference bilateral between Trump and Merz was reported during the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove No conclusion: Searched for any Trump-Merz in-person meeting, White House visit, video conference, or dedicated bilateral at sidelines of multilateral events. No contradictory evidence found. The pattern of evidence (phone calls, multilateral summits) consistently shows no dedicated Trump-Merz bilateral meeting of the required format occurred during the window. Merz's October 13 statement that he 'would like to' talk to Trump suggests no bilateral was pre-arranged. The October 5 interaction is consistently described as a phone call across all sources.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying bilateral meeting (in-person or via secure video conference) between Trump and Merz was confirmed to have occurred between October 1-22, 2025. The only Trump-Merz interaction was a phone call (October 5), which does not meet the criteria. Both attended the multilateral Sharm el-Sheikh summit (October 13), but the criteria explicitly excludes multilateral summits, and no dedicated bilateral meeting between the two was reported. The window closed with no qualifying event occurring. Resolution: No.

question: Will NVIDIA be the second-largest company in the world by market cap on December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to the second-largest company in the world by market cap on December 31, 2025, as of market close.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Nvidia's market capitalization close at or above $4.8 trillion on any trading day between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13?
subquestions.background_information:
As of October 1, 2025, Nvidia reached a market cap of $4.53 trillion and became the world's largest company. Currently, Microsoft is the second-largest company with approximately $3.74 trillion market cap (as of July 2025). For Nvidia to maintain its position as second-largest by year-end 2025, it would need to significantly outperform competitors like Microsoft and Apple. A market cap of $4.8 trillion represents approximately a 6% increase from Nvidia's recent peak and would demonstrate continued momentum in AI-driven growth. The current market cap threshold for being second-largest appears to be around $3.9-4.0 trillion based on Apple's recent valuations.

Sources:
- Yahoo! Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/nvidia-becomes-world-largest-company-203000845.html
- Mint: https://www.livemint.com/market/who-s-next-to-touch-m-cap-of-4-trillion-and-can-nvidia-hit-6-trillion/amp-11720746611510.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Nvidia's market capitalization closes at or above $4.800 trillion on any trading day between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 (inclusive). Market capitalization will be calculated as the closing share price multiplied by the number of outstanding shares as reported by Yahoo Finance. The primary data source will be Yahoo Finance's Nvidia quote page (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA). If Yahoo Finance becomes unavailable or changes its methodology, MarketWatch (https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/stock/nvda) will be used as a secondary source. If neither source is available, Bloomberg Terminal data will be considered authoritative. The resolution will be based on the first trading day when the threshold is met or exceeded.
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of Nvidia's ability to maintain its dominant market position against competitors like Microsoft and Apple. If Nvidia reaches $4.8 trillion within this short timeframe, it would demonstrate strong momentum and investor confidence in its AI-driven growth story, making it more likely to maintain its position as a top-2 company by year-end. Conversely, failure to reach this threshold could indicate market saturation, competitive pressures, or diminishing returns from AI investments.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Nvidia's closing market capitalization must be ≥ $4.800 trillion on any trading day between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 inclusive. Observable evidence: closing share price × shares outstanding ≥ $4.8T as reported by Yahoo Finance or equivalent. Key entities: NVDA (Nvidia), $4.8T threshold.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Nvidia market capitalization trillion 2025 October November' — general search for market cap data. 2) 'NVDA stock price closing October November 2025' — specific closing price data. 3) 'Nvidia NVDA stock price $4.8 trillion market cap October 2025' — targeted threshold search. 4) 'Nvidia NVDA closing price October 29 2025 $5 trillion market cap confirmed' — confirmation of $5T milestone. 5) 'Nvidia market cap October 28 2025 closing price $4.89 trillion' — first day above threshold.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Oct 14: ~$180.82/share, market cap ~$4.38T (below). Oct 19: market cap $4.58T (below). Oct 21-22: market cap ~$4.44T (below). Oct 27: market cap $4.46T (below). Oct 28: closing price $201.03, market cap $4.885T (ABOVE $4.8T — qualifying). Oct 29: closing price $207.04–207.16, market cap $5.03T (qualifying). Nov 6: market cap $4.74T (above). No qualifying events before Oct 28 in the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: October 28, 2025: Nvidia closed at $201.03/share with market cap of $4.885 trillion per [The Globe and Mail](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/article-nvidias-stock-market-value-nears-us5-trillion-the-most-ever-for-a/), [Deadline](https://deadline.com/2025/10/nvidia-nears-record-5-trillion-valuation-after-gtc-news-1236600615/), [Chosun.com](https://www.chosun.com/english/world-en/2025/10/29/EVPF67VCMJCX5NQPOMMEPCDWWQ/). $4.885T > $4.800T threshold. Explicitly stated, not inferred. Date is within window. October 29, 2025: market cap $5.03T per [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3169127/nvidia-nvda-reaches-historic-5-trillion-market-cap-amid-ai-boom), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/nvidia-becomes-first-company-to-close-abover-5-trillion-market-cap-133101454.html) — also qualifying but not first.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First qualifying event: October 28, 2025 market close (UTC equivalent: 2025-10-28T21:00:00Z, corresponding to 4:00 PM ET NYSE close). Closing market cap: $4.885 trillion. Multiple sources explicitly confirm this figure.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence exists within the window. All data before October 28 shows market cap below $4.8T: Oct 14 (~$4.38T), Oct 16 (~$4.4T), Oct 19 ($4.58T), Oct 21-22 (~$4.44T), Oct 24 (~$4.38T), Oct 27 ($4.46T). October 28 is confirmed as first qualifying date.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality sources (Yahoo Finance, Globe and Mail, Deadline, GuruFocus, CBS News, Japan Times, Hindustan Times, CBC News) all consistently confirm that October 28 closing market cap was ~$4.885T and October 29 closing was ~$5.03T. No contradictory evidence found. The question window (Oct 14 – Nov 13) clearly encompasses Oct 28. The threshold ($4.8T) is lower than confirmed closes on Oct 28 ($4.885T) and Oct 29 ($5.03T).
evidence.step8_final_decision: Nvidia's market capitalization closed at $4.885 trillion on October 28, 2025 — the first trading day within the window where the $4.800 trillion threshold was met or exceeded. This is confirmed by multiple independent, high-quality sources. Resolution: Yes, with first qualifying occurrence on 2025-10-28.

question: GOP uses 'Nuclear Option' to break filibuster by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US Senate passes a motion to invoke cloture and end debate on any part of the legislative process, with such a cloture motion receiving Yea votes from fewer than three-fifths of the Senators by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve "No".

Confirmations are considered part of the Senate’s “advice and consent” function, not part of the Senate’s “legislative process,” and will therefore not count towards this market's resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the U.S. government.

subquestions.question: Will Senator John Thune publicly endorse or express support for using the 'nuclear option' to bypass the filibuster for legislative matters (excluding nominations) by November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Senate Majority Leader John Thune has been a key decision-maker regarding filibuster rules. He recently used the nuclear option for nominations in September 2025 but has explicitly ruled out using it for legislative matters like the government shutdown resolution. Thune stated on October 21, 2025: 'The filibuster has protected the country... makes the Senate the Senate.' His position is currently opposed to legislative nuclear option use, but pressure from House Republicans like Marjorie Taylor Greene and Chip Roy continues. Thune's public statements are tracked through official channels and media reports.

Current status (October 31, 2025): Thune has publicly opposed using nuclear option for legislation.

Sources:
- https://www.spectrumnews.org/content/shutdown-sparks-new-conversations-on-nuclear-option/
- https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/493625-chip-roy-floats-nuclear-option-on-senate-filibuster-to-end-shutdown
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Senator John Thune (R-SD), in his capacity as Senate Majority Leader, makes a public statement (through official channels, press releases, interviews, or social media) explicitly endorsing or expressing support for using the 'nuclear option' (a procedural change requiring simple majority vote) to bypass the filibuster for legislative matters (excluding nominations) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive). Statements must be verifiable through official Senate communications (https://www.thune.senate.gov/) or major news outlets. Vague or conditional statements (e.g., 'we might consider') do not count. The statement must clearly indicate support for changing Senate rules to allow legislative passage with fewer than 60 votes.
subquestions.rationale: Thune's position as Senate Majority Leader makes his stance on filibuster reform crucial. A shift from his current opposition to supporting the nuclear option for legislation would indicate increased Republican willingness to break the filibuster, directly signaling higher probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes. This is a leading indicator of Senate Republican leadership's intent regarding procedural changes.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: John Thune (Senate Majority Leader) makes an explicit public statement endorsing/supporting the 'nuclear option' to bypass the legislative filibuster (not nominations) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30. Observable evidence: press releases, interviews, social media posts with clear affirmative support for changing Senate rules to allow legislative passage with fewer than 60 votes. Key entities: John Thune, nuclear option, legislative filibuster, Senate Majority Leader role.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'John Thune nuclear option filibuster legislative 2025' (Oct-Nov window) — to find any endorsement; 2) 'Senate filibuster nuclear option 60 votes simple majority 2025' (Oct-Nov window) — broader context; 3) 'Thune filibuster nuclear option endorsement support late November 2025' — to find any position change; 4) 'Senate filibuster rule change vote November 2025 Thune statement' — to find any procedural actions; 5) 'Thune changed position filibuster nuclear option support late November 2025' — to find any reversals.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events found where Thune endorsed the nuclear option. All events found show Thune explicitly opposing the nuclear option: (a) Oct 31 - spokesperson confirmed position 'unchanged,' called it a 'bad idea'; (b) Nov 4-5 - 'The votes aren't there,' gave floor speech defending filibuster; (c) Nov 5 - 'I know where math is on this issue'; (d) Nov 10 - shutdown ended through bipartisan deal preserving filibuster; (e) Nov 24 - still defending filibuster against Bessent op-ed; (f) Nov 28 - still resisting Trump's calls, preserving filibuster stance. All potential events rejected as they are the opposite of the required condition.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No match found. Sources consistently show Thune opposing the nuclear option throughout the entire window: [New York Post](https://nypost.com/2025/11/04/us-news/senate-majority-leader-says-he-doesnt-have-the-votes-to-eliminate-filibuster-despite-trumps-wishes/), [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5583744-gop-leader-thune-defends-filibuster-trump/), [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/senate/3870690/thune-johnson-against-trump-demand-nix-senate-filibuster/), [Newsday](https://www.newsday.com/long-island/politics/trump-senate-filibuster-thfrcofx), [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/news/politics/25/11/49024359/scott-bessent-says-if-radical-left-again-shuts-down-government-in-january-gop-should-immediately-end-the-filibuster). Thune's actual quotes: 'The votes aren't there,' 'I know where math is on this issue. It's just not happening,' and 'one of my priorities as leader will be to ensure that the Senate stays the Senate.' These are explicit rejections, not endorsements.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying Yes event because no such event occurred. The window closed November 30, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying occurrence was found anywhere in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: All sources across the entire window (Oct 31 – Nov 30) consistently show Thune opposing the nuclear option. There is no contradicting source claiming Thune endorsed it. The government shutdown ended Nov 10-12 through a bipartisan deal that preserved the filibuster — confirming Thune never invoked the nuclear option. As of Nov 28, 2025 (the latest source), Thune was still firmly resisting Trump's calls to eliminate the filibuster.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Senator John Thune did NOT publicly endorse or support using the nuclear option for legislative matters during the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window. He consistently and explicitly opposed it throughout this entire period, defending the filibuster as an essential Senate institution. The condition for Yes resolution was never met. Resolution is No, with the window closing without the event occurring. Resolution datetime = end of window: 2025-11-30T23:59:59Z.

question: Will the federal government be shut down for 10–29 days in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve according to how many days the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announces that the U.S. federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse in appropriations by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM.

Days are counted based on notices checked at 10:00 AM ET each day. If the Office of Personnel Management announces a partial shutdown, this will count; however, announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather will not qualify. 

If there are multiple government shutdowns during the relevant period, this market only applies to the first shutdown, as the market will resolve after the end of the first shutdown. Notices of emergency furloughs or impacted government operations count toward the shutdown days.  

If no shutdown occurs during the period, this market will resolve to "No shutdown".

The resolution source for this market will be the website of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass a continuing resolution (CR) to fund the government by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: A continuing resolution (CR) is a temporary funding measure that maintains government operations at current spending levels when Congress fails to pass full appropriations bills by the fiscal year deadline (September 30). The House of Representatives, with its Republican majority (219-212), must pass any funding legislation first under the Constitution's Origination Clause. Current political dynamics show significant partisan gridlock, with House leadership indicating reluctance to pursue bipartisan stopgap measures. As of September 2025, no CR has been passed, and only 2 of 12 appropriations bills have cleared the House. The passage of a CR by September 30 would significantly reduce the likelihood of an October 1 shutdown. Sources: https://www.congress.gov/legislation, https://www.cbo.gov/publication/59787
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes a continuing resolution (defined as any bill that provides temporary funding for federal agencies at current or adjusted levels to avoid a lapse in appropriations) between 2025-09-17 and 2025-09-30 23:59:59 ET. Resolution will be determined by the official House roll call vote records published on Congress.gov. The bill must receive at least 218 votes (majority of the House) and be recorded as passed. If multiple CRs are passed, the first one meeting these criteria resolves the question. If no CR passes by the deadline, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The House's ability to pass a continuing resolution by September 30 is a crucial indicator of whether Congress can avoid a government shutdown. Given that the House must originate spending bills and currently has a slim Republican majority requiring Democratic support for passage, failure to pass a CR strongly signals legislative gridlock that makes an October 1 shutdown more likely. This subquestion provides an early, binary indicator of congressional dysfunction that correlates with shutdown probability.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: U.S. House passes a CR between Sept 17–Sept 30, 2025, with at least 218 votes (majority of the House), recorded on Congress.gov. Key entities: House of Representatives, CR (temporary funding bill), 218-vote threshold, Sept 17–30 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'House of Representatives continuing resolution CR government funding September 2025' (Sept 17–30) — to find House vote; 2) 'government shutdown September 30 2025 funding deadline' (Sept 17–30) — to find shutdown context; 3) 'House vote CR second continuing resolution September 30 2025 recess' (Sept 29–Oct 2) — to check for any second House vote; 4) 'government shutdown October 1 2025 House Senate vote CR' (Sept 29–Oct 1) — to check final outcome.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: On September 19, 2025, the House passed a CR (HR 531) with a vote of 217-212, funding the government through November 21. This is within the window. No additional House CR votes occurred within the window (House Republicans were in recess from ~Sept 26 through October 7). Senate rejected the CR on September 19 and again on September 30. Government shut down on October 1, 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The House passed a CR on September 19, 2025 — within the window. However, the resolution criteria requires 'at least 218 votes (majority of the House).' Multiple sources confirm the vote was 217-212 [HotAir](https://hotair.com/john-s-2/2025/09/19/house-passes-bill-to-avoid-government-shutdown-n3806975), [WacoTrib](https://wacotrib.com/news/nation-world/government-politics/article_25e81cc7-6ba9-59a6-8564-9539763093dc.html), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/house-passes-trump-backed-plan-avert-government-shutdown), [POLITICUSUSA](https://www.politicususa.com/p/mike-johnson-and-trump-may-have-just). The vote of 217 falls one vote short of the stated 218-vote threshold. No second House CR vote occurred in the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 19, 2025 — House passed CR 217-212. This is within the Sept 17–30 window. However, vote count is 217, not ≥218 as required by the resolution criteria.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The September 19 vote is the only House CR vote in the window. No earlier qualifying event (≥218 votes) exists. No later House CR vote occurred within the window, as the House went on recess ~September 26 through October 7.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources consistently confirm: (1) The House passed the CR 217-212 on Sept 19; (2) The Senate rejected it; (3) The government shut down October 1, 2025; (4) House Republicans were in recess and no further House votes on the CR were held before September 30. The Independent confirms: 'The House, under Speaker Mike Johnson, was on recess and unavailable for immediate votes.' The vote count of 217 is confirmed by multiple independent sources. There is no contradictory evidence about the vote count.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The House passed a CR on September 19, 2025 (within the window), but the vote was 217-212 — one vote short of the 218-vote threshold explicitly stated in the resolution criteria. No additional House CR vote occurred within the window. The government shut down on October 1, 2025. Since the only House CR vote in the window (217 votes) did not meet the ≥218 threshold required by the resolution criteria, the question resolves No. The definitively impossible moment is when the fiscal year ended (September 30 at midnight) with no passing vote meeting the threshold — i.e., the window closed.

question: Taylor Swift holds top ten spots on the Billboard Hot 100 for the week of October 18th?

subquestions.question: Will Taylor Swift's 'The Life of a Showgirl' album debut with at least 1 billion streams on Spotify within its first 3 days of release (October 3-5, 2025)?
subquestions.background_information:
Taylor Swift's album 'The Life of a Showgirl' is scheduled for release on October 3, 2025. Her previous album 'The Tortured Poets Department' set streaming records with 300 million streams in its first day and 1 billion streams in its first 5 days, making it the fastest album to reach 1 billion streams on Spotify. Currently, 'The Life of a Showgirl' has already broken Spotify's pre-save record, indicating massive fan anticipation. For the ultimate question about Billboard Hot 100 domination, streaming numbers are a crucial indicator as Billboard's Hot 100 formula incorporates streaming data from platforms like Spotify. Historically, albums with massive streaming debuts (like Swift's previous albums) have resulted in multiple songs charting simultaneously. 

Sources:
- https://www.euronews.com/culture/2025/09/02/taylor-swift-already-breaks-spotify-record-before-release-of-new-album
- https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2025/09/03/taylor-swifts-new-album-makes-history-on-spotify-a-month-before-it-drops
- https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/billboard-hot-100-streaming-sales-airplay-formula-explained-1235597898/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Taylor Swift's album 'The Life of a Showgirl' reaches at least 1,000,000,000 streams on Spotify (global total across all tracks) between October 3, 2025 (00:00 UTC) and October 5, 2025 (23:59 UTC). The official streaming count will be determined by Spotify's official public announcements or data releases through their verified channels (Twitter/X @Spotify, Instagram @spotify, or official Spotify newsroom). If Spotify does not release official streaming numbers within 7 days after October 5, 2025, Billboard's reported streaming numbers (from their chart methodology articles) will be used as a secondary source. If no reliable streaming data is available from either source by October 11, 2025, the question will resolve as No.

Primary source: https://twitter.com/spotify
Secondary source: https://www.billboard.com/pro/how-billboard-album-charts-compiled-streaming-sales/
subquestions.rationale: This question is highly relevant because streaming performance is a major component of Billboard Hot 100 chart placement. If Swift's new album achieves exceptional streaming numbers (1B+ in 3 days), it would indicate massive consumer engagement likely to translate into multiple songs simultaneously charting in the top 10. Her previous album 'The Tortured Poets Department' achieved 1B streams in 5 days and resulted in her occupying the entire top 14 spots on the Hot 100. This streaming threshold (1B in 3 days) would represent an even stronger debut than her previous record-breaking album, making Billboard Hot 100 domination more likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Taylor Swift's 'The Life of a Showgirl' reaches ≥1,000,000,000 global Spotify streams from October 3-5, 2025 (23:59 UTC). Confirmation must come from Spotify official channels (@Spotify Twitter/X, Instagram, or newsroom) or Billboard within 7 days of October 5 (by October 11, 2025). Key entities: Taylor Swift, The Life of a Showgirl, Spotify global streams, 1 billion threshold, 3-day window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: (1) 'Taylor Swift Life of a Showgirl album release' (2) 'Taylor Swift new album 2025 Spotify streams' (3) 'Taylor Swift Life of a Showgirl billion streams Spotify record' (4) 'Taylor Swift Life of a Showgirl total streams first week Spotify' (5) 'Taylor Swift Life of a Showgirl 384 million first three days streams Billboard' (6) 'Taylor Swift Life of a Showgirl Spotify global total streams week October 2025' (7) 'Taylor Swift Life of a Showgirl Spotify streams day 2 day 3 October 4 5' (8) 'Taylor Swift Tortured Poets Department 1 billion Spotify streams days record comparison'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Album released Oct 3, 2025. (B) Day-1 streams: ~249-310 million global Spotify (conflicting figures across sources). (C) CBS News: '249.8 million first-day streams on Spotify.' (D) The Mirror: '309 million streams on Spotify on its first day.' (E) Billboard (Oct 8): '384 million official on-demand U.S. streams' in first 3 days — U.S. only, NOT global. (F) Album described as 'second-biggest album debut in Spotify history' trailing TTPD (which had 380M day-1 streams and reached 1 billion in 5 days). (G) No Spotify official announcement found stating 1 billion global streams in 3 days. No Billboard article found confirming 1 billion global streams in first 3 days. All rejected as evidence for Yes resolution due to: insufficient totals (day-1 ~250-310M global), U.S.-only data from Billboard (384M in 3 days, not global), no explicit 1-billion announcement.

subquestions.question: Will China approve at least 10 rare earth export license applications to India between October 1 and October 31, 2025?

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The current pattern shows diplomatic assurances without follow-through implementation, so a sudden increase in approved applications would be a strong indicator that China is moving toward lifting restrictions more broadly.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires China to approve at least 10 distinct rare earth export license applications specifically for shipments to India between October 1–31, 2025. Observable evidence would be an official announcement from China's Ministry of Commerce or verified reporting from Reuters/Bloomberg/AP citing Chinese government approval of 10+ license applications for India. subquestions.question: Will OpenAI announce a new major capital raise (at least $10B) or strategic partnership that explicitly requires a for-profit restructuring by October 25, 2025?

- SoftBank commitment: $40B (reportedly paused)

The announcement must come from OpenAI's official channels (blog, press release, SEC filing) or be confirmed by credible reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, TechCrunch). If the announcement occurs but specific dollar amounts or structural requirements are not disclosed, this resolves No. Resolution sources: OpenAI official communications (https://openai.com) and credible news reports.

If OpenAI announces another major capital raise requiring for-profit restructuring, it indicates the company is actively pursuing the structural change again despite recent setbacks. This would be a strong signal that the ultimate transition to for-profit is likely, as investors typically require clear equity structures and profit potential before committing large sums.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: OpenAI announces (between Oct 1-25, 2025) a NEW capital raise ≥$10B USD OR strategic partnership with explicit financial terms, where the announcement EXPLICITLY states the deal requires or is contingent on for-profit restructuring (including removal of profit caps or nonprofit control). Must be from official OpenAI channels or confirmed by ≥2 major outlets. Must indicate firm commitment. Dollar amounts AND structural requirements must be disclosed.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'OpenAI capital raise $10 billion for-profit restructuring 2025' (Oct 1-25 window) - to find primary capital raise; 2) 'OpenAI for-profit conversion restructuring announcement October 2025' - to find restructuring-tied announcements; 3) 'OpenAI SoftBank $40 billion investment contingent for-profit conversion deadline 2025' - to check SoftBank contingency; 4) 'OpenAI Microsoft deal for-profit public benefit corporation announcement October 2025' - for Microsoft deal; 5) 'OpenAI new investment $10 billion October 2025 nonprofit restructuring contingent' - broad search; 6) 'OpenAI official blog press release capital raise for-profit October 2025' - official channels check
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Secondary share sale ~$6.6B (Oct 2, 2025) - REJECTED: secondary sale not primary capital raise; $6.6B < $10B threshold; multiple sources confirm it was a liquidity event, not capital raising. No new deal within the window explicitly meets all criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp found within Oct 1-25, 2025 window. The secondary sale (Oct 2) failed criteria. Chip deals (Oct 6, Oct 13) failed criteria. Pre-window deals were from March and September 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence found within the window. evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple sources confirm the Oct 2025 secondary sale was only ~$6.6B and was a liquidity event, not new capital. No new announcement within the Oct 1-25 window of ≥$10B capital raise explicitly contingent on for-profit restructuring is found across all searches. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No event within the Oct 1-25, 2025 window satisfies the specific resolution criteria: (1) the secondary share sale was ~$6.6B and was not a primary capital raise; (2) the SoftBank ≥$10B deal with for-profit contingency was announced in March 2025 (before the window); (3) the Microsoft MOU was signed September 2025 (before the window); (4) no new ≥$10B capital raise explicitly contingent on for-profit restructuring was announced within this period. The window closed with no qualifying event.

question: Will the Fed cut-pause-pause in 2025?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings in 2025 (September 16-17, October 28-29, and December 9-10).

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered. 

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the December meeting by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the September 2025 Consumer Price Index (CPI) show year-over-year inflation at or below 2.2%?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions, including potential rate cuts, are heavily influenced by inflation data. The Fed targets 2% inflation over the longer run, and inflation readings significantly above this target typically discourage rate cuts. The most recent CPI data (July 2025) showed year-over-year inflation at 2.6%, which remains above the Fed's target. A significant drop below this level could signal to the FOMC that inflation is sustainably moderating, potentially paving the way for rate cuts. The September 2025 CPI release will be a key data point considered by the FOMC at their October 28-29 meeting.

Current inflation context:
- July 2025 CPI: 2.6% year-over-year
- Fed's target: 2% inflation
- Threshold: 2.2% represents a meaningful decline from current levels that could signal sustainable disinflation

Sources:
- Federal Reserve Inflation Target: https://www.federalreserve.gov/faqs/money_12848.htm
- July 2025 CPI Data: https://www.bls.gov/cpi/
- FOMC Meeting Calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Labor Statistics' September 2025 Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), not seasonally adjusted, shows year-over-year inflation at or below 2.2% when released on October 10, 2025. The official BLS release date is typically around the 10th-15th of each month. If the September CPI is not released by October 15, 2025, this question resolves based on the first official BLS release of September CPI data. The data must be accessed from the official BLS website at https://www.bls.gov/cpi/. If the BLS changes its reporting methodology or discontinues this series, the question resolves based on the most comparable official inflation measure published by the BLS. This question resolves based on data published between 2025-09-05 and 2025-10-15.
subquestions.rationale: Inflation data is a primary driver of Fed policy decisions. A September CPI reading at or below 2.2% would represent meaningful disinflation from current levels (2.6% in July 2025) and could signal to the FOMC that inflation is approaching their target sustainably. This would increase the likelihood of rate cuts at subsequent meetings, making a 'cut-pause-pause' pattern more probable. Conversely, if inflation remains elevated (above 2.2%), the Fed would be more likely to maintain higher rates for longer, reducing the probability of the cut-pause-pause pattern.

question: Will Ghislaine Maxwell testify before Congress in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will the House Oversight Committee publicly announce a formal grant of immunity or a clemency arrangement for Ghislaine Maxwell by October 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Ghislaine Maxwell's willingness to testify before Congress appears contingent on receiving immunity or clemency protections. According to multiple news reports from July 2025, Maxwell's legal team has explicitly stated she will invoke her Fifth Amendment rights unless granted formal immunity from Congress or clemency from President Trump. The House Oversight Committee has already subpoenaed Maxwell but has rejected granting immunity as of late July 2025. Maxwell's attorneys argue that without these protections, her testimony could prejudice her ongoing legal appeals, including her pending Supreme Court petition. This creates a standoff where Maxwell's testimony likely requires either Congressional immunity or presidential clemency to proceed.

Current status (as of October 1, 2025): The Oversight Committee has rejected immunity requests, and no clemency has been granted. Any movement toward either of these protections would represent a significant shift in the political dynamics surrounding Maxwell's potential testimony.

Sources:
- https://abc17news.com/news/2025/07/29/maxwell-offers-to-testify-before-congress-but-with-major-conditions-including-immunity/
- https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/29/politics/ghislaine-maxwell-congress-testimony-immunity/index.html
- https://www.westernjournal.com/ghislaine-maxwell-agrees-testify-congress-major-demands-met/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the House Oversight Committee or its official spokesperson releases a public statement between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15 (inclusive) announcing either: (1) a formal grant of Congressional immunity for Ghislaine Maxwell's testimony, or (2) an arrangement for presidential clemency that enables Maxwell's testimony. The announcement must be published on the official House Oversight Committee website (https://oversight.house.gov/) or through official committee social media channels. Statements from individual members of Congress do not qualify unless they are officially designated as speaking for the committee. If no such announcement occurs by October 15, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly addresses the primary precondition Maxwell's legal team has set for her testimony. If Congress grants immunity or arranges clemency, it significantly increases the likelihood of Maxwell testifying in 2025. Conversely, if these protections are not provided by mid-October, it indicates continued resistance from Congress or the administration, making testimony less likely. This is an early indicator because immunity/clemency decisions would need to precede any actual testimony, and movement on this issue in October would signal whether the political will exists to overcome the current standoff.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: House Oversight Committee or its official spokesperson releases a public statement between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15 announcing (1) formal congressional immunity for Maxwell's testimony OR (2) a presidential clemency arrangement enabling her testimony, published on oversight.house.gov or official committee social media. Key entities: House Oversight Committee, Chair James Comer, Ghislaine Maxwell. Timing: Oct 1-15, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'House Oversight Committee Ghislaine Maxwell immunity clemency 2025' (Oct 1-15) — to find direct announcements. Query 2: 'Ghislaine Maxwell congressional immunity testimony October 2025' (Oct 1-15) — to find immunity-related actions. Query 3: 'House Oversight Committee formal immunity grant Maxwell announcement October 2025' — to find formal announcements. Query 4: 'Maxwell immunity rejected committee no immunity testimony October 2025' — to find contradictory evidence.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No qualifying event found. Multiple sources explicitly confirm the OPPOSITE: (1) TheBlaze reports Maxwell 'had previously offered to testify before Congress under conditions of immunity, but her offer was rejected' [https://www.theblaze.com/news/supreme-court-rejects-ghislaine-maxwell-s-appeal-on-first-day-of-session]; (2) The Hill (Oct 7) reports 'the committee rejected the request' for immunity [https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5543253-garcia-trump-ghislaine-maxwell-pardon/]; (3) National Review describes 'a standoff' because her attorneys demand immunity [https://www.nationalreview.com/news/supreme-court-rejects-ghislaine-maxwells-appeal-to-reverse-sex-trafficking-conviction/]; (4) Chair Comer on Oct 8 'strongly discouraged' Trump from pardoning Maxwell [https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5545275-comer-trump-maxwell-pardon/]; (5) The committee contacted Maxwell's attorneys only to schedule her deposition — without immunity [https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/house/3845304/oversight-committee-ghislaine-maxwell-testify/].
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with a timestamp exists. The immunity rejection was already established before/during the window. The committee's actions during Oct 1-15 were scheduling a deposition without immunity, and discouraging clemency — the exact opposite of the resolution criteria.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event occurred at all, so no first-occurrence analysis is needed.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence strongly supports No resolution: multiple credible sources (The Hill, National Review, TheBlaze, Washington Examiner) consistently report the committee rejected Maxwell's immunity request and Comer discouraged presidential clemency. No source reports a formal immunity grant or clemency arrangement announcement from the committee during the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly shows that during the Oct 1-15, 2025 window, the House Oversight Committee explicitly rejected Maxwell's immunity request and Chair Comer actively discouraged presidential clemency. The committee instead sought to schedule Maxwell's deposition without immunity. No formal immunity or clemency arrangement announcement was made by the committee. The question resolves No. The window closed on Oct 15, 2025 with no qualifying event having occurred.

subquestions.question: Will the United States impose new sanctions on Iran that significantly restrict its oil exports (reducing exports by at least 25% from current levels) by February 5, 2026?
subquestions.background_information: The ultimate question concerns potential US military strikes against Venezuela, Iran, Colombia, Mexico, or Cuba. Escalating tensions with Iran could serve as an indicator of increased US willingness to use military force in geopolitical conflicts. Following the January 3, 2026 strike on Venezuela, President Trump has threatened further military action and criticized other nations. Iran has strongly condemned the Venezuela operation, and Trump has previously warned Iran about potential Israeli military action if it resumes nuclear activities. Current Iranian oil exports are estimated at approximately 1.5 million barrels per day as of late 2025, having increased following some sanctions relief. New sanctions that significantly restrict Iran's oil exports would represent a major escalation in US-Iran tensions and could indicate increased likelihood of military confrontation.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the United States government imposes new sanctions on Iran between January 6, 2026 and February 5, 2026 (inclusive) that result in a reduction of Iran's crude oil exports by at least 25% from the baseline level of 1.5 million barrels per day. Resolution will be determined using official US government announcements of sanctions and oil export data from the International Energy Agency's monthly oil market reports. If the IEA data is unavailable, secondary sources such as Bloomberg or Reuters oil market reporting will be used. The reduction must be sustained for at least 30 consecutive days following the sanctions announcement. If sanctions are announced but export data is inconclusive or unavailable by March 5, 2026, the question will resolve NO.
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an indicator of escalating US geopolitical aggression. If the US imposes significant new sanctions on Iran following the Venezuela strike, it suggests the administration is pursuing an increasingly confrontational foreign policy across multiple fronts. This would increase the probability of additional military strikes against the countries mentioned in the ultimate question, as it demonstrates a pattern of escalation rather than an isolated incident.

evidence.step1_decompose: YES requires: (1) New US sanctions on Iran between Jan 6 - Feb 5, 2026; (2) These sanctions result in Iran's crude oil exports dropping by ≥25% from 1.5M bpd baseline (i.e., to ≤1.125M bpd); (3) The reduction sustained for ≥30 consecutive days post-announcement; (4) Verified by IEA monthly data, Bloomberg, or Reuters. If data inconclusive by Mar 5, 2026 → resolves NO.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'US sanctions Iran oil exports 2026' (Jan 6 - Feb 5, 2026) - to find sanctioning actions; Query 2: 'United States Iran new sanctions January February 2026' - to find all rounds of sanctions; Query 3: 'Iran crude oil exports barrels per day January February 2026 reduction' - to measure export impact; Query 4: 'IEA Iran oil exports data 2026 barrels' - to find official export data; Query 5: 'Iran oil exports January 2026 million barrels per day data' - to verify export levels; Query 6: 'US Iran sanctions oil 25% reduction exports significant February 2026' - to find if 25% reduction was explicitly reported.
evidence.step3_event_detection: New US sanctions within window confirmed: (A) Jan 15, 2026 - US Treasury designated 11 individuals and 12 entities under EO 13902, targeting oil export shadow banking networks; (B) Jan 23, 2026 - US Treasury sanctioned 9 vessels and 8 companies linked to Iran's shadow fleet; (C) Jan 30, 2026 - US Treasury sanctioned Iran's Interior Minister, digital asset exchanges, and 18 individuals/companies for oil revenue laundering. These are confirmed within the window. HOWEVER, no evidence of a 25% reduction in exports was found. Iran's exports remained ~1.4-1.5M bpd in January and were INCREASING in mid-February 2026 (to 3M+ bpd during Feb 15-20 loading surge).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Sanctions condition is partially met (new sanctions were imposed within the window). HOWEVER, the critical export reduction criterion is NOT met: (1) [Invezz, Jan 13](https://invezz.com/news/2026/01/13/us-sanctions-threat-puts-iranian-oil-exports-in-peril-prices-hit-multi-month-high/) reports Iranian exports at 'just under 1.4M bpd' before sanctions; (2) [IEA Feb 2026 report via Market Screener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/iea-expects-oil-supply-to-rebound-after-u-s-winter-storm-slashed-output-ce7e5ad2df81f62c) states 'Iran maintained stable crude supply at 3.45M bpd in January'; (3) [Business Standard, Feb 26](https://www.business-standard.com/world-news/iran-ramps-up-oil-exports-amid-rising-us-military-presence-in-region-126022600120_1.html) states 'Iranian exports expected to average 1.5-1.6M bpd in February 2026'; (4) [News18, Feb 26](https://www.news18.com/business/tankers-full-of-crude-are-waiting-at-sea-why-arent-buyers-taking-the-oil-despite-big-discounts-ws-kl-9931564.html) states Chinese imports of Iranian crude at '1.2M bpd' in early February; none of these indicate a 25%+ reduction to ≤1.125M bpd. There was NO sustained 25% reduction in Iran's oil exports within the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Sanctions announcements have exact timestamps: Jan 15, Jan 23, Jan 30, 2026. Export data for the window comes from IEA February 2026 Monthly Oil Market Report (published ~Feb 12, 2026) which shows stable Iranian supply at ~3.45M bpd production and ~1.5M bpd exports in January - no 25% reduction. This is published within the March 5 deadline.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question asks whether the specific threshold (25% export reduction sustained 30 days) was ever met. No qualifying event was found. The sanctions were announced, but the export reduction threshold was never met within the window or the 30-day sustained period that would have been detectable by March 5, 2026.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: Multiple sources confirm Iran was actively INCREASING oil exports in mid-to-late February 2026 (loading at 3x the January rate per TankerTrackers/Bloomberg). Chinese imports of Iranian oil dipped from 1.25M bpd to 1.03M bpd in February - a ~17.6% decline, but (a) this is still above the ≤1.125M bpd threshold, (b) much of this occurred post-window, and (c) this was partly offset by Iran's pre-emptive export surge before potential military action. The IEA February 2026 report explicitly shows no sustained 25% reduction. The resolution criteria's fallback clause ('if export data is inconclusive or unavailable by March 5, 2026, resolves NO') also applies - but in this case, data IS available and shows NO 25% reduction.
evidence.step8_final_decision: While the US did impose new sanctions on Iran multiple times within the Jan 6 - Feb 5, 2026 window (Jan 15, Jan 23, Jan 30), there is no evidence that these sanctions resulted in a 25% reduction (≤1.125M bpd) in Iran's crude oil exports sustained for 30 consecutive days. IEA data confirms Iran's supply remained stable at ~3.45M bpd production and ~1.5M bpd exports in January 2026, and Iran actually ramped up exports in mid-February. The export reduction criterion is definitively not met, and the resolution should be NO as of February 5, 2026 (end of window) when no qualifying export reduction had occurred.

subquestions.question: Will Nikita Bier post fewer than 10 original tweets (excluding retweets, replies, and quote tweets) on his verified X account (@nikitabier) between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14?

Only tweets where Bier is the original author count toward the total; retweets, replies to others' tweets, and quote tweets are excluded. evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: @nikitabier posts fewer than 10 original tweets (excluding retweets, replies, quote tweets) between 2025-10-15T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-14T23:59:59Z. Observable evidence needed: exact tweet count from X API or archive.org snapshots. Key threshold: <10 original tweets in exactly 30 days.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Nikita Bier tweets X Twitter October November 2025' — to find documented tweets in window. 2) '@nikitabier Twitter posts activity 2025' — to find activity data. 3) 'Nikita Bier original tweets count posting frequency October 2025' — to find count data. 4) 'Nikita Bier X account suspended deleted private 2025' — to check account status. 5) 'Nikita Bier fired left X product head November 2025' — to check employment/account status. 6) 'nikitabier tweet post November 2025 X product announcement' — to find November tweets.

These are only the newsworthy tweets covered by media. The account was not suspended or deleted — Bier remained active as X's Head of Product throughout the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: News articles explicitly document at least 7 distinct original tweets from @nikitabier within the window. Sources: [TheRegister](https://www.theregister.com/2025/10/15/twitter_x_bot_show_user_info/), [LatestLY Oct 17](https://www.latestly.com/socially/technology/x-links-coming-soon-x-product-head-nikita-bier-confirms-platform-working-on-new-feature-may-boost-posts-containing-text-and-links-7164385.html), [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91425207/xs-ux-update-wants-to-save-your-links-from-social-medias-black-hole), [Mashable India](https://in.mashable.com/tech/101625/product-head-of-x-nikita-bier-says-2-video-games-can-crash-twitter-internet-reacts-with-hilarious-aw), [Social Media Today](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/x-formerly-twitter-bangers-highlight-top-posts-in-the-app/805087/), [Sportskeeda](https://www.sportskeeda.com/pop-culture/news-did-brittany-venti-earn-1000-clackface-post-youtuber-denies-rumor-controversial-photos-create-outrage). However, exact count is not available — only newsworthy tweets are captured, not all original tweets.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Exact timestamps of individual tweets not available; news article publication dates provide approximate dates. No official X API count or archive.org snapshot count is available through news search.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — the question is about a cumulative count over 30 days, not a single first occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: Account was active and not suspended/deleted throughout the window (Bier remained X's Head of Product through at least Nov 9, 2025 based on Bangers announcement). The documented tweets from news coverage alone reach ~7, but this is an undercount since news only covers notable posts. There is no evidence of an exact count being published anywhere. Without an exact, verified count, the question cannot be definitively resolved. subquestions.question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo or his agent publicly request a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks before 2026-01-03?
subquestions.background_information:
Giannis Antetokounmpo's future with the Milwaukee Bucks has become increasingly uncertain following the team's 9-13 start to the 2025-26 season. Recent developments include Antetokounmpo removing nearly all Bucks-related content from his social media accounts and initiating discussions with the Bucks front office about his future. According to ESPN's Shams Charania, Antetokounmpo and his agent Alex Saratsis have begun conversations with the team regarding whether his best fit lies in staying or moving elsewhere, with a resolution expected in the coming weeks. Antetokounmpo has expressed frustration over the team's performance and there is reported tension in the locker room. While Antetokounmpo has not yet publicly requested a trade, league insiders believe this could be a precursor to a formal trade demand. Historically, public trade requests from star players often precede actual trades, making this a significant indicator of Antetokounmpo's future with the team.

Sources:
- ESPN: https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39456723/giannis-antetokounmpo-opens-talks-bucks-future-trade-deadline-looms
- Real GM: https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/275344/Giannis-Antetokounmpo-Opens-Talks-With-Bucks-About-His-Future

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if Giannis Antetokounmpo or his officially recognized agent (currently Alex Saratsis of Octagon Basketball) publicly requests a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 (inclusive). A public trade request is defined as: (1) A statement directly from Antetokounmpo or his agent through official channels (social media accounts, press conference, or official statement), or (2) A report from at least two credible NBA news sources (including ESPN, The Athletic, NBA.com, or official team/league sources) citing Antetokounmpo or his agent directly requesting a trade. The request must be specific to Antetokounmpo seeking a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks organization. General expressions of dissatisfaction or frustration without a specific trade request do not qualify. If the trade request is later retracted but occurred within the resolution window, the question still resolves 'Yes.' Resolution will be determined using official NBA sources (NBA.com) and credible reporting from ESPN (https://www.espn.com/nba) and The Athletic (https://theathletic.com/nba).
subquestions.rationale: A public trade request from Antetokounmpo or his agent would be the strongest possible indicator that a trade is imminent. Historical NBA precedent shows that when star players publicly request trades, teams typically accommodate those requests within the same season to avoid locker room disruption and maximize trade value. Given Antetokounmpo's stature as a franchise player and his no-trade clause, his explicit request would significantly increase the probability of a trade before the February deadline. This subquestion captures a crucial decision point that would substantially update forecasts about the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Giannis Antetokounmpo or his agent Alex Saratsis must publicly request a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03. This requires either (1) a direct statement via official channels, or (2) reports from at least two credible NBA sources citing a specific trade request. General expressions of dissatisfaction do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Giannis Antetokounmpo trade request Milwaukee Bucks' (2025-12-04 to 2026-01-03) — to find evidence of a formal request. Query 2: 'Giannis Antetokounmpo trade demand 2025' (same window) — alternative phrasing. Query 3: 'Giannis Antetokounmpo formally demands trade Bucks January 2026' (2025-12-28 to 2026-01-03) — to check if a request occurred late in the window. Query 4: 'Giannis agent Alex Saratsis trade request statement' (same window) — to check for agent-initiated request.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate event found that constitutes a formal public trade request. What was found: (1) Shams Charania reported Giannis and his agent began discussions with the Bucks about his future (Dec 3-4, 2025), but this was characterized as discussions, not a trade request; (2) Doc Rivers repeatedly stated 'Giannis has never asked to be traded. Ever.' (Dec 4, Dec 28, 2025); (3) Giannis himself on Dec 28 called trade questions 'disrespectful' and affirmed commitment; (4) ESPN/Bleacher Report reported as of Dec 29 that Bucks 'won't trade Giannis without a forceful request,' indicating no such request had been made; (5) Reports from Jan 1-2, 2026 show Giannis publicly expressing desire to win with Bucks and taking responsibility for losses. question: Will Amazon acquire Warner Bros. Discovery?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if it is announced that Warner Bros. Discovery will be, has been, or is being acquired by or merged with the listed entity by 11:59 PM ET on May 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If no merger or acquisition takes place by the specified date, this market will resolve to "No Acquisition by May 31, 2026".

subquestions.question: Will Warner Bros. Discovery receive a formal acquisition offer from Amazon at or above $25 per share by November 23, 2025?

Amazon has the financial capacity for a major acquisition with over $80 billion in cash and short-term investments as of Q2 2025. A formal offer from Amazon would indicate serious interest in acquiring WBD and could trigger a bidding war with other potential suitors like Paramount Skydance, which has reportedly offered $20 per share. The $25 threshold represents a 25% premium to WBD's current ~$20 share price and would value the company at approximately $61 billion, making it a substantial premium offer that would significantly influence the acquisition landscape.

Sources:

- https://www.cordcuttersnews.com/warner-bros-discovery-confirms-multiple-offers-buy-company/
- https://www.amazon.com/ir/annual-reports

(NASDAQ: WBD) or any substantial portion of its business (including but not limited to Warner Bros. Studio division, Discovery Global, or the entire company) at a price of $25.00 per WBD share or higher, with the announcement occurring between 2025-10-24 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-11-23 23:59:59 UTC. The resolution will be based on official corporate communications from Amazon's investor relations (https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-releases) or WBD's investor relations (https://wbd.com/investors/). If conflicting information arises, SEC filings will take precedence over press releases.
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as a crucial indicator for the ultimate Amazon-WBD acquisition outcome because Amazon making a formal premium offer would demonstrate serious acquisition intent and significantly increase the likelihood of a successful deal. A $25+ per share offer would represent a substantial premium over WBD's current price and would likely force other bidders to increase their offers or drop out. Given Amazon's financial resources and strategic interest in media content (as shown by their MGM acquisition), their formal participation in the bidding process would be a strong signal that a major acquisition is imminent. This subquestion captures whether Amazon transitions from being a rumored suitor to an actual bidder with a concrete offer, which would be a major development in the acquisition timeline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Amazon.com formally announces (via press release from Amazon IR/WBD IR, or SEC filing: 8-K, 13D, or similar) an offer to acquire WBD or substantial portion at ≥$25.00/share, between 2025-10-24T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-23T23:59:59Z. evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria require a formal Amazon offer ≥$25/share via official press release or SEC filing between Oct 24–Nov 23, 2025. question: Will Italy win the third most gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the third most gold medals at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most gold medals won will use most overall medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most gold medals won, and Norway wins more overall medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the gold medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

question: Will Rodrigo Paz Pereira win by 15–20%?
description:
A second-round (runoff) vote for the Bolivia Presidential election is scheduled to take place on October 19, 2025 

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the 2025 Bolivian Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the 'margin of victory' is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first and second-place candidate. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the second round of the Bolivian Presidential Election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the results of the election aren’t known by March 31, 2026 ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve solely based on the first official vote count released by the Bolivian Government, specifically the Plurinational Electoral Body (Órgano Electoral Plurinacional, OEP) (https://www.oep.org.bo/).

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

subquestions.question: Will Rodrigo Paz Pereira's polling average lead over Jorge 'Tuto' Quiroga reach at least 15 percentage points in any credible national poll published between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Following the first-round election on August 17, 2025, Rodrigo Paz Pereira leads Jorge 'Tuto' Quiroga by approximately 5.2 percentage points (32.1% vs 26.9%). Polling data will be crucial in tracking momentum shifts leading up to the October 19 runoff election. Historically, polling leads in Bolivian elections have been predictive of final outcomes, though margins can change significantly during runoff campaigns. The current polling landscape shows Paz with a modest lead, but substantial movement could indicate either consolidation of support or erosion of his position. Key factors to watch include endorsement effects (particularly from third-place finisher Samuel Doria Medina), campaign messaging effectiveness, and voter sentiment shifts in critical regions like La Paz and Santa Cruz.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if any credible national poll published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) shows Rodrigo Paz Pereira's support percentage minus Jorge 'Tuto' Quiroga's support percentage equal to or greater than 15 percentage points. Polls must be conducted by organizations with demonstrated track records in Bolivian electoral polling and published with full methodology. The polling margin must be based on valid vote intention among likely voters. If multiple polls are published on the same date showing different margins, the question resolves based on the poll showing the largest margin. The resolution will be determined using polling data from the following sources (in order of priority): 1) CELAG (Centro Estratégico Latinoamericano de Geopolítica) 2) CIESMORI Bolivia 3) Tarija Electoral Studies Center 4) Other nationally recognized polling firms with established track records. If no qualifying poll is published during the specified period, the question resolves NO.
subquestions.rationale: Polling momentum is a strong early indicator of electoral outcomes. A 15+ point lead in credible polling would suggest Paz is consolidating broad support across different voter bases, which could translate into a significant margin of victory in the actual election. This threshold represents a substantial increase from the current 5.2% gap and would indicate either significant erosion of Quiroga's support or major consolidation behind Paz. Given that the ultimate question focuses on a 15-20% victory margin, polling data showing such a large lead would be highly informative about the likely final outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Any credible national poll (by CELAG, CIESMORI, or equivalent) published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, showing Rodrigo Paz Pereira's support percentage minus Jorge 'Tuto' Quiroga's support percentage ≥ 15 percentage points in vote intention among likely voters. evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Rodrigo Paz Pereira poll Bolivia 2025' — to find any polls showing Paz's support. 2) 'Tuto Quiroga encuesta Bolivia septiembre 2025 CELAG CIESMORI' — to find specific credible polling firm surveys. 3) 'Bolivia encuesta segunda vuelta Paz Quiroga septiembre 2025' — to find runoff polling data. 4) 'Bolivia runoff poll survey Paz Quiroga October 2025 voting intention' — to find voting intention surveys. 5) 'Bolivia encuesta elecciones segunda vuelta intención de voto octubre 2025' — Spanish-language search for vote intention. 6) 'Bolivia polling 15 points lead Paz Quiroga runoff election October 2025' — to specifically find evidence of the required threshold being met.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events found. Articles from September 2025 discuss: (1) Bolivia's first-round results (Paz ~32%, Quiroga ~26-27%, a ~5-6 point gap); (2) Campaign activities, debates, and economic issues; (3) Political polarization and guild warnings to candidates; (4) Bolivia's economic crisis. No articles reported any credible national polling data showing vote intentions for the runoff election with specific percentages. The only percentage data found are from the first-round election results (not polls).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No qualifying poll was found in any article from September 1-October 1, 2025. The first-round election results showed Paz at ~32% vs. Quiroga at ~26-27% (a gap of approximately 5-6 points), which is far below the 15-point threshold required. More importantly, these are election results, not runoff polling data. Multiple sources [Crux](https://cruxnow.com/church-in-the-americas/2025/09/ahead-of-second-round-of-presidential-election-bolivian-church-hopeful-about-new-government/), [bne IntelliNews](https://www.intellinews.com/bolivia-releases-opposition-figure-camacho-after-three-years-in-detention-399100/), and others from September 2025 discuss the runoff without referencing any specific polling data showing the required margin.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp could be extracted for a qualifying poll because no qualifying poll was found in the evidence. The window closed on 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z without a qualifying poll being identified.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at all within the window, let alone a first occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: I verified by: (1) Searching multiple times using different query variations in both English and Spanish; (2) Looking for CELAG, CIESMORI, and other specific polling organizations by name; (3) Checking whether any article from the period reported specific runoff polling numbers. The consistent finding across all searches was that no credible national poll with runoff vote intentions (let alone a 15-point lead) was reported in the news between September 1-October 1, 2025. The context (first-round gap of ~5-6 points) further suggests a 15-point lead in any runoff poll would be unlikely, though this cannot be the sole basis for resolution. The resolution is based on absence of evidence, combined with the resolution criteria stating the question resolves NO if no qualifying poll is published.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves NO. The resolution criteria explicitly states: 'If no qualifying poll is published during the specified period, the question resolves NO.' question: Will India strike Pakistan by Dec 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if India initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Pakistani territory by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or any operation conducted by Indian ground forces will not qualify as a strike under this market.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

Stratton's progressive platform makes her natural labor ally, but her trailing position in polls suggests she needs institutional backing to compete with Krishnamoorthi's financial advantage. A major union endorsement would signal strong ground operation support and potentially shift undecided voters, making it a meaningful early indicator of her nomination chances. The 46% undecided voters in recent polls suggest the race remains fluid, and labor support could be decisive.

subquestions.question: Will NASA successfully complete the wet dress rehearsal for Artemis II by February 2, 2026, 11:59 PM ET?
subquestions.background_information: The wet dress rehearsal (WDR) is a critical pre-launch test where NASA loads the SLS rocket with cryogenic propellants (liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen) and conducts a full countdown simulation without actually launching. This test validates all systems, procedures, and ground infrastructure under launch-like conditions. Previous Artemis missions experienced delays due to issues during WDR, particularly hydrogen leaks and propellant loading problems. For Artemis II, NASA has targeted February 2, 2026, for this test based on current schedules and launch window constraints. A successful WDR would indicate that the rocket and ground systems are ready for launch, while failure could lead to rollback to the Vehicle Assembly Building for repairs, potentially delaying the February launch window. Sources: NASA's Artemis II rollout announcement (https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-artemis-ii-moon-rocket-rolls-out-to-launchpad/), CBS News coverage (https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nasa-artemis-ii-moon-rocket-rollout-launchpad-february-2026/), and NASA's wet dress rehearsal description (https://www.nasa.gov/exploration/systems/sls/wet-dress-rehearsal.html).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if NASA officially announces the successful completion of the wet dress rehearsal for Artemis II between 2026-01-21 and 2026-02-02 23:59:59 ET. Success is defined as: (1) All propellants (approximately 800,000 gallons of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen) are fully loaded into the SLS rocket tanks; (2) The full countdown sequence is executed through to T-10 seconds (simulated launch); (3) NASA's official communications (press release, social media, or mission blog) declare the test 'successful' or 'complete' without major issues requiring rollback. The primary source for resolution will be NASA's official Artemis II mission updates (https://www.nasa.gov/artemis-ii). Secondary sources include NASA's Kennedy Space Center launch blog (https://blogs.nasa.gov/kennedy/) and NASA's official Twitter account (@NASA). If NASA announces a postponement of WDR beyond February 2, 2026, but then completes it successfully before February 20, 2026, the question resolves No (since the condition was not met by the deadline). Any WDR attempt that is aborted or fails to complete all objectives by February 2, 2026, results in No.
subquestions.rationale: The wet dress rehearsal is a crucial indicator of launch readiness for Artemis II. Historical issues with WDRs (e.g., hydrogen leaks in Artemis I) have directly caused launch delays. A successful WDR by February 2 would signal that technical hurdles are overcome, maintaining the February launch window. Conversely, failure or delay would suggest unresolved problems, increasing risk of missing the February 28 deadline. This subquestion provides early evidence on whether the rocket systems are functioning as planned, which is informative for the ultimate launch outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires NASA to successfully complete the Artemis II wet dress rehearsal (WDR) between 2026-01-21 and 2026-02-02 23:59:59 ET. All three conditions must be met: (1) full propellant loading (~800,000 gallons of LH2/LOX); (2) full countdown sequence through T-10 seconds (simulated launch); (3) NASA officially declares it 'successful' or 'complete' without major issues requiring rollback.
