Query 4: 'NASA Artemis II WDR fueling test results February 2026' (Feb 2 - Feb 6) to find official NASA results.
evidence.step3_event_detection: The WDR was originally scheduled for January 31, then rescheduled to February 2, 2026 due to cold weather. Countdown began January 31, with the simulated launch window opening at 9 p.m. EST on February 2. During the test, a hydrogen leak was detected at the Tail Service Mast Umbilical (TSMU) interface. Multiple pauses were required. The ground launch sequencer halted the countdown at T-5:15 minutes (not T-10 seconds) due to a high hydrogen leak rate. NASA subsequently announced a delay to March 2026 and the need for a second WDR. No qualifying event (WDR completed successfully through T-10 seconds with NASA declaring it 'successful' without major issues) occurred within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Criterion (1): Propellant loading — Sources confirm the core stage was eventually successfully filled with liquid hydrogen and oxygen, despite the leak pauses. [NASA blog](https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/missions/2026/02/03/artemis-ii-wet-dress-rehearsal-nasa-discusses-initial-results/), [NASASpaceFlight](https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/02/artemis-ii-wdr-resolutions-march-target/). Criterion (2): Full countdown through T-10 seconds — FAILED. The countdown was terminated at T-5 minutes 15 seconds due to the hydrogen leak. The T-10 second threshold was never reached. [MoneyControl](https://www.moneycontrol.com/science/nasa-s-artemis-ii-pushed-back-launch-delayed-till-march-2026-after-hydrogen-leak-in-key-tests-article-13808748.html), [India Today](https://www.indiatoday.in/science/story/artemis-ii-wet-test-scrubbed-due-to-hydrogen-leak-in-moon-rocket-2862246-2026-02-03), [NASASpaceFlight](https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/02/artemis-ii-wdr-resolutions-march-target/). No contradictory evidence exists showing the countdown reached T-10 seconds.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The WDR was attempted on February 2, 2026, but the countdown was terminated at T-5 minutes 15 seconds due to a hydrogen leak — far short of the required T-10 seconds threshold. The question resolves No. The condition became definitively impossible when the countdown was halted at T-5:15 minutes on February 2/3, 2026, and confirmed when NASA announced the March delay on February 3. subquestions.question: Will Zootopia 2's domestic box office tracking reach or exceed $120 million for its 3-day opening weekend by November 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Box office tracking estimates from major industry sources provide early indicators of a film's potential opening weekend performance. As of October 2025, initial tracking for Zootopia 2 shows projections ranging from $95-110M (BoxOfficePro) to $115-130M (BoxOfficeTheory). The current top projected opening weekends for 2025 include A Minecraft Movie ($162M), Lilo & Stitch ($141M), Superman ($125M), and Wicked: For Good ($112-115M). For Zootopia 2 to achieve the second-best opening weekend of 2025, it would need to surpass at least two of these competitors. Tracking numbers typically solidify and become more accurate as release dates approach, with final tracking numbers often published 1-2 weeks before release.

Sources:
- BoxOfficePro tracking: https://www.boxofficepro.com/
- BoxOfficeTheory tracking: https://forums.boxofficetheory.com/
- Movieweb analysis: https://movieweb.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if any of the following major box office tracking sources (BoxOfficePro, BoxOfficeTheory, or Deadline) publishes a tracking estimate for Zootopia 2's domestic 3-day opening weekend that reaches or exceeds $120 million between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29 (inclusive).

If multiple tracking estimates are published, the highest value from any of these sources within the resolution window will be used. The tracking estimate must be explicitly stated as a 3-day opening weekend projection and must come from an official publication (not forum speculation).

If no tracking estimates are published by these sources by November 29, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC, the question resolves No.

Tracking sources:
- BoxOfficePro: https://www.boxofficepro.com/
- BoxOfficeTheory: https://forums.boxofficetheory.com/
- Deadline: https://deadline.com/
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion provides an early indicator of Zootopia 2's potential opening weekend performance. Tracking estimates that reach or exceed $120M would suggest the film is on track to potentially surpass competitors like Superman ($125M projection) and compete for the second-highest opening weekend position. Since tracking numbers typically become more accurate as release approaches, a high tracking number by November 29th would indicate strong pre-release buzz and ticket sales momentum that could translate into actual box office performance during the opening weekend.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: BoxOfficePro, BoxOfficeTheory, or Deadline must publish an explicit tracking estimate for Zootopia 2's domestic 3-day opening weekend at or above $120 million, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29. Key threshold: $120M, 3-day (Fri-Sun), from qualifying sources only.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Zootopia 2 box office tracking opening weekend 2025' (Nov 1-29); 2) 'Zootopia 2 domestic opening weekend projection forecast' (Nov 1-29); 3) 'BoxOfficePro Zootopia 2 tracking estimate opening weekend $120 million' (Nov 1-29); 4) 'Deadline Zootopia 2 tracking 3-day opening weekend projection' (Nov 1-29); 5) 'Box Office Theory Zootopia 2 $122 million opening weekend tracking estimate' (Nov 1-29); 6) 'Zootopia 2 $140 OR $150 OR $160 million three-day 3-day weekend box office' (Nov 25-29).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) BoxOfficePro (Nov 14, 2025) long-range forecast listed Zootopia 2 at $100M–$190M alongside other films — this is a wide range, with the upper bound well above $120M; (B) Deadline (Nov 6, 2025) published a 5-day opening projection of $125M+ — explicitly described as a 5-day (Wed-Sun) opening, NOT 3-day; (C) Box Office Theory (via SlashFilm, Nov 20, 2025) — upper bound of $122M for 'opening weekend' cited; (D) Post-release projections (Nov 27-28) from multiple non-qualifying sources showing 3-day projections well above $120M (film tracking toward $140M-$150M+ for 5 days after earning $59.2M domestically through 2 days). Rejected: Deadline's Nov 6 projection ($125M) because it's explicitly a 5-day projection. Secondary citations of Box Office Theory are indirect. BoxOfficePro's range ($100M–$190M) has upper end exceeding $120M but is ambiguous as a tracking estimate.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires an estimate 'explicitly stated as a 3-day opening weekend projection' from official publications. Key findings: (1) [BoxOfficePro](https://www.boxofficepro.com/long-range-forecast-avatar-fire-and-ash-tracking-to-exceed-the-way-of-waters-134m-opening/) (Nov 14): Lists Zootopia 2 at $100M–$190M — this is BoxOfficePro's standard long-range 3-day opening weekend tracking range. The upper end ($190M) far exceeds $120M. BoxOfficePro typically provides 3-day projections. (2) [Deadline](https://deadline.com/2025/11/zootopia-2-box-office-projection-1236609211/) (Nov 6): Explicitly projects a 5-day (Wed-Sun Thanksgiving) opening of $125M+, NOT a 3-day estimate. (3) Box Office Theory (cited in [SlashFilm](https://www.slashfilm.com/2031145/zootopia-2-disney-billion-dollar-box-office-hit-preview/), Nov 20): $102M–$122M for 'opening weekend' — upper bound $122M meets threshold, but this is a secondary citation. (4) By Nov 27-28, Deadline and others were projecting $140M–$150M for the 5-day, with the 3-day (Fri-Sun) portion projected well above $120M based on actual daily numbers ($59.2M domestic through Wed-Thu), but these are actual-based projections, not pre-release tracking. BoxOfficePro's $100M–$190M range in their Nov 14 article, while a qualifying source, represents a wide uncertainty range rather than a specific point estimate.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: BoxOfficePro article: Published 2025-11-14 (exact date confirmed). Deadline article (5-day): Published 2025-11-06. SlashFilm citing Box Office Theory: Published 2025-11-20. These are within the resolution window (Oct 31 – Nov 29, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The BoxOfficePro long-range forecast from Nov 14 is the earliest qualifying source publication with a range that includes values at and above $120M. The Deadline article (Nov 6) is earlier but explicitly projects a 5-day opening, not 3-day. Box Office Theory's estimate (upper bound $122M) was reported Nov 20 via SlashFilm.
evidence.step7_verification: Key ambiguity: The BoxOfficePro range ($100M–$190M) is very wide and represents uncertainty rather than a specific tracking estimate at $120M+. The resolution criteria says 'the highest value from any of these sources' would be used — the BoxOfficePro range's upper end of $190M exceeds $120M, but it's debatable whether a range's upper bound constitutes a tracking estimate 'reaching or exceeding $120M.' However, BoxOfficePro's standard practice is to publish 3-day opening weekend ranges. The Box Office Theory upper bound of $122M (per SlashFilm citing BOT) meets the threshold, though this is not an 'official publication' by Box Office Theory itself but rather a secondary citation. Additionally, post-release data (Nov 27-28) indicates actual 3-day performance was tracking well above $120M, but the question requires pre-release tracking estimates from specific sources. The Deadline Nov 25 article projects $125M for 5-day Thanksgiving window — still not a 3-day estimate from Deadline. The Variety article (Nov 26, Nov 27) projects $125M-$150M for the 'Thanksgiving holiday weekend' (5-day) and $125M-$150M for the 'opening weekend.' These are not from the qualifying sources. The actual 3-day (Fri-Sun) box office, based on Yahoo/Variety reporting, was being projected at approximately $80-100M for the 3-day portion (with $59.2M domestic through first 2 days Wed-Thu, and $140M-$150M for the 5-day). This means the 3-day (Fri-Sun) was approximately $80-90M — potentially BELOW $120M when considered as a strict 3-day (Fri-Sat-Sun) number. The confusion arises because Thanksgiving weekends are often reported as 5-day frames.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution is complex. Most tracking estimates from qualifying sources either: (a) explicitly project a 5-day Thanksgiving window (not 3-day) — Deadline's $125M+ is for 5 days; (b) provide wide ranges that include $120M+ in their upper bounds (BoxOfficePro's $100M-$190M); (c) are secondary citations of Box Office Theory (not official publications from BOT itself). The BoxOfficePro Nov 14 long-range forecast shows a range of $100M-$190M for Zootopia 2 — while the upper bound exceeds $120M, this is not a specific tracking estimate at $120M+, but rather a wide probability range. The Box Office Theory estimate (upper end $122M for 'opening weekend') from SlashFilm's report on Nov 20 is the strongest candidate for Yes resolution, as it: (1) is from a qualifying source (Box Office Theory); (2) has an upper bound that reaches $122M; (3) is for 'opening weekend' (typically 3-day). However, this evidence comes through a secondary publication (SlashFilm), not directly from Box Office Theory's official forum. The resolution criteria requires estimates from 'official publication (not forum speculation).' Given that BoxOfficeTheory is a forum (forums.boxofficetheory.com), and the estimate was only referenced via SlashFilm, and the Deadline estimate is explicitly 5-day, the strictest reading of the criteria creates ambiguity. However, given that: (1) BoxOfficePro's range has an upper bound of $190M for what are standard 3-day forecasts; (2) the film's actual trajectory strongly suggests 3-day projections exceeded $120M by late November (the film earned approximately $160M over 5 days based on the data); and (3) Deadline's pre-release article projected $125M for the 5-day window (implying the 3-day would be lower, perhaps $80-95M based on typical Thanksgiving splits), the evidence is genuinely ambiguous. The ScreenRant article from Nov 26 explicitly states Zootopia 2 is projected at $94.6M for the 3-day weekend — this is below $120M. This is a non-qualifying source but provides context that many 3-day projections were BELOW $120M. Given the substantial ambiguity, particularly that: (a) Deadline's qualifying projection was explicitly 5-day ($125M); (b) actual 3-day estimates from multiple non-qualifying sources were $94-100M range; (c) BoxOfficePro's range was very wide; (d) BOT's upper-bound $122M came through a secondary source — this question's resolution is unclear and I cannot definitively confirm a qualifying source explicitly stated a $120M+ 3-day projection.

question: Will Silver (SI) hit (HIGH) $110 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Silver (SI) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Silver (SI) futures contracts, the Active Month is the nearest of CME's designated delivery-cycle months (March, May, July, September, December) that is not the spot month. The Active Month becomes a non-active month effective on its First Position Date, at which point the next eligible contract month becomes the Active Month.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures.

question: EU/NATO country announces peacekeeping force in Ukraine in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any NATO or EU member country officially announces that they will be sending troops to Ukraine as part of a peacekeeping force by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must be part of a formal agreement between a NATO or EU member country and another country or international organization or otherwise indicative of a formalized policy.

Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, or otherwise are not indicative of a formalized policy will not count

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from NATO, the EU, or member states of either entity, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the UK or France publicly commit to sending at least 2,000 troops each to a peacekeeping force in Ukraine by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The UK and France have been the primary advocates for a European peacekeeping force in Ukraine, with both countries signaling willingness to contribute troops. According to Foreign Policy (May 2025), Britain and France indicated they could contribute 5,000-10,000 personnel combined, but other major European nations have refused to send soldiers. As of August 2025, EurActiv reported that France and the UK were considering deploying 'hundreds of soldiers' but no firm commitments had been made. A public commitment from either country to deploy a substantial number of troops (2,000+) would represent a significant escalation in their willingness to participate in ground operations and could indicate progress toward the formation of an actual peacekeeping force. Sources: Foreign Policy (https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/05/15/european-peacekeeping-force-ukraine-wont-work/), EurActiv (https://www.euractiv.com/section/global-europe/news/whos-in-and-whos-out-of-ukraines-reassurance-force/)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if either the United Kingdom or France officially announces through government channels (ministry of defense, head of state, or official government spokesperson) a commitment to deploy at least 2,000 military personnel specifically for peacekeeping operations in Ukraine. The announcement must include both the number of troops (≥2,000) and specify their role as peacekeepers. Statements must be unambiguous commitments, not conditional or exploratory. The announcement must occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). If multiple announcements are made, the first qualifying announcement determines the outcome. Primary sources: UK Government announcements (https://www.gov.uk/search/all?keywords=ukraine+peacekeeping&order=relevance), French Government announcements (https://www.gouvernement.fr/en/news), and official NATO statements (https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/news.htm). If official sources are unavailable, a consensus of at least three major international news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP) reporting the commitment will be accepted.
subquestions.rationale: The UK and France have been the primary drivers behind the peacekeeping force proposal. A firm, substantial troop commitment from either country would represent a concrete step toward actual deployment, indicating that political will has moved beyond theoretical discussions to actionable planning. This would significantly increase the likelihood of an eventual NATO/EU peacekeeping force announcement, as these two countries' participation is seen as essential for any credible mission.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Either UK or France must officially announce (via MoD, head of state, or official government spokesperson) a commitment to deploy ≥2,000 military personnel specifically for peacekeeping in Ukraine, with both the number AND peacekeeping role explicitly stated, as an unambiguous (non-conditional) commitment, between Sep 1 and Oct 1, 2025. Observable evidence would be a press release, official statement, or credibly reported government announcement naming ≥2,000 troops and 'peacekeeping' role.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'UK France troops peacekeeping Ukraine 2025' (Sep-Oct window) — general peacekeeping coverage; 2) 'UK Britain 2000 troops Ukraine peacekeeping specific number commitment' (Sep-Oct) — looking for specific numbers; 3) 'France 2000 troops Ukraine commitment specific number September 2025' — same for France; 4) 'UK France Ukraine peacekeeping troop numbers specified 2000 5000 10000' — numerical threshold; 5) 'MNF-U Multinational Force Ukraine UK headquarters' — looking for specific UK structure announcements; 6) 'UK France Ukraine 10000 20000 troops peacekeeping Macron announcement' — larger numbers.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key events found: (A) September 4, 2025 Paris 'Coalition of the Willing' summit — Macron announced 26 countries pledged a 'reassurance force' for post-ceasefire deployment; UK's Starmer co-chaired. (B) UK MoD announced a 2-star Army officer would lead the MNF-U headquarters in Kyiv (Sept 6). (C) France pledged €2 billion military aid at the summit. (D) One medium.com source attributed '10,000–20,000 troops per ally' to Macron but this lacks primary source citation. (E) NaturalNews mentioned '2,000 troops reportedly being prepared' but without country attribution or authoritative sourcing. Rejected: all commitments were conditional on ceasefire/peace agreement; no per-country number ≥2,000 was specifically announced by UK or France.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require: (1) official announcement through government channels ✓ (Paris summit was official); (2) commitment to deploy ≥2,000 military personnel ✗ (no specific per-country number announced); (3) specifically for peacekeeping operations ✗ (described as 'reassurance force' not 'peacekeeping' in formal terms, though similar); (4) both number and role stated ✗ (no specific number given); (5) unambiguous, non-conditional commitment ✗ (all pledges were explicitly conditional on ceasefire/peace deal); (6) within window ✓ (Sep 4 is within window). Criteria 2, 4, and 5 are not met. Sources: [Irish Times Sept 4](https://www.irishtimes.com/world/europe/2025/09/04/macron-says-26-states-ready-to-send-troops-in-postwar-reassurance-force-for-ukraine/), [RFI Sept 4](https://www.rfi.fr/en/international/20250904-macron-says-26-countries-pledge-troops-as-a-reassurance-force-for-ukraine), [Euronews Sept 4](https://www.euronews.com/2025/09/04/coalition-of-the-willing-26-countries-agree-to-deploy-troops-or-equipment-to-post-war-ukra), [bne IntelliNews Sept 4](https://www.intellinews.com/the-coalition-of-the-willing-meet-in-paris-to-try-and-stop-the-war-in-ukraine-399624/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 4, 2025 for the Paris summit announcement. September 6, 2025 for the UK MNF-U headquarters announcement. No timestamp exists for a qualifying announcement meeting all criteria (number ≥2,000 + peacekeeping role + unconditional).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (meeting all criteria) was found at any point in the window, so there is no 'first occurrence' to identify. Searched through October 1, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Boris Johnson (Sept 24) criticized the UK's 'limited commitment' of only 'reassurance forces', suggesting no firm unconditional troop number was announced. bne IntelliNews explicitly stated 'the summit produced no concrete security guarantees or troop commitments'. All sources confirm commitments were conditional on ceasefire/peace deal. The NaturalNews mention of '2,000 troops reportedly being prepared' lacks attribution and is from a low-reliability source. The Medium.com source attributing '10,000-20,000 troops per ally' to Macron is not corroborated by primary sources and appears to be a paraphrase. No primary source (gov.uk, gouvernement.fr) announced a specific number ≥2,000 for peacekeeping.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. The evidence clearly shows that while UK and France pledged participation in a multinational 'reassurance force,' neither country made an announcement: (a) specifying their individual contribution as ≥2,000 troops, AND (b) characterizing those troops explicitly as 'peacekeepers,' AND (c) making an unconditional (non-conditional) commitment. All pledges were conditional on a ceasefire or peace agreement being reached first. The window closed on October 1, 2025 without any qualifying announcement. Resolution_datetime = 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z as the window closed without the condition being definitively foreclosed by a specific event earlier, but rather simply never having been met.

question: Will another MrBeast video get 100m+ week 1 views by November 30?

subquestions.question: Will MrBeast post a YouTube video (excluding Shorts) that receives at least 10 million views within its first 24 hours between 2025-09-27 and 2025-10-27?
subquestions.background_information: MrBeast's videos often achieve massive view counts quickly, but his recent focus has shifted toward Shorts, which may impact long-form video performance. His most recent long-form video uploads have varied in initial view velocity. For example, his 'I Bought the NFL' sketch (September 2025) received 9 million total views (source not specifying 24-hour window), while his Squid Game recreation (2021) achieved 100M views in 4 days. Current subscriber count is 435M (Tubefilter, September 2025). A 24-hour view threshold of 10M would indicate strong initial engagement for a long-form video, potentially signaling capacity for 100M+ week-1 views. Sources: https://www.tubefilter.com/2025/09/15/top-50-most-subscribed-youtube-channels-worldwide-09-14-2025/, https://www.prweek.com/article/1876151/flag-football-tswift-balance-creator-cookouts-nfls-influencer-play-card
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if MrBeast posts at least one YouTube video (excluding Shorts) between 2025-09-27 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-27 23:59:59 UTC that reaches ≥10,000,000 views within 24 hours of its public upload time (as shown in YouTube Analytics). The view count must be verified using the public view counter on the video's YouTube page (e.g., https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast). If multiple videos qualify, the first to meet the condition determines resolution. If no video meets the condition within the window, resolves No. If YouTube's view counter is unavailable or frozen, use archived data from Wayback Machine (https://archive.org) or reputable third-party trackers like SocialBlade (https://socialblade.com) as fallback.
subquestions.rationale: Initial 24-hour view velocity is a strong leading indicator of week-1 performance for viral content. If a MrBeast video fails to hit 10M views in the first day (a threshold he has frequently exceeded historically), it would suggest reduced momentum for long-form content amid his shift to Shorts, making 100M+ week-1 views less likely. Conversely, hitting this threshold would signal sustained virality potential.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: MrBeast posts at least one YouTube video (NOT a Short) between 2025-09-27T00:00:00Z and 2025-10-27T23:59:59Z that reaches ≥10,000,000 views within 24 hours of upload. Observable evidence: news reports or view trackers confirming ≥10M views within 24 hours of a non-Short YouTube video by MrBeast uploaded in the window. Key entities: MrBeast (@MrBeast), YouTube (non-Short only). Threshold: 10 million views in ≤24 hours. Timing: upload and view milestone both within the specified window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'MrBeast YouTube video October 2025 views' — to find any video posted and its view count; 2. 'MrBeast new video upload September October 2025' — to find specific new uploads; 3. 'MrBeast Would You Risk Dying $500,000 video views 24 hours' — to find view count data for the September 27 video; 4. 'MrBeast burning house video views first day September 27 2025' — to confirm 24-hour views; 5. 'Kotaku MrBeast 46 million views burning house video' — to verify the specific 24-hour claim.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) MrBeast's 'Would You Risk Dying For $500,000?' — a 25-minute YouTube video uploaded on September 27, 2025. Kotaku (published Sept 29, 2025) explicitly states it 'attracted over 46 million views in a single day.' This is clearly not a Short (it is 25 minutes long, confirmed by multiple sources including NDTV, Yahoo, and Economic Times). (2) MrBeast's 'I Saved 1,000 Animals From Dying' — released October 25, 2025, per Hindustan Times and Mint. No 24-hour view count data available for this video. (3) MrBeast's 'call your ex' video — explicitly identified as a YouTube Short, excluded per resolution criteria. The September 27 video is the primary qualifying candidate.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The 25-minute video 'Would You Risk Dying For $500,000?' was uploaded on September 27, 2025 (within the window per NDTV, Yahoo, Metro, Mandatory, and Sportskeeda). It is explicitly NOT a YouTube Short (it is 25 minutes long). [Kotaku](https://kotaku.com/mrbeast-house-fire-trapped-prize-stunt-viral-youtube-backlash-safety-2000629861) published September 29, 2025, explicitly states the video 'attracted over 46 million views in a single day' — well above the 10 million threshold. The Kotaku figure of 46 million views 'in a single day' directly and explicitly satisfies the ≥10 million views within 24 hours criterion.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Video upload date: September 27, 2025 (multiple sources confirm this as 'Saturday, 27 September'). First 24-hour view count: 46+ million views (reported by Kotaku, published September 29, 2025, noting the views accumulated 'in a single day'). The upload timestamp is confirmed as September 27, 2025, which is the start date of the resolution window. Exact upload time (hours/minutes) is not available from news sources, but the date September 27, 2025 is firmly established and falls within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is confirmed as the first video in the window — the window starts on September 27, 2025, the exact same date as this video's upload. No earlier qualifying video could exist within the window. The 'I Saved 1,000 Animals' video was released October 25, 2025, which is later. No other MrBeast non-Short video within the window is mentioned in any article with 10M+ views in 24 hours. The September 27 video is the first qualifying occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) Some sources mention the 'call your ex' challenge with 38 million views — but this is explicitly described as a 'YouTube Short,' not a standard video, and is therefore excluded per resolution criteria. (2) Some sources list slightly different overall view counts (44M, 45M, 46M, 49M, 53M) due to different timestamps of reporting — these are cumulative totals from different observation points, not contradictions. The Kotaku source explicitly says '46 million views in a single day,' which is the specific metric needed. (3) The video is confirmed as 25 minutes long (full YouTube video, not a Short). No contradictory evidence found suggesting this video did NOT reach 10M views within 24 hours.
evidence.step8_final_decision: MrBeast posted a 25-minute YouTube video (clearly not a Short) titled 'Would You Risk Dying For $500,000?' on September 27, 2025, the first day of the resolution window. Per Kotaku (Sept 29, 2025), the video attracted over 46 million views in a single day — far exceeding the 10 million view threshold within 24 hours. The upload date is September 27, 2025, which falls within the resolution window (2025-09-27 to 2025-10-27). All resolution criteria are clearly met. Resolution: Yes.

A discharge petition requires 218 signatures to succeed, but reaching a significant threshold like 100 signatures would indicate substantial bipartisan support and momentum. As of early September 2025, the petition is newly filed and signatures are being collected. Discharge petitions are rare and difficult to succeed—only about 2% have been successful since 1967—but they can signal strong member support for legislation. The current number of signatures is not yet publicly reported, but tracking this threshold can serve as an early indicator of whether the bill has enough backing to potentially move forward. Sources: https://www.oann.com/newsroom/rep-luna-introduces-resolution-to-advance-the-end-congressional-stock-trading-act/, https://www.newsmax.com/newsfront/anna-paulina-luna-stock-trading-ban/2025/08/29/id/1178769/, https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/anna-paulina-luna-congressional-stock-trading-ban-discharge-petition.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the discharge petition for H.R. 1908 (End Congressional Stock Trading Act) reaches at least 100 signatures on the official House of Representatives discharge petition tracker between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), as recorded by the Clerk of the House. The primary data source is https://clerk.house.gov/DischargePetitions/ (specifically the entry for H.R. 1908). If the Clerk's website does not show the count, but multiple credible news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg) consistently report the petition reached ≥100 signatures during this period, the question resolves Yes. If the petition is withdrawn or deemed invalid by the House Parliamentarian during the resolution window, it resolves No. If no reliable data is available by 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The discharge petition signature count is a concrete, near-term indicator of legislative momentum for a congressional stock trading ban. If it gains rapid support (e.g., 100+ signatures in one month), it suggests bipartisan interest in forcing a vote, increasing the odds of the ultimate bill passing. If it stalls, it indicates lack of support, making the ultimate outcome less likely. This subquestion is resolvable quickly and provides evidence on whether the bill has traction beyond its sponsors.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires Luna's discharge petition for H.R. 1908 to reach exactly ≥100 signatures on the Clerk of the House's discharge petition tracker between September 1 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence would include: (1) Clerk of the House data showing ≥100 signatures, or (2) multiple credible news sources (Reuters, AP, Bloomberg) consistently reporting ≥100 signatures during this period.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searches conducted: (1) 'Anna Paulina Luna discharge petition H.R. 1908 End Congressional Stock Trading Act signatures' (2025-01-01 to 2025-10-01); (2) 'discharge petition congressional stock trading ban 2025 signatures' (2025-01-01 to 2025-10-01); (3) 'Luna discharge petition H.R. 1908 signatures count September 2025' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01); (4) 'congressional stock trading ban discharge petition signatures September 2025' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01); (5) 'Luna stock trading discharge petition 100 signatures how many signed' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01); (6) 'H.R. 1908 discharge petition clerk house signatures update October' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-15); (7) 'Luna stock trading petition withdrawn leadership deal floor vote September October 2025' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-15); (8) 'End Congressional Stock Trading Act discharge petition status update signatures October 2025' (2025-09-15 to 2025-10-15); (9) 'Luna stock trading ban discharge petition signatures count update September 2025' (2025-09-10 to 2025-10-01); (10) 'congressional stock trading ban floor vote September October Johnson leadership deal' (2025-09-15 to 2025-10-15).

subquestions.question: Will the CDC report at least 20 new confirmed measles cases in the U.S. between December 2, 2025 and December 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

This represents a significant surge from previous years, with 2025 already surpassing the previous record of 1,274 cases in 2019. Current outbreaks are concentrated in Utah, Arizona, South Carolina, and New York, with 92% of cases occurring in unvaccinated individuals. The CDC reports that national vaccination coverage has declined to 92.5%, below the 95% threshold needed for herd immunity. The current weekly case rate (as of November 2025) suggests ongoing transmission that could continue through December 2025. Given that measles has an incubation period of 7-14 days and is highly contagious (each case can cause 12-18 new infections in unvaccinated populations), December case counts will serve as a strong indicator of whether transmission is continuing at levels that could lead to 500+ cases in 2026.

Sources:
- CDC Measles Data & Research: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html
- NBC News measles coverage: https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/measles-cases-rise-us-2025-rcna185678
- SheKnows outbreak analysis: https://www.sheknows.com/health-wellness/articles/3018958/measles-outbreak-2025-us/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if the CDC's weekly measles surveillance report shows at least 20 new confirmed measles cases reported for the United States between December 2, 2025 (start date) and December 31, 2025 (end date), inclusive. The case count will be determined by summing the weekly reported cases from all CDC Weekly Measles and Rubella Updates published during this period. The primary data source will be the CDC's Measles (Rubeola) page at https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html. If this source becomes unavailable, resolution will use archived versions from the Wayback Machine (archive.org) or official CDC press releases. If no weekly reports are published during this period, resolution will be based on the next available CDC report covering this timeframe. Cases must be confirmed measles (rubeola) cases in humans within the United States as defined by CDC criteria.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as an early indicator for the ultimate question because ongoing measles transmission in December 2025 would strongly suggest that the conditions driving the current outbreak (low vaccination rates, susceptible populations, and efficient transmission) will persist into 2026. Given measles' high reproductive number and the timing of school terms/holiday gatherings in December, sustained transmission during this period would indicate that the U.S. is unlikely to achieve containment before 2026 begins. A 'Yes' outcome (≥20 cases) would suggest continued spread into 2026, making 500+ cases more likely, while a 'No' outcome would indicate successful containment efforts or seasonal decline in transmission.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: CDC weekly measles surveillance reports must show ≥20 new confirmed measles (rubeola) cases in the U.S. between Dec 2, 2025 and Dec 31, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: CDC weekly totals must increase by at least 20 from the Dec 2 baseline. Key entities: CDC Weekly Measles and Rubella Update; cumulative U.S. case counts.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Donald Trump signs an executive order between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-20 (inclusive) that specifically addresses mail-in voting or voting machines. subquestions.question: Will the Consumer Confidence Index (CCI) from The Conference Board fall below 95.0 for September 2025?

A reading below 95.0 would indicate significant consumer pessimism about current and future economic conditions, potentially signaling weaker consumer spending ahead. Historical data shows that when the CCI falls below 95.0, it often precedes economic slowdowns as consumers reduce spending.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index (seasonally adjusted) for September 2025 is reported at or below 95.0. subquestions.rationale: Consumer confidence is a strong leading indicator for GDP growth, as consumer spending accounts for the majority of US economic activity. The September reading provides timely insight into consumer sentiment during the critical third quarter, making it highly relevant for forecasting Q3 GDP growth outcomes.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for YES: The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index (seasonally adjusted) for September 2025 must be reported at or below 95.0, and the data must be published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). question: Will the next government funding bill be a clean CR?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the next government funding bill that becomes law in the United States by December 31, 2025, is a clean continuing resolution. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

A clean continuing resolution is defined as a funding measure that temporarily extends current government spending at the previous fiscal year’s levels for a specified period, without incorporating any additional policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass a clean continuing resolution (CR) by November 7, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A clean continuing resolution temporarily extends government funding at previous fiscal year's levels without policy riders or earmarks. The current government shutdown began on October 1, 2025, after Congress failed to pass appropriations bills. House Speaker Mike Johnson has repeatedly brought clean CRs to the floor, but they have failed to pass due to opposition from conservative Republicans who demand spending cuts or policy changes. The House has held ten votes on clean CRs as of October 17, 2025, all failing. A clean CR passing the House would indicate reduced opposition from fiscal conservatives and increased likelihood of eventual passage, while continued failure suggests ongoing division. Current status: No clean CR has passed the House despite multiple attempts.

Sources:
- Star Local: https://example.com/star-local-shutdown-article (Note: Actual URL needed)
- House.gov: https://www.house.gov/legislative-activity
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes a clean continuing resolution (as defined: a bill that extends funding at FY2025 levels without any policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-07 23:59:59 UTC. Resolution will be determined using the official House vote records from https://clerk.house.gov/Votes and confirmed by at least two credible news sources (e.g., https://www.c-span.org/congress/bills/, https://www.nytimes.com/politics). If the House passes multiple clean CRs during this period, the first passage counts. If the data sources become unavailable, resolution will be based on consensus of credible reporting from at least three major news organizations.
subquestions.rationale: House passage of a clean CR is a crucial indicator for the ultimate question because the House has been the primary obstacle to clean CRs during this shutdown. If the House can pass a clean CR, it suggests reduced conservative opposition and increased likelihood that a clean CR will eventually become law. If the House continues to reject clean CRs through November 7th, it indicates persistent division that makes ultimate passage of a clean funding bill less likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the U.S. House of Representatives to pass a 'clean' continuing resolution (a bill extending funding at FY2025 levels without any policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications) between 2025-10-31T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-07T23:59:59Z. Observable evidence would be: an official House floor vote passing such a bill, confirmed by vote records from clerk.house.gov and at least two credible news sources.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'House of Representatives clean continuing resolution November 2025' — to find any House vote on a CR; 2) 'continuing resolution CR vote House passed November 2025' — to find specific passage; 3) 'House vote continuing resolution shutdown November 6 7 2025' — to find any late-window vote; 4) 'government shutdown deal resolution Senate House November 7 2025' — to check if shutdown ended; 5) 'Senate passes continuing resolution shutdown ends November 2025' — to check if resolution ended in this period.
evidence.step3_event_detection: All sources consistently report: (1) The House passed H.R. 5371 (a clean CR extending funding through November 21) on September 19, 2025 — BEFORE the question window (Oct 31 – Nov 7). (2) The House has been OUT OF SESSION since September 19, 2025 and remained so throughout the entire question window. (3) The Senate voted 14 times to advance H.R. 5371 and failed each time. (4) As of November 7, 2025 (38th day of shutdown), the House had NOT reconvened and no new CR was passed by the House. The Senate was planning a 15th vote (on a new package with a minibus) on November 7, but no House vote followed. Speaker Johnson stated he would reconvene the House only after the Senate acts, and a 48-hour notice period would be needed.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No House passage of a clean CR occurred between Oct 31 and Nov 7, 2025. Multiple sources confirm the House was out of session throughout this period: [JD Supra](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/tracking-the-2025-us-government-6534963/) states 'The House and Senate are both out of session, with no continuing resolution (CR) vote scheduled'; [Yahoo/Senate update](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/u-senate-convenes-34th-day-222345699.html) states 'The House has not been in session since September 19'; [MSNBC](https://www.msnbc.com/opinion/msnbc-opinion/senate-shutdown-end-mike-johnson-democrats-rcna241901) confirms 'The House of Representatives has been inactive since September 19, 2025'; [British Caribbean News](https://britishcaribbeannews.com/senate-president-urges-local-banks-to-aid-federal-workers-struggling-during-shutdown/) confirms the shutdown was still ongoing on November 7 (38th day). Johnson pledged to reconvene with 48-hour notice only after Senate passes something — which had not happened by Nov 7.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The shutdown was still active on November 7, 2025 (day 38), with the House not in session and no vote taken. No House CR passage timestamp exists within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying House vote on a clean CR occurred at any point within the Oct 31 – Nov 7 window. The House had not even reconvened during this period.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources unanimously confirm: (a) the House was out of session from September 19 onward; (b) the government shutdown was ongoing on November 7 (day 38); (c) the only CR the House passed was on September 19, outside the window; (d) the Senate was working toward a deal but had not passed anything, and even if the Senate had voted, the House would need 48 hours notice then a vote — impossible by Nov 7. No contradictory evidence found suggesting the House voted on any CR in this window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. House did NOT pass a clean continuing resolution between Oct 31 and Nov 7, 2025. The House was not in session during this entire period. The government shutdown continued through at least November 7, 2025 (day 38). The condition for Yes resolution definitively was not met within the window. The shutdown was still ongoing at the close of the window, so the earliest definitive No is the window end: 2025-11-07T23:59:59Z.

question: Will Israeli troops enter Suwayda in 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will Israeli Defense Forces conduct at least 3 ground incursions into Syrian territory within 20km of the Suwayda border between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent reports indicate escalating Israeli ground operations in southern Syria, particularly in provinces bordering Suwayda. According to Enab Baladi (2025-09-28), Israeli forces conducted multiple ground incursions into Quneitra province in September 2025, including raids in Sida Golan, Tal al-Ahmar al-Sharqi, Jabata al-Khashab, Ofaniya, and Khan Arnaba. These operations involved military vehicles entering Syrian territory, searching homes, conducting surveys, and making arrests. The Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) reported these incidents, with some occurring within 20km of the Suwayda border. Israel has maintained an active military presence in southern Syria since the fall of the Assad regime in December 2023, with hundreds of strikes and ground operations documented. The current pattern shows increased frequency of ground incursions near Suwayda, potentially signaling preparation for larger operations.

Sources:
- Enab Baladi: https://english.enabbaladi.net/
- Syrian Arab News Agency: https://sana.sy/en/
- Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Israeli Defense Forces conduct at least 3 separate ground incursions into Syrian territory within 20km of the Suwayda Governorate border between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). A ground incursion is defined as: 1) IDF military vehicles crossing into Syrian territory from Israel or occupied Golan Heights, 2) Remaining in Syrian territory for at least 30 minutes, 3) Involving at least 3 military vehicles or 12 soldiers. Incursions must be reported by at least two independent credible news sources (e.g., SANA, Enab Baladi, Al Jazeera, Reuters) or officially acknowledged by IDF spokesperson. Aerial operations, maritime operations, and undercover operations do not count. If the primary sources (SANA, Enab Baladi) cease publication, secondary sources including Reuters, AFP, or AP reports will be used. The distance measurement will be based on the nearest point of the incursion location to the Suwayda Governorate border using Google Maps coordinates.
subquestions.rationale: Increased frequency of Israeli ground operations near Suwayda's borders would indicate heightened military activity and potential preparation for entry into Suwayda itself. Recent patterns show Israel conducting multiple ground incursions in neighboring provinces (Quneitra, Daraa), and escalation of this activity toward Suwayda would signal increased likelihood of Israeli troops eventually entering Suwayda Governorate. This subquestion tracks observable military patterns rather than directly asking about Suwayda entry, making it an effective leading indicator.

evidence.step1_decompose: Requires: (1) IDF military vehicles crossing into Syrian territory from Israel/occupied Golan Heights, (2) remaining in Syrian territory for ≥30 minutes, (3) involving ≥3 military vehicles or 12 soldiers, (4) location within 20km of Suwayda Governorate border, (5) at least 3 separate qualifying incursions between Oct 1-31 2025, (6) reported by ≥2 independent credible sources or IDF acknowledgment. Key constraint: incursions must be geographically within 20km of Suwayda's border.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'IDF Israeli forces ground incursion Syria Suwayda October 2025' - to find direct evidence; 2) 'Israel Syria ground operation Sweida border 2025' - to find Suwayda-specific reports; 3) 'IDF ground incursion Quneitra Syria October 2025 vehicles checkpoint' - to find Quneitra incursions; 4) 'Israeli military patrol Daraa Suwayda Syria October 2025' - to find Daraa-area incursions; 5) 'IDF Israeli forces Jamlah Daraa Suwayda border distance incursion' - geographic proximity analysis; 6) 'Israeli incursion Suwayda Sweida direct ground troops October 2025' - Suwayda-specific incursions
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple ground incursions by IDF were confirmed in October 2025, all in Quneitra and western Daraa: Oct 4 (Madinat al-Salam/Quneitra, 2 Humvees; Jamlah/Daraa, 6-17 vehicles stayed 1+ hour); Oct 8 (al-Samdaniya al-Sharqiya/Quneitra, 3 vehicles, ~30 min); Oct 10 (Saida Al-Hanout/Quneitra, 3 vehicles + 2 Humvees); Oct 11 (Tablain junction/Quneitra, 3 vehicles); Oct 16-17 (Ruwayhina/Quneitra, 9 vehicles; Tal Krum Jaba); Oct 18 (Ofania/Khashab road, 2 tanks + 5 vehicles); Oct 23 (al-Razaniyah and Abu Rajm, 5 vehicles); Oct 26 (Hadar-Tranjah road + Eastern Samdaniyah, 3 Humvees + tanks); Oct 27 (Bariqa, al-Razaniyah, Saqri checkpoint); Oct 29 (Bir Ajam + Eastern al-Samadaniyah). NONE of these incursions were reported to be within Suwayda Governorate or within 20km of the Suwayda border.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The critical criteria failure is GEOGRAPHIC: The resolution requires incursions 'within 20km of the Suwayda Governorate border.' All confirmed IDF ground incursions in October 2025 occurred in: (a) Quneitra Governorate (which borders Daraa and Damascus provinces, not Suwayda directly); (b) Western Daraa/Yarmouk Basin (Jamlah, Abidin, Koya, Saisoun). Geographic context: Suwayda Governorate is located in southeast Syria, its western border abuts eastern Daraa. The Yarmouk Basin is in the far WESTERN part of Daraa, over 50km from the Suwayda border. Quneitra is even further. No sources report any IDF ground incursion near the Suwayda Governorate border. Sources: [SANA](https://sana.sy/en/local/2271505/), [SOHR](https://www.syriahr.com/en/371035/), [Enab Baladi](https://english.enabbaladi.net/archives/2025/10/israeli-incursions-threaten-civilians-and-erode-national-belonging/), [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/israeli-forces-raid-several-villages-in-syria-s-quneitra/3725224)
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Not applicable — no qualifying incursion within 20km of Suwayda border was found.
evidence.step7_verification: Searched extensively for any IDF ground incursion specifically in or near Suwayda. No such reports found. Israel did conduct airstrikes near Suwayda in July 2025 (during Druze crisis), but these were air operations (not ground), and they occurred before the October 2025 window. During October 2025, IDF ground operations were confined to Quneitra and western Daraa (Yarmouk Basin area), which are geographically approximately 50-80km from the Suwayda border. The 20km requirement is thus definitively not met by any reported October 2025 ground incursion.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is NO. While the IDF conducted numerous ground incursions into Syrian territory during October 2025, none were reported within 20km of the Suwayda Governorate border. All incursions were in Quneitra and western Daraa (Yarmouk Basin), which are far from the Suwayda border. The geographic criterion (within 20km of Suwayda border) was not met by any qualifying incursion during the Oct 1-31 window. The window closed with no qualifying incursions.

subquestions.question: Will Israel announce a formal withdrawal from at least two of its nine military posts in southern Syria by January 11, 2026?
subquestions.background_information: Since December 2023, Israel has maintained military presence at nine strategic posts in southern Syria, including positions on Mount Hermon and in the Syrian side of the disengagement zone. These positions include Tell al-Ahmar in Quneitra province and posts in villages such as Bir Ajam, Barikah, and Zubeida. Israel has justified this occupation as necessary for security against potential threats. Current reporting indicates these positions are a major sticking point in negotiations, with Syria demanding full withdrawal to pre-December 8, 2024 borders as a precondition for any security agreement. An Israeli withdrawal from even a subset of these positions would signal significant progress in negotiations and willingness to compromise on territorial control, which is crucial for reaching a broader security agreement. Sources: https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2025/11/20/Israel-s-Netanyahu-visits-occupied-Syrian-territory-as-tensions-rise, https://syrianobserver.com/news/94220.html, https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/9/netanyahu-behind-stalled-israel-syria-negotiations/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Israeli government or Ministry of Defense officially announces the withdrawal of Israeli military forces from at least two of the following nine identified positions in southern Syria: Mount Hermon (Syrian side), Tell al-Ahmar (Quneitra), Bir Ajam, Barikah, Zubeida, Ain Ziwan, Abu Qubais, and any two additional positions officially confirmed by the Israeli military as occupied posts. The announcement must occur between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11 (inclusive) and be verifiable through official Israeli government statements, Ministry of Defense publications, or IDF spokesperson announcements. Resolution will be based on official Israeli sources such as the Prime Minister's Office website (https://www.gov.il/en) or IDF official statements (https://www.idf.il/en). If multiple sources conflict, the most authoritative Israeli government source will prevail. Withdrawals must be explicitly announced as completed or in progress with specific timeline commitment.
subquestions.rationale: Israeli military withdrawal from occupied Syrian territory is a core Syrian demand and major obstacle to any security agreement. A partial withdrawal would demonstrate Israel's willingness to compromise on territorial control, which is essential for progress toward a broader security framework. This serves as a concrete indicator of negotiation progress rather than just diplomatic statements.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official Israeli government announcement (PM's Office, Ministry of Defense, or IDF spokesperson) of formal withdrawal (completed or in-progress with specific timeline) from at least 2 of 9 identified military posts in southern Syria (Mount Hermon, Tell al-Ahmar, Bir Ajam, Barikah, Zubeida, Ain Ziwan, Abu Qubais, plus 2 others) between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Israel withdrawal military posts southern Syria 2025' - to find any withdrawal announcements; 2) 'Israel IDF Syria military withdrawal announcement' - to find official IDF/government statements; 3) 'Israel formal withdrawal Syria military posts Mount Hermon Tel al-Ahmar Bir Ajam' - targeted search for specific posts; 4) 'Israel Syria nine military posts withdrawal announcement IDF official' - targeted for the 9-post context; 5) 'Israel IDF withdrawal Syria posts announcement January 2026' - January window search; 6) 'Israel Syria deal withdrawal Golan Heights buffer zone January 2026' - diplomatic developments.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events reviewed: (a) Dec 28, 2025 - 55th Reserve Brigade completed mission and will be replaced - REJECTED: this is a unit rotation, not withdrawal of posts; (b) Jan 1, 2026 - Haredi brigade deployed to southern Syria - REJECTED: this is reinforcement, opposite of withdrawal; (c) Jan 5-6, 2026 Paris talks - discussions about Israeli withdrawal - REJECTED: these are negotiations, no withdrawal announced; (d) Multiple IDF incursion reports throughout window - REJECTED: these confirm continued presence. No candidate event matching criteria found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found matching the criteria. On December 23, 2025, Defense Minister Katz explicitly stated 'We will not move an inch from Syria' [APA](https://en.apa.az/asia/israel-will-not-withdraw-from-syria-defense-minister-says-487223) and 'We are not withdrawing even a millimeter from Syria' [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/israeli-defense-minister-vows-no-full-withdrawal-from-gaza-occupied-syrian-territories/3778947). On January 6, 2026, after US-brokered Paris talks, 'Israel's defense ministry had not issued any formal response to the [withdrawal] proposal' [Devdiscourse](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/law-order/3751722-syria-demands-concrete-timeline-for-israeli-withdrawal-in-peace-talks). The IDF maintained nine posts and continued incursions throughout the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp exists — no withdrawal announcement was made in the window. The earliest definitive 'No' evidence is December 23, 2025, when Defense Minister Katz publicly stated Israel would not withdraw from Syria.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (withdrawal announcement) was found at any point in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The Dec 28 brigade withdrawal is explicitly a unit rotation with replacement troops already designated. The Jan 5-6 Paris talks resulted in a de-escalation mechanism, not a withdrawal announcement. Israel's positions throughout the window were uniformly expansionary/retentive, not withdrawing. Multiple sources confirm continued IDF presence at all nine posts through January 9, 2026.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. Israel made no formal announcement of withdrawal from any of the nine military posts in southern Syria during the resolution window. To the contrary, Israeli officials explicitly stated Israel would not withdraw from Syria, new forces were deployed, and the IDF continued active incursions throughout the window. The condition for Yes was definitively foreclosed on December 23, 2025 when Defense Minister Katz explicitly stated 'We are not withdrawing even a millimeter from Syria,' though Israel's continued non-withdrawal persisted through the entire window end of January 11, 2026.

question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The CDC reported a general fertility rate of 54.5 births per 1,000 women aged 15–44 for Q1 2025 (see: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm). 

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the initial reported rate for Q2 2025 exceeds 54.5, according to the CDC's Vital Statistics Rapid Release series. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

If the CDC does not release general fertility rate data for Q2 2025 by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Resolution will be based on the first published estimate for Q2 2025, regardless of any subsequent revisions.

The resolution source will be the CDC’s Vital Statistics Rapid Release.

subquestions.question: Will the number of weekly U.S. initial unemployment claims drop below 200,000 at least once between September 1 and September 16, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Initial unemployment claims serve as an indicator of labor market health and economic confidence, which are factors that influence fertility decisions. Lower unemployment claims suggest stronger job security and economic stability, potentially encouraging family planning. The current weekly initial unemployment claims (as of August 2025) are approximately 210,000-220,000 based on recent Department of Labor reports. Historically, claims below 200,000 have been associated with strong labor markets (e.g., pre-COVID levels). Sources: U.S. Department of Labor (https://www.dol.gov/ui/data.pdf), Federal Reserve Economic Data (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/ICSA).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims for any week between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-16 (inclusive) fall below 200,000, as reported by the U.S. Department of Labor's Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report (https://www.dol.gov/ui/data.pdf). The data must be from the official report published on or before 2025-09-19. If multiple weeks qualify, the first occurrence resolves the question to Yes. If no week during this period has claims below 200,000, the question resolves No. If the report is delayed beyond 2025-09-19 or data is unavailable, the question resolves based on the last available report before 2025-09-19.
subquestions.rationale: A drop in initial unemployment claims below 200,000 would signal improved economic confidence and job security, which are key factors couples consider when deciding to have children. This could indicate a higher likelihood of increased fertility rates in Q2 2025, as economic stability often correlates with higher birth rates.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims must fall below 200,000 for any week falling between September 1–16, 2025, as reported by the DOL on or before September 19, 2025. Observable evidence: Official DOL weekly claims report showing a sub-200,000 figure. Key threshold: <200,000. Window: Sept 1–16, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'U.S. initial unemployment claims weekly September 2025' — to find DOL data for Sept 2025. Query 2: 'jobless claims Department of Labor unemployment insurance weekly report September 2025' — to find official report data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Three DOL reports published before Sept 19, 2025: (1) Week ending Aug 30 (reported Sept 4): 237,000 — outside the window. (2) Week ending Sept 6 (reported Sept 11): 263,000 — inside the window but far above 200K. (3) Week ending Sept 13 (reported Sept 18): 231,000 — inside the window but above 200K. No candidate events below 200,000 identified.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Week ending Sept 6 = 263,000 [CalculatedRisk](http://www.calculatedriskblog.com/2025/09/weekly-initial-unemployment-claims_11.html) and [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-weekly-jobless-claims-increase-as-labor-market-softens-4235438). Week ending Sept 13 = 231,000 [Reuters via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-weekly-jobless-claims-fall-124046237.html) and [InvestingChannel](https://news.investingchannel.com/article/696160/weekly-initial-unemployment-claims-decrease-to-231000). Neither value is below 200,000. Criteria NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Reports published Sept 11, 2025 (week ending Sept 6) and Sept 18, 2025 (week ending Sept 13) — both within the Sept 19 publication deadline. Timestamps are exact and reliable.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (claims below 200,000) was found at any point in the September 1–16 window. The minimum observed was 231,000 (week ending Sept 13), well above the 200,000 threshold.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality sources (Reuters, CalculatedRisk, Yahoo Finance, NASDAQ, Barron's, Investing.com) consistently report 263,000 for week ending Sept 6 and 231,000 for week ending Sept 13. No source reports any figure below 200,000 during this period. The 4-week moving average was also above 200K at 240,000–240,500. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Both qualifying weeks within the September 1–16, 2025 window had seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims well above 200,000 (263,000 and 231,000 respectively). The condition of claims falling below 200,000 was never met in this window. Resolution: No.

question: Will Eric Adams join Trump administration by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump officially nominates or appoints Eric Adams to his administration by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The Trump administration includes individuals formally appointed or nominated by Donald Trump to roles within the U.S. federal government, such as Cabinet members, Executive Office staff, senior policy advisors, ambassadors, or White House staff whose appointments are publicly announced by official government channels.

Nominations will qualify even if the individual is not confirmed.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Eric Adams suspend his mayoral campaign and withdraw from the NYC mayoral election by October 6, 2025?

Recent reports indicate that Trump administration officials have been in talks with Adams' team about potential federal positions, including the ambassadorship to Saudi Arabia, as part of a strategy to narrow the field and boost Republican chances against Democratic nominee Zohran Mamdani. Suspending his campaign would be a prerequisite for Adams to potentially accept a Trump administration role, as remaining in the race would conflict with taking a federal position. subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Eric Adams officially suspends his mayoral campaign and withdraws from the New York City mayoral election between 2025-09-06 and 2025-10-06 (inclusive), as confirmed by either: (1) An official filing with the New York City Campaign Finance Board (NYCCFB) showing campaign suspension/withdrawal; or (2) An official public statement from Eric Adams or his campaign spokesperson announcing campaign suspension/withdrawal. The negotiations reported between Trump officials and Adams' team suggest that campaign withdrawal is likely a prerequisite for any federal appointment. This subquestion provides an early observable signal about whether Adams is seriously considering joining the Trump administration, as he would need to exit the mayoral race before accepting any federal role.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for YES: Eric Adams officially suspends his mayoral campaign and withdraws from the NYC mayoral election between 2025-09-06 and 2025-10-06 (inclusive), confirmed by (1) an official NYCCFB filing showing campaign suspension/withdrawal, OR (2) an official public statement from Eric Adams or his campaign spokesperson. evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Eric Adams suspend mayoral campaign withdraw NYC election 2025' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-06) — to find suspension announcement. This is satisfied by: (1) Adams' personal video posted to X on September 28, 2025 explicitly stating 'Despite all we've achieved, I cannot continue my re-election campaign' [ABC News](https://abcnews.go.com/US/eric-adams-ends-campaign-new-york-city-mayor/story?id=125400654); (2) Campaign spokesman Todd Shapiro's confirmation per [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2025/09/28/new-york-city-mayor-eric-adams-reelection-campaign-democratic-socialist-mamdai-cuomo/); (3) Widely reported by multiple major news outlets. Multiple sources confirm Sunday, September 28, 2025 as the date. Using the AP-sourced timestamp from Brandon Sun: 2025-09-28T17:37:00Z (12:37 PM CDT). This is clearly within the resolution window.

TheBlaze article from September 5, 2025 (before the window start) shows Adams actively denied drop-out rumors as of that date.
