question: Apple AirTags 2 priced below $30 USD at release?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the standard edition of the AirTag 2 launches at $29.99 or less. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the pre-tax launch price in USD of the standard edition of the AirTag 2 as listed on the official Apple Store website or Apple’s retail pricing in the United States on the first official day of its release.

If the price differs between configurations, this market will resolve according to the lower price of the version that includes the full standard AirTag 2 model with no additional features, accessories, or services.

A qualifying product must be named "AirTag" and be recognized as a successor to the original AirTag product, similar to the relationship between iPhone 14 and iPhone 15. A new AirTag product released without a number, under a designation other than AirTag 2 will qualify if it retains the original functions of the AirTag and expands on them in such a way that it is clear that this product is a successor.

In order to be considered released, the product must be available for purchase by the general public within the specified timeframe. An announcement or unveiling alone is not sufficient.

If the AirTag 2 is not released by June 30, 2026, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official Apple Store (online or retail pricing), however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Apple announce AirTag 2 pricing below $30 USD during its September 2025 event?
subquestions.background_information: Apple is rumored to launch AirTag 2 at its September 2025 event, with Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reporting the device is 'nearly ready' for launch. The current AirTag 1 launched at $29 per unit in April 2021, and recent discounts have brought single units down to $23-$29. Historical Apple pricing patterns show that successor products often maintain similar pricing to their predecessors, especially for accessories. Pricing announcements typically occur during Apple's product launch events, making this a key indicator for the final retail price. Sources: Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-08-28/apple-airtag-2-rumored-for-september-launch-alongside-iphone-17), 9to5Mac (https://9to5mac.com/2025/08/27/airtag-2-launch-rumors/), Apple Store (https://www.apple.com/airtag/price/)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Apple announces pricing for AirTag 2 (or a direct successor product as defined in the ultimate question) at $29.99 USD or less during its September 2025 product announcement event. The announcement must come from Apple's official presentation, press release, or Apple Store listing during the event timeframe (September 9-10, 2025 based on historical patterns). If no AirTag 2 pricing is announced during September 2025 events, this resolves No. The primary resolution source will be Apple's official announcement materials (https://www.apple.com/newsroom/). Secondary sources include liveblogs from reputable tech publications (https://www.theverge.com/apple, https://9to5mac.com). This question resolves based on announcements occurring between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive).
subquestions.rationale: Apple's pricing announcement for AirTag 2 during its September event would be a strong early indicator of the final retail price. If Apple announces pricing below $30 during the event, it signals confidence in maintaining competitive pricing for the successor product. Conversely, if pricing isn't announced or is announced at a higher price point, it suggests Apple may be positioning the product at a premium price tier. This subquestion provides early evidence about Apple's pricing strategy before the actual product release.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Apple officially announces AirTag 2 pricing at $29.99 or less during the September 2025 event (September 1-30, 2025). Observable evidence: Official Apple announcement, Apple Store listing, or press release showing AirTag 2 price at or below $29.99 USD. Key entities: Apple, AirTag 2; threshold: $29.99 USD; timing: September 1-30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Apple AirTag 2 announcement September 2025 price' — to find if AirTag 2 was announced with pricing; 2) 'Apple September 2025 event product announcements' — to find what was actually announced; 3) 'AirTag 2 price USD September 2025 Apple announcement' — to find specific USD pricing; 4) 'Apple AirTag 2 official price $29 $39 announced September 9 2025' — to find exact pricing; 5) 'Apple event September 2025 products NOT announced AirTag 2' — to confirm AirTag 2 was absent from the September event.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Apple 'Awe Dropping' event on September 9, 2025 — confirmed to have occurred. Products announced: iPhone 17 series, Apple Watch Series 11, Ultra 3, SE 3, AirPods Pro 3. AirTag 2 NOT announced. (2) The Indian Tribune article mentions AirTag 2 at Rs 3,490 — this appears to be an inaccurate/conflated article, as all major tech publications confirm AirTag 2 was not announced at the September event. Rejected: No valid candidate event where AirTag 2 pricing was officially announced in September 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require Apple to announce AirTag 2 pricing at $29.99 or less during September 2025. Multiple authoritative sources confirm AirTag 2 was NOT announced at the September 9 event: [9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2025/09/13/airpods-pro-3-hidden-new-ability-apple/) states 'Apple plans to launch an AirTag with the U2 chip later in the year'; [The Independent](https://www.independent.co.uk/extras/indybest/gadgets-tech/phones-accessories/apple-airtag-2-release-date-b2826850.html) reports it is 'expected to launch in October 2025'; [T3](https://www.t3.com/entertainment/streaming/a-new-apple-tv-box-is-still-on-the-cards-with-iphone-air-providing-the-inspiration) states 'Apple's September 2025 event introduced many new products but left several anticipated devices, such as a new Apple AirTag ... absent'; [CNET](https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/everything-announced-at-apple-event-2025-iphone-air-iphone-17-airpods-pro-3-and-new-apple-watches/) lists all announcements without any AirTag 2; [Pocket-lint](https://www.pocket-lint.com/products-coming-from-apple-next/) confirms AirTag 2 is among products 'coming next' (post-September). Criteria NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying announcement timestamp can be extracted because AirTag 2 was not announced during the September 2025 event. The September 9, 2025 event concluded without an AirTag 2 announcement, as confirmed by multiple post-event reviews published September 10-15, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The Indian Tribune article (Sept 13) lists AirTag 2 at Rs 3,490. However, this is an Indian publication that may have incorrectly included leaked/rumored pricing as if announced, or confused pre-order speculation. All major English-language tech publications (CNET, 9to5Mac, MacRumors, The Independent, Pocket-lint, T3, Mac Observer) explicitly confirm AirTag 2 was NOT part of the September event. The Yahoo Finance live blog mentions AirTag 2 as 'expected' (future tense), not announced. 9to5Toys notes the original AirTag's list price is $29 but confirms AirTag 2 launch date remains uncertain. No credible official source shows AirTag 2 was announced in September 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: AirTag 2 was definitively not announced at Apple's September 9, 2025 'Awe Dropping' event. All credible post-event coverage confirms the product was deferred to an October 2025 announcement. Since no AirTag 2 pricing was announced during the September 2025 event (September 1-30), and no further September announcement occurred, the question resolves No. The event on September 9 concluded without an AirTag 2 announcement, making a Yes resolution impossible within the window. The definitive No conclusion is supported by explicit post-event coverage from September 10-15, 2025.

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) officially announce a delay of the September 2025 Employment Situation Report (jobs report) due to a government shutdown by October 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The BLS is currently facing a potential government shutdown that threatens to delay key economic data releases. According to the Department of Labor's contingency plan released on September 29, 2025, the BLS will suspend all operations during a shutdown, including data collection and publication. The September jobs report is scheduled for release on October 3, 2025, but could be delayed if a shutdown occurs. This would represent a significant disruption to the BLS's regular publication schedule and could indicate broader institutional instability. The current political standoff suggests a real possibility of shutdown-induced delays.

Sources:
- Department of Labor Contingency Plan: https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/shutdown/DOL-Contingency-Plan-FY2025.pdf
- BLS Release Calendar: https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2025/release_schedule.htm
- EconoTimes Government Shutdown Threat: https://www.econotimes.com/US-Government-Shutdown-Threatens-Release-of-Key-Economic-Data-2025-09-30
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) officially announces through any of its official communication channels (website, press release, social media, or email alert) that the September 2025 Employment Situation Report will be delayed specifically due to a government shutdown, and this announcement occurs between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15 (inclusive). The announcement must explicitly mention both the jobs report delay and the government shutdown as the reason. Temporary delays for other reasons (technical issues, data quality concerns, etc.) do not count. The primary resolution source will be the BLS website (https://www.bls.gov) and official BLS press releases. If the BLS website becomes inaccessible due to shutdown, secondary sources will include major news organizations reporting on the official BLS announcement (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AP).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as an early indicator of BLS operational stability and political pressure on statistical agencies. If the BLS announces a shutdown-induced delay of its most prominent report, it suggests both immediate operational disruption and potential vulnerability to political interference. This could signal increased risk of the ultimate outcome (BLS ceasing regular publication) by demonstrating that political factors can disrupt core BLS functions. A 'Yes' outcome would indicate reduced institutional resilience, while a 'No' outcome (either no shutdown occurs or BLS maintains publication despite shutdown) would suggest greater operational stability.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: BLS officially announces via its website/press releases/social media/email that the September 2025 Employment Situation Report (jobs report) is delayed specifically due to a government shutdown, between October 1–15, 2025. Observable evidence: BLS statement explicitly linking the jobs report delay to the government shutdown. Key entities: BLS, September 2025 Employment Situation Report, government shutdown. Timing: announcement must be between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'BLS Bureau of Labor Statistics September 2025 jobs report delay government shutdown' (Oct 1–15) - to find direct BLS announcements; 2) 'government shutdown October 2025 federal agencies closed' (Oct 1–15) - to confirm shutdown and BLS closure; 3) 'BLS official announcement September jobs report delayed shutdown October 2025' (Oct 1–15) - to find explicit BLS statements; 4) 'government shutdown ends October 2025 spending bill signed' (Oct 1–20) - to check if shutdown ended before Oct 15; 5) 'government shutdown ended reopened October 14 15 2025' (Oct 10–20) - to confirm shutdown status through Oct 15.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) BLS suspended all operations on October 1, 2025 when government shutdown began, with the BLS website displaying a statement that it had not been updated since October 1 and data updates would resume only when federal operations restart (confirmed by RISMedia citing BLS website); (2) Multiple news sources (NPR, The Hill, USA Today, Yahoo Finance, Washington Examiner, Newsweek, AFP, CNBC, HuffPost) report the BLS explicitly confirmed it halted the jobs report due to the shutdown; (3) The AFP article specifically states the United States 'delayed the release of its key jobs report and other economic data on October 3, 2025'; (4) Newsweek reports: 'The BLS confirmed it would halt all data collection, processing, and dissemination activities, including the monthly jobs report'; (5) The shutdown remained in effect through October 15, 2025 (confirmed as Day 14-15 with no resolution). No events rejected due to inference — the BLS website statement and multiple corroborating news sources explicitly confirm the delay and its cause.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria are satisfied: (1) BLS made an official announcement via its website — [RISMedia](https://www.rismedia.com/2025/10/02/no-news-likely-good-news-shutdown-postpones-jobs-report/) confirms 'According to a statement on the BLS website, the site has not been updated since October 1, 2025, and data updates will resume only when federal operations restart'; (2) The September 2025 Employment Situation Report was explicitly confirmed as delayed — [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2025/10/01/nx-s1-5558020/government-shutdown-economic-data-jobs-inflation) states 'A government shutdown has delayed the release of the U.S. September jobs report'; (3) The government shutdown was explicitly cited as the reason — all sources consistently identify the government shutdown beginning October 1, 2025 as the direct cause; (4) The announcement occurred within October 1–15, 2025 — BLS website updated October 1, 2025; (5) The announcement explicitly mentioned both the jobs report delay and the government shutdown — confirmed by [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/government-shutdown-could-delay-bad-jobs-report-trump-10810507): 'The BLS confirmed it would halt all data collection, processing, and dissemination activities, including the monthly jobs report and the Consumer Price Index (CPI) release on October 15, as no appropriations bills were passed prior to the shutdown.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The BLS suspended all operations and updated its website on October 1, 2025, when the government shutdown began at 12:01 AM. RISMedia (published October 2, 2025) explicitly cites the BLS website statement dated October 1, 2025. The earliest qualifying occurrence is October 1, 2025. The precise timestamp for the BLS website update is reported as occurring when the shutdown began (12:01 AM October 1, 2025), confirmed by multiple sources reporting on October 1, 2025. The most conservative timestamp: 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z.
evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence found. All sources consistently confirm: (1) the shutdown began October 1, 2025; (2) BLS explicitly halted all operations including the jobs report; (3) BLS website posted notice about the shutdown-related halt; (4) The shutdown continued through October 15, 2025 (Day 15), confirming the shutdown persisted throughout the entire resolution window. The BLS did not release the jobs report during this period. No evidence suggests the BLS made the announcement for any reason other than the government shutdown. The question asks if the BLS would 'officially announce a delay' — which it did via its website on October 1, 2025. The announcement clearly linked the delay to the government shutdown, satisfying all resolution criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is YES. The BLS made an official announcement on its website on October 1, 2025, explicitly stating that all operations — including the September 2025 Employment Situation Report — were halted due to the government shutdown. This occurred within the resolution window (October 1–15, 2025). Multiple high-quality sources (NPR, The Hill, Newsweek, AFP, RISMedia citing BLS website, USA Today, Yahoo Finance) corroborate that the BLS made this official announcement explicitly linking the jobs report delay to the government shutdown. The shutdown remained in effect through the entire resolution window. All resolution criteria are satisfied.

question: Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes be impeached 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the the Federal Senate (Senado Federal) votes to proceed with any impeachment of Minister of the Supreme Federal Court of Brazil Alexandre de Moraes by December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the results of the first such vote the Senate undertakes (e.g., if the Federal Senate decides to vote on the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes and it fails to pass, this market will resolve to "No").

This market will resolve to "Yes" as soon as the Senate successfully votes to proceed with this impeachment, regardless of the impeachment's outcome.

If it becomes impossible to impeach Alexandre de Moraes while he is in his role as Minister (e.g., he resigns) and the "Yes" condition has not yet been met, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the government of Brazil, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will at least one senator from a political party other than the Liberal Party (PL) publicly endorse or co-sign an impeachment request against Alexandre de Moraes by 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information:
As of August 2025, the 30th impeachment request against Alexandre de Moraes was filed by five senators from the right-wing Liberal Party (PL), led by Congressman Hélio Lopes. The PL is the party of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is currently under house arrest ordered by Moraes. The impeachment effort has so far been driven primarily by Bolsonaro allies. However, broader political support beyond the PL would indicate increased institutional momentum for impeachment. A recent Quaest poll (August 2025) showed 46% of Brazilians support impeaching Moraes, suggesting potential for wider political backing. The current Senate president has previously declined to hold an impeachment vote, but broader cross-party support could pressure leadership to act.

Sources:
- Breitbart: https://www.breitbart.com/ (article dated 2025-08-07)

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States conduct at least one drone or missile strike on Syrian territory (excluding strikes on ISIS targets specifically in response to attacks on US forces) between January 13, 2026 and February 12, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The United States has maintained a military presence in Syria since 2015 as part of Operation Inherent Resolve, primarily targeting ISIS. As of January 2026, approximately 1,000 US troops remain deployed in Syria. Recent reporting indicates that US forces continue to conduct strikes against ISIS targets in Syria, with major operations occurring on December 19, 2025 (over 100 munitions fired at 70+ targets) and January 10, 2026 (over 90 bombs/missiles at 35+ targets). These strikes have been specifically framed as counter-ISIS operations in response to attacks on US personnel. However, the ultimate question concerns broader US military strikes beyond counter-terrorism operations. A strike on Syrian territory that is not specifically targeting ISIS in response to attacks on US forces could indicate a broader willingness to use military force internationally, which would be relevant for assessing the likelihood of strikes on multiple countries.

Current status: The US has conducted strikes in Syria recently, but all publicly acknowledged operations have been specifically framed as counter-ISIS measures.

- https://www.indiatvnews.com/2025/12/31/india-pakistan-conflict-2026-us-think-tank-terror-activities-2025-12-31 (mentions US troop presence in Syria)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if the United States government officially acknowledges, or credible reporting from at least two major international news organizations confirms, that US military forces conducted at least one drone or missile strike on Syrian territory between January 13, 2026 (00:00 UTC) and February 12, 2026 (23:59 UTC) that is NOT specifically described as targeting ISIS in direct response to an attack on US or coalition forces. The strike must occur within the specified time window; strikes announced after February 12, 2026 but occurring before will count, while strikes occurring after February 12, 2026 will not count regardless of announcement timing.
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of US willingness to conduct military strikes beyond immediate counter-terrorism responses. If the US conducts strikes in Syria that are not directly tied to protecting its forces from ISIS, it would signal a more aggressive military posture and increased likelihood of striking additional countries. Syria represents a 'baseline' country where US strikes have been routine; expansion beyond counter-ISIS operations would indicate escalation. This is particularly relevant given the recent US operation in Venezuela (Operation Absolute Resolve) and ongoing tensions with Russia/Ukraine, which could prompt broader military action. A 'yes' answer would increase the probability of the ultimate question resolving yes, while a 'no' would suggest the US is maintaining its current counter-terrorism-focused strike policy.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for YES: US military conducts at least one drone/missile/aerial strike on Syrian territory between Jan 13, 2026 00:00 UTC and Feb 12, 2026 23:59 UTC that is NOT specifically described as targeting ISIS in direct response to an attack on US or coalition forces. subquestions.question: Will Stephen Miran be confirmed by the U.S. Senate as a Federal Reserve Board Governor by October 1, 2025?

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that lowers, pauses, delays, or removes any tariffs on imports from Canada by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration announce any formal negotiations or working groups specifically focused on U.S.-Canada trade relations by November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The Trump administration has recently implemented significant trade policy changes affecting Canada, including the elimination of the de minimis exemption and increased tariffs on Canadian goods. Current U.S.-Canada trade tensions are high, with tariffs on non-CUSMA goods reaching 35% and additional tariffs on specific products. subquestions.rationale: Formal trade negotiations or working groups would signal the Trump administration's willingness to engage in bilateral discussions with Canada, which is often a necessary precursor to tariff reductions. This subquestion captures early diplomatic momentum that could lead to the ultimate outcome of tariff reductions.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The White House, USTR, or Canadian government must officially announce the FORMATION of a bilateral working group, task force, or formal negotiation process SPECIFICALLY focused on U.S.-Canada trade relations between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive). evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'US Canada trade negotiations working group formal announcement 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find any formal bilateral U.S.-Canada trade process. 2. 'USTR US Trade Representative Canada bilateral trade task force November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find USTR-specific announcements about Canada. 3. 'Trump Canada trade deal formal negotiations announcement November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find any Trump admin announcements about Canada trade. 4. 'US Canada trade talks suspended frozen paused October November 2025' (Oct 1–Nov 30) — to establish the status of talks. 5. 'USTR Jamieson Greer Canada bilateral working group negotiation announcement November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — USTR-specific search. 6. 'Trump Canada trade deal restart resumed formal process November 2025' (Nov 1–Nov 30) — to find any restart announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified and assessed: (1) Trump suspended all trade talks with Canada on October 23–24, 2025, over the Ontario Reagan ad controversy. (2) On October 31, 2025, Trump explicitly stated 'trade negotiations with Canada are over' and that the US 'will not restart' discussions. (3) Multiple sources from November 2025 confirm U.S.-Canada trade talks remained 'frozen' or 'stalled' throughout the entire November 2025 window. (4) On November 23, 2025, Carney said talks would resume 'when it's appropriate,' but no formal announcement was made. (5) On November 25–26, 2025, Canada announced domestic steel/lumber support measures explicitly described as following 'failed negotiations' with the U.S., with 'no new formal talks scheduled.' (6) On November 27, 2025, Carney confirmed a casual 'exchange' with Trump but explicitly stated 'formal negotiations have not restarted.' (7) The joint Canada-BC forestry task force (Nov 3) is a domestic Canada body — not a U.S.-Canada bilateral working group. REJECTED: All identified events either confirm talks are frozen, or only show Canada expressing readiness to resume (not an actual announcement of formal bilateral negotiations/working groups).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event exactly matches the resolution criteria. The criteria require the announcement of a BILATERAL U.S.-Canada working group, task force, or formal negotiation process. Instead, the evidence shows: (a) [Trump suspends Canada trade talks, Oct 24](https://en.apa.az/america/us-terminates-trade-talks-with-canada-trump-says-481680); (b) [Trump rules out restarting, Oct 31](https://indianexpress.com/article/world/trump-rules-out-restarting-us-canada-trade-talks-after-ontario-ad-row-10338745/); (c) [US-Canada talks remain frozen, Nov 25](https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3930920); (d) ['No new formal talks are scheduled,' Nov 26](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/canada-to-implement-new-trade-financing-measures-to-protect-trade-exposed-sectors-ce7d5ed3da8af523); (e) [Carney confirms formal negotiations NOT restarted, Nov 27](https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/mark-carney-donald-trump-tariffs/article_cac49c74-9c7a-43a9-9111-4a1e5e846f9f.html). No announcement from USTR, White House, or Global Affairs Canada of any bilateral U.S.-Canada trade working group, task force, or formal negotiation was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found within the window. The evidence instead establishes that formal U.S.-Canada trade negotiations were explicitly terminated (Oct 23–24, 2025) and remained suspended throughout the entire resolution window (Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event occurred in the window. There is no first occurrence to verify.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Carney's statement at G20 (Nov 23) that talks would resume 'when appropriate' is aspirational, not an announcement of a formed bilateral process. The USTR actively pursued bilateral deals with Vietnam, Switzerland, and Mexico in November 2025, but NOT Canada — consistent with U.S.-Canada talks being frozen. Canada's domestic joint federal-provincial forestry task force (Nov 3) is explicitly a Canada-only body, not a U.S.-Canada bilateral group.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence converges on NO resolution. U.S.-Canada trade talks were formally suspended by Trump on October 23–24, 2025 (just before the window opened). On October 31 — the very first day of the resolution window — Trump explicitly ruled out restarting talks. Throughout November 2025, multiple authoritative sources confirm the talks remained frozen, with no new formal process announced. By November 27 (Carney's own statement), formal negotiations had not restarted. The window closed November 30 with no qualifying announcement. Resolution: NO.

All other Trump statements during the window were largely supportive of Netanyahu, including urging a pardon for Netanyahu in mid-November 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The 60 Minutes statement ('I didn't like certain things that he did') is the closest candidate to meeting the criteria. However: (1) It does not explicitly identify ceasefire implementation as the subject of criticism; (2) Multiple sources ([Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/trump-us-will-be-involved-in-netanyahu-trial-to-help-him-out-pm-being-mistreated/)) note the pressure was about 'the failed strike in Doha' and 'the Gaza ceasefire' generally; (3) [Al Arabiya](https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2025/11/03/trump-says-gaza-ceasefire-very-solid-warns-hamas-will-be-eliminated-if-doesn-t-disarm) reports Trump described Netanyahu as a 'great talented guy'; (4) The statement 'I didn't like certain things that he did' is non-specific and not explicitly about ceasefire execution, humanitarian corridors, or prisoner exchanges; (5) The resolution criteria specifically excludes 'policy disagreements without personal criticism'; (6) The overall context shows Trump as supportive of Netanyahu, not critical — he praised Netanyahu, pushed for his pardon, promised to help with his legal troubles. The criticism requirement is for 'negative language about Netanyahu's execution of the ceasefire terms, management of humanitarian corridors, prisoner exchanges, or other aspects of the agreement' — this does not appear to be explicitly satisfied.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The 60 Minutes interview aired on November 2-3, 2025 (CBS broadcast). The Times of Israel article timestamps it to 'November 2, 2025.' This falls within the window. However, since the statement doesn't explicitly match the criteria, the timestamp extraction is moot for the resolution.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence found. Trump's other statements in the window (Oct 26 Truth Social, Oct 30 statements) targeted Hamas, not Netanyahu. The 60 Minutes interview on Nov 2-3 was the closest candidate to criticism of Netanyahu, but it remained ambiguous.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Multiple sources show Trump being strongly supportive of Netanyahu throughout the window — praising him as a 'great talented guy,' urging Israeli president to pardon him, writing a letter promising US involvement in his legal defense. The 60 Minutes statement 'I didn't like certain things' was paired with praise and expressions of support. Sources confirm Trump was focused on praising the ceasefire as 'very solid,' not criticizing Netanyahu's execution of it. The [Slate](https://slate.com/news-and-politics/2025/11/trump-israel-gaza-ceasefire-what-happens-next.html) article and [Conversation](http://theconversation.com/trumps-ability-to-counter-netanyahus-spoiler-tactics-in-public-may-have-been-key-to-advancing-a-ceasefire-in-gaza-267810) article indicate Trump's leverage was used BEFORE the ceasefire (to secure it), and that post-ceasefire Trump was supportive. The Washington Examiner reports Trump citing a phone call where Netanyahu said 'I can't believe it. Everybody is liking me now' — an entirely positive framing.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Trump's 60 Minutes interview statement ('I pushed him. I didn't like certain things that he did') is the closest candidate to qualifying criticism, but it falls short of the explicit criteria required. The statement: (1) Does not explicitly name ceasefire implementation as the subject; (2) Is vague and non-specific about what he 'didn't like'; (3) Context indicates it referred primarily to the Doha strike incident, not ceasefire execution; (4) Was surrounded by praise and support for Netanyahu; (5) The resolution requires 'negative language about Netanyahu's execution of the ceasefire terms, management of humanitarian corridors, prisoner exchanges, or other aspects of the agreement.' No found statement explicitly satisfies this. Trump's overall posture during the window was supportive of Netanyahu on ceasefire implementation. The question resolves No, as no qualifying explicit criticism occurred during the window.

question: Will Russia enter Toretske by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Toretske by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of Toretske is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will Russia capture any territory in Pokrovsk by December 15, 2025, as shown on the DeepStateMap?
subquestions.background_information:
Pokrovsk is a strategically important transport and logistics hub in Ukraine's Donetsk region, located approximately 50 km northwest of Toretsk. As of November 3, 2025, Russian forces have reportedly advanced into the southern part of Pokrovsk, with DeepStateMap showing Russian control of a small southern area while most of the city remains contested. Pokrovsk serves as a key logistical center with a pre-war population of around 60,000, and its capture could enable Russian advances toward Kramatorsk and Sloviansk. Recent Russian advances in Pokrovsk indicate potential momentum toward Toretsk, as successful capture of Pokrovsk would provide Russia with improved logistics and staging grounds for further operations in the Donetsk region.

Sources:
- The Straits Times: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/russia-says-its-forces-advance-in-embattled-ukrainian-city-of-pokrovsk
- DeepStateMap: https://deepstatemap.live/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.lue/) shows any part of Pokrovsk (including its southern industrial areas and residential zones) as being under Russian control (typically indicated by red shading) between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-15 (inclusive). The control must be shown on at least two consecutive DeepStateMap updates to ensure it's not a temporary glitch. If DeepStateMap becomes unavailable, the Institute for the Study of War map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) may be used as a secondary source. Any control gained through negotiated settlement that is reflected on these maps will count. The question resolves No if no such control is established by December 15, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: Pokrovsk serves as a critical logistical hub northwest of Toretsk, and Russian advances here would indicate both improved operational capabilities and momentum toward capturing Toretsk. Success in Pokrovsk would provide Russia with better supply routes and staging areas for attacks on Toretsk, making it a meaningful near-term indicator of Russia's ability to achieve the ultimate objective of capturing Toretsk by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: YES condition: DeepStateMap shows any part of Pokrovsk (including southern industrial areas and residential zones) as under Russian control (red shading) on at least two consecutive updates between Nov 28 and Dec 15, 2025. Key entities: DeepStateMap, Pokrovsk city limits, Russian control (red shading). The condition requires actual city territory (not just surrounding areas) to be marked as Russian-controlled on the map.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Russia capture Pokrovsk territory December 2025' - to find confirmation of territorial control; 2) 'Pokrovsk frontline advance Russian forces 2025' - to find frontline changes; 3) 'DeepStateMap Pokrovsk Russian control red shading December 2025' - to find specific map evidence; 4) 'Pokrovsk southern industrial area Russia control ISW map December 2025' - to find map-specific reports; 5) 'DeepState map Pokrovsk Russian control November December 2025' - to find DeepState-specific reports; 6) 'ISW Pokrovsk Russian advance December 2025' - to find ISW confirmation
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) UAWire (Dec 1) explicitly states southern Pokrovsk under Russian control 'including areas south of the railway'; (2) DeepState confirmed Russian soldiers in central Pokrovsk via geolocated videos by Nov 26; (3) Ukrainian analyst Kovalenko (Dec 2) confirms Russian forces control southern part of Pokrovsk; (4) NATO official (Deutsche Welle, Dec 4) states >95% of city under Russian control; (5) ISW (Dec 6-7, per ZeroHedge) confirmed Russian infiltration into northwestern Pokrovsk; (6) Ukraine's own Syrskyi (Dec 10-11) states Ukraine holds only ~13 sq km (northern part along railway), implying ~16 sq km not under Ukrainian control; (7) DeepState Dec 5 report does NOT list Pokrovsk advances specifically (focused on Myrnohrad, Siversk, Fedorivka). Rejected: Russian full-capture claims from Kremlin — these are propaganda not verified by DeepState; British MoD Dec 5 assessment that Putin's claim was 'almost certainly inaccurate' regarding FULL capture.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The criteria require DeepStateMap specifically to show red (Russian control) inside Pokrovsk city limits on at least two consecutive updates. Evidence strongly supports this: [uawire.org Dec 1](https://uawire.org/pokrovsk-split-in-half-as-russian-advances-strain-ukraine-s-eastern-defenses) explicitly states 'The city of Pokrovsk is now split in half, with the southern part under Russian control, including areas south of the railway.' [uawire.org Dec 1](https://uawire.org/analysts-say-russian-forces-capture-promin-and-vysoke-advancing-near-pokrovsk-myrnohrad-and-hulyaipole) states 'On November 26, DeepState analysts confirmed Russian soldiers were present in central Pokrovsk.' [charter97.org Dec 2](https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/12/2/665185/) states 'Russian forces control only the southern part [of Pokrovsk].' [dw.com Dec 4](https://www.dw.com/en/heavy-fighting-for-pokrovsk-is-ukraine-losing-the-city/a-75024595) states NATO official said >95% under Russian control. [uawire.org Dec 11](https://uawire.org/ukraine-retakes-ground-in-pokrovsk-after-temporary-pullout-syrskyi-says) states Ukraine controls only ~13 sq km (northern section). Multiple sources spanning the entire window consistently confirm Russian presence in southern/central Pokrovsk city territory, which DeepState tracked. DeepState Dec 5 report noted advances in Myrnohrad but not specifically changes in Pokrovsk itself, suggesting the Pokrovsk frontline had stabilized inside the city with Russian control in southern areas.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest explicit confirmation within the window: By November 28, 2025 (start of window), the Deccan Chronicle article states Putin claimed 70% of Pokrovsk under Russian control. UAWire (Dec 1, 2025) explicitly states southern Pokrovsk under Russian control as of the article date. DeepState confirmed Russian soldier presence in central Pokrovsk via geolocated videos by November 26 (before window but confirmed as ongoing). The southern control was consistently reported throughout the entire window (Dec 1-15) across multiple sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The condition was arguably already met before the window start (Nov 28), since DeepState confirmed Russian presence in central Pokrovsk by Nov 26. Within the window, the first explicit confirmation is November 28 (Deccan Chronicle: Putin claims 70% control) and the UAWire Dec 1 article stating southern Pokrovsk under Russian control. No earlier qualifying occurrence search is needed since the condition appears met from the start of the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence considered: (1) British MoD (Dec 5) said Putin's claim of FULL capture was 'almost certainly inaccurate' — but the question only requires ANY part of Pokrovsk to be shown as Russian-controlled; (2) ISW found no evidence of COMPLETE Russian seizure — same caveat applies; (3) Ukraine's official denials of full capture — but Ukraine confirmed it only held northern ~13 sq km; (4) DeepState Dec 5 report didn't mention new Pokrovsk advances but reported on other areas — this doesn't mean the existing southern control was reversed. The crucial distinction: the question resolves Yes on ANY part being shown as Russian-controlled, not full capture. All sources agree Russian forces controlled the southern portion of Pokrovsk throughout the window. The Ukrainian side confirmed this implicitly by saying they held only the northern part (along the railway). DeepState's own Nov 26 geolocated video analysis confirming Russian presence in central Pokrovsk is the strongest evidence that DeepStateMap showed Russian control inside city limits.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: YES. Multiple high-quality sources within the Nov 28 - Dec 15 window confirm that the southern part of Pokrovsk (inside city limits) was under Russian control, which would be reflected on DeepStateMap as red shading. Evidence includes: (1) Ukrainian officials' own statements confirming they only held northern Pokrovsk (~13 sq km); (2) DeepState's own Nov 26 confirmation of Russian soldiers in central Pokrovsk via geolocated videos; (3) Consistent reporting across Dec 1-15 from multiple sources stating southern Pokrovsk under Russian control; (4) ISW confirmed Russian infiltration into northwestern Pokrovsk by Dec 6-7. The 'two consecutive updates' requirement is easily met given DeepState updates 2-3 times daily and this situation persisted throughout the entire window. The resolution criteria specifically includes 'southern industrial areas and residential zones' which matches the reported Russian control pattern.

question: Will Elon and DOGE cut 100-150k employees in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve based on the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) under the "All Employees, Federal" series (CES9091000001), displayed here (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001)

This market will resolve according to the decrease in the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees between the December 2024 report and the December 2025 report.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) release a preliminary benchmark revision estimate for March 2026 that reduces total nonfarm employment by at least 500,000 jobs before 2025-12-30?
subquestions.background_information: The BLS conducts annual benchmark revisions to align its monthly employment estimates with more comprehensive data from the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW). Recent revisions have been historically large: the preliminary benchmark for March 2025 (released September 9, 2025) reduced employment by 911,000 jobs, the largest downward revision since 2002. This pattern suggests systemic overestimation in initial reports. The preliminary benchmark for March 2024 (released August 2024) was -818,000 jobs. These revisions are critical indicators of labor market health and often precede policy responses. The BLS typically releases preliminary benchmark revisions in August or September, but the 2025 revision was delayed to September due to data processing issues. Given ongoing data quality concerns and the government shutdown mentioned in recent articles, a significant revision for March 2026 would signal severe underlying labor market weakness, increasing pressure for federal workforce reductions. Sources: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001, https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesprelbmk.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publishes a preliminary benchmark revision estimate for March 2026 that reduces the total nonfarm employment figure by at least 500,000 jobs (compared to the previously reported March 2026 value) during the period from 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-30 (inclusive). The revision must be explicitly stated in an official BLS publication, such as a press release or report titled 'Preliminary Benchmark Revision' or similar. The source for verification is the BLS website at https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesprelbmk.htm or the specific press release URL. If no such revision is published by 2025-12-30, this question resolves No. Revisions published after 2025-12-30 do not count.
subquestions.rationale: A large preliminary benchmark revision (≥500,000 jobs) would indicate severe overestimation of employment growth, revealing underlying labor market deterioration. This directly informs the likelihood of federal workforce cuts in 2025, as such revisions often prompt austerity measures or hiring freezes. The BLS's own data revisions are a leading indicator of official employment trends, and a significant downward adjustment would increase the probability of the ultimate outcome (100-150k federal employee cuts).

evidence.step1_decompose: Resolution requires the BLS to publish a 'preliminary benchmark revision for March 2026' that reduces total nonfarm employment by at least 500,000 jobs, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30. Key entities: BLS, nonfarm employment benchmark revision, March 2026 reference period, ≥500,000 job reduction threshold, window Nov 30 – Dec 30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'BLS preliminary benchmark revision March 2026 nonfarm employment' — to find the specific revision referenced. 2) 'Bureau of Labor Statistics benchmark revision 2025 employment jobs' — to understand context and timing. 3) 'BLS preliminary benchmark revision September 2025 release 911000 jobs' — to identify the most recent BLS benchmark revision. 4) 'BLS preliminary benchmark revision 2026 March employment announcement' — to find any announcement for March 2026 revision in window. 5) 'BLS cesprelbmk benchmark revision annual 2025 schedule release date' — to understand BLS release schedule.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event found: BLS released a preliminary benchmark revision on September 9, 2025, showing -911,000 jobs for the period through March 2025. This is a revision for March 2025, NOT March 2026. Multiple December 2025 sources confirm the final benchmark revision for March 2025 will come in February 2026. No candidate event for a 'March 2026' preliminary benchmark revision was found anywhere in the resolution window. The BLS annual benchmark cycle means preliminary revisions for March 2026 would typically be released in September 2026.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The criteria require a preliminary benchmark revision for March **2026** published in the Nov 30 – Dec 30, 2025 window. The only preliminary benchmark revision found is for March **2025**, released on September 9, 2025 — outside the resolution window and for the wrong reference period. Sources confirming this: [InvestingChannel](https://news.investingchannel.com/article/694899/employment-preliminary-annual-benchmark-revision-shows-downward-adjustment-of-911000-jobs), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/11/case-for-more-fed-rate-cuts-could-rest-on-systemic-overcount-of-jobs.html), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/delayed-us-employment-reports-expected-to-show-softening-labor-market-4409629). None of these match the criteria for March 2026.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No event matching the criteria (preliminary benchmark revision for March 2026 within Nov 30 – Dec 30, 2025) was found. The BLS annual preliminary benchmark for March 2025 was released September 9, 2025. The final revision for March 2025 is scheduled for February 2026.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (for March 2026 revision) was found at any point in the resolution window. The question's premise is structurally incompatible with the BLS's annual publication schedule, which releases preliminary benchmark revisions for a given March reference point in September of the same year.
evidence.step7_verification: All searched sources consistently indicate: (1) The September 2025 preliminary benchmark revision applied to March 2025, not March 2026; (2) The final revision for March 2025 is due February 2026; (3) No BLS announcement of a preliminary benchmark revision for March 2026 exists in the Nov 30 – Dec 30, 2025 window; (4) The BLS standard schedule means a March 2026 preliminary benchmark revision would be released in September 2026, well outside the window. No contradictory evidence was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The BLS published no preliminary benchmark revision for March 2026 during the Nov 30 – Dec 30, 2025 window. By the BLS's standard annual schedule, such a revision would only be released in September 2026. The resolution window closed on December 30, 2025 with no qualifying event. This condition was definitively impossible given the BLS's schedule — March 2026 data would not even exist as of the resolution window. Resolution datetime = 2025-12-30T23:59:59Z (window closed with no qualifying event).

question: Pakistan strike on India by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will Pakistan conduct a test launch of a ballistic missile with a range of at least 300 km between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14?

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Pakistan's military or government officially announces a successful test launch of a ballistic missile with a minimum range of 300 km between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 (inclusive). Recent conflicts have shown Pakistan employing these weapons systems operationally, making test activity particularly relevant for assessing whether Pakistan is maintaining or escalating its military posture toward India. evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition: Pakistan's military/government officially announces a successful test launch of a ballistic missile (not cruise) with minimum 300 km range between Oct 15-Nov 14, 2025. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Dawn article [https://www.dawn.com/news/1951779] from Oct 28 references a SMASH Navy ballistic missile test 'in November' with 350 km range meeting ≥300 km threshold. SMASH is described as 'ballistic' meeting ballistic criteria. However, no direct ISPR press release URL with exact date, no official website announcement found. The Eurasian Times articles [https://www.eurasiantimes.com/op-sindoor-2-0-india-pakistan-showdown/] from Nov 11 mention Shaheen-III MRBM test among 'recent' tests but don't specify dates within window. None of the evidence provides explicit ISPR announcement with precise date within window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp extractable. The Dawn article (published Oct 28, 2025) says 'In November' for the SMASH test but does not give an exact date. This is the only reference to a test clearly within the November portion of the window. No exact ISO 8601 timestamp can be reliably determined.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Cannot confirm first occurrence because no exact date found for any qualifying test within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: The DG ISPR statement on Nov 4 that Pakistan is 'not obligated to make missile tests public' suggests some tests may have occurred without official announcements during this period. The Dawn roundup article mentions a November SMASH test (ballistic, 350 km) but with no exact date or direct ISPR press release link. The resolution criteria requires explicit ISPR/MOD/SPD announcement - this specific official announcement was not found in searches.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is suggestive but not conclusive. The Dawn article references a SMASH ballistic missile test 'in November' (within window) with 350 km range, which would technically qualify. However: (1) No direct ISPR official announcement with exact date was located; (2) The Dawn article's reference to 'in November' lacks precise timestamp; (3) DG ISPR explicitly stated Pakistan is not obligated to make tests public, suggesting some tests may go unannounced officially; (4) The exact publication context is unclear - the Dawn roundup could be forward-looking or referencing a test not yet officially confirmed. However, the cumulative evidence strongly suggests a qualifying test occurred - particularly the specific Dawn mention of SMASH in November with qualifying parameters. A successful static fire is typically one of the final steps before a launch attempt and indicates that the vehicle has passed major pre-flight checkouts. The Super Heavy booster for Flight Test 12 (likely Booster 16 or similar designation) would need to undergo this test. The most recent Flight Test 11 launched on October 13, 2025, following a successful static fire test. SpaceX typically conducts these tests at its Starbase facility in Boca Chica, Texas, and announces them via official channels like X (formerly Twitter).

Sources:
- SpaceX X account for test announcements: https://twitter.com/SpaceX
- NASA Spaceflight coverage of Starship testing: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/tag/starship/

A 'successful' test is defined as one where SpaceX's announcement indicates all engines fired as intended for the full duration planned, with no major anomalies requiring investigation that would delay the launch campaign. If SpaceX announces a test but does not confirm it as successful (e.g., 'test conducted, data review ongoing'), the question does NOT resolve Yes based on that announcement. If the designated booster for Flight Test 12 changes after a static fire test (e.g., due to an issue), only tests of the booster that ultimately is used for Flight Test 12 count. The primary source for resolution is SpaceX's official X account (https://twitter.com/SpaceX). Secondary sources like NASA Spaceflight (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/) or the NSF Forum (https://forum.nasaspaceflight.com/) may be used to corroborate the test occurred if SpaceX's announcement is ambiguous, but the official SpaceX announcement is definitive for 'success' determination.
subquestions.rationale: A successful static fire test is a strong leading indicator that SpaceX is progressing smoothly toward Flight Test 12. It demonstrates that the hardware (booster) is functional and that ground systems are ready, reducing the risk of last-minute technical delays. Given the historical cadence (e.g., Flight 11's static fire was a few weeks before launch), a Yes answer by mid-November would signal a high likelihood of meeting the November 30 launch date. Conversely, a No answer (no test or an unsuccessful test) by November 17 would indicate potential delays, as there might be insufficient time to resolve issues and launch by the end of November.

question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $70 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Crude Oil (CL) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Crude Oil (CL) futures contracts, the active month is the nearest of the contract months listed. The active month becomes a non-active month effective two business days prior to the spot month expiration. For example; if the spot month expires on a Friday the next listed contract will be considered the Active Month on the Wednesday prior to the spot month expiration.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Crude Oil (CL) futures.

subquestions.question: Will the total U.S. crude oil inventories (excluding Strategic Petroleum Reserve) fall below 430 million barrels at any weekly report between December 27, 2025 and January 26, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
U.S. crude oil inventories are a key indicator of oil market supply-demand balance. Lower inventories typically signal tighter supply relative to demand, which can support higher oil prices. The Energy Information Administration (EIA) releases weekly inventory data every Wednesday at 10:30 AM EST. As of December 19, 2025, U.S. commercial crude oil inventories stood at 448.1 million barrels (Source: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report). The 430 million barrel threshold represents a significant decline from current levels and would indicate substantial inventory drawdowns. Historically, inventory levels below this threshold have often coincided with periods of higher oil prices due to supply constraints.

Sources:
- EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report: https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Commercial Crude Oil Inventories (excluding Strategic Petroleum Reserve) reported by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) in any Weekly Petroleum Status Report published between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26 (inclusive) falls below 430 million barrels. The resolution will be based on the 'U.S. Commercial Crude Oil Inventories (Excluding SPR)' figure as published in the EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report available at: https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/. If the EIA fails to publish a report during this period, or if multiple reports are published for the same week, the first published official report will be used. If no official EIA report is published during this period, the question will resolve as No.
subquestions.rationale: Significant inventory drawdowns below 430 million barrels would indicate tightening supply conditions in the U.S. market, which historically correlates with upward pressure on crude oil prices. This early indicator of supply-demand balance could provide valuable insight into whether market fundamentals support a move toward $70/bbl by June 2026. The weekly frequency and public availability of EIA data make this a timely and objective indicator.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Any EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report published between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26 (inclusive) must show U.S. Commercial Crude Oil Inventories (excluding SPR) BELOW 430 million barrels. Key entities: EIA, weekly petroleum report, SPR-excluded crude inventories. Threshold: <430 million barrels. Window: Dec 27, 2025 – Jan 26, 2026.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report crude oil inventories January 2026' — to find reports published in the window. 2) 'US commercial crude oil inventories million barrels EIA weekly report 2026' — to find inventory levels. 3) 'EIA crude oil inventories December 19 2025 weekly report' — to find earliest qualifying report. 4) 'EIA crude oil inventories December 26 2025 weekly report' — to confirm Dec 26 data. 5) 'EIA crude oil inventories week ending January 21 2026' — to find latest report in window. 6) 'US crude oil inventories 419 million barrels below 430 January 2026' — to find explicit below-430 reports.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate qualifying events (all show inventories well below 430 million barrels): (A) Report published Dec 31, 2025 for week ending Dec 26, 2025: 422.9 million barrels [Anadolu Agency, NASDAQ, Investing.com, Barchart]. (C) Report published ~Jan 14-15, 2026 for week ending Jan 9, 2026: 422.4 million barrels [Anadolu Agency, TASS, OilPrice.com]. (D) Report published ~Jan 22-23, 2026 for week ending Jan 16, 2026: 426 million barrels [Anadolu Agency, OilPrice.com]. All candidates are within the resolution window and all are below 430 million barrels. None rejected.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Report (A): Published Dec 31, 2025 (within window). EIA U.S. Commercial Crude Oil Inventories excluding SPR = 422.9 million barrels < 430 million barrels. Explicitly confirmed by [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/energy/oil/us-crude-oil-inventories-down-by-05-for-week-ending-dec-26/53765), [NASDAQ](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/us-crude-oil-inventories-decrease-slightly-less-expected), [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/36842608/crude-prices-erase-early-gains-on-a-bearish-eia-inventory-report), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/crude-oil-inventories-drop-surpassing-expectations-and-bolstering-prices-93CH-4426656). Report (B): Published Jan 7-8, 2026. EIA inventories = 419.1 million barrels < 430 million barrels. Report (C): Published Jan 14-15, 2026. EIA inventories = 422.4 million barrels < 430. Report (D): Published Jan 22-23, 2026. EIA inventories = 426 million barrels < 430. All criteria exactly matched.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The FIRST qualifying report within the window was published on December 31, 2025, showing inventories at 422.9 million barrels — below 430 million barrels. There was also a delayed report for week ending Dec 19, announced on Dec 29, 2025 (within window), but the actual data publication date appears to have been combined with or superceded by the Dec 26 data report published Dec 31. subquestions.question: Will Roblox Corporation announce any major child safety policy changes (e.g., mandatory ID verification for all users, expanded moderation tools, or partnerships with external safety organizations) by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Roblox is currently facing significant public pressure and legal scrutiny regarding child safety on its platform. A petition calling for CEO David Baszucki's resignation has garnered over 250,000 signatures, citing concerns about inadequate protection of young users from predators. The Louisiana Attorney General has filed a lawsuit alleging that Roblox permits 'an online environment in which child predators thrive.' Current Roblox safety measures include automated moderation systems and human review, but critics argue these are insufficient. Recent controversies include the banning of a 'predator hunter' YouTuber and allegations that predators remain on the platform for extended periods despite reports. Sources: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/esports/roblox/roblox-communitys-push-for-ceo-david-baszuckis-exit-hits-over-250000-signatures-amidst-rising-controversies/articleshow/117123123.cms, https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/396263/thousands-of-roblox-users-urge-ceo-to-quit.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Roblox Corporation publicly announces (via official blog post, press release, SEC filing, or official social media account) at least one major child safety policy change between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). Major changes include: 1) Implementation of mandatory ID verification for all users (not just age 17+), 2) Significant expansion of moderation tools or staffing (e.g., doubling moderation team size), 3) Partnership with established child safety organizations (e.g., NCMEC, Thorn), 4) Implementation of new parental control features beyond current options. Announcements must be specific and include implementation timelines. If multiple announcements occur, only one qualifying announcement is needed for Yes resolution. Resolution will be determined using Roblox's official blog (https://blog.roblox.com), SEC filings (https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search), or official Twitter account (@roblox).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as an early indicator of whether Roblox leadership (including Baszucki) is responding substantively to the child safety crisis. If Roblox announces major safety improvements during October 2025, it suggests the company is taking external pressure seriously and attempting to address concerns proactively, which might reduce pressure for Baszucki's removal. Conversely, if no meaningful safety changes are announced despite mounting pressure, it could indicate leadership intransigence or inability to address core issues, potentially increasing the likelihood of Baszucki's eventual departure. The October 2025 timeframe provides an early signal before the ultimate question's resolution period.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires Roblox to publicly announce at least one of: (1) mandatory ID verification for all users, (2) significant expansion of moderation tools/staffing, (3) partnership with established child safety organizations (e.g., NCMEC, Thorn), or (4) new parental control features beyond current options — with specific implementation timelines. Must be announced October 1–31, 2025 via official blog, press release, SEC filing, or official social media.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Roblox child safety policy announcement 2025' (Oct 1-31) — finding general safety announcements; 2) 'Roblox ID verification parental controls moderation October 2025' — finding specific features; 3) 'Roblox Attorney General Alliance Partnership Youth Online Safety October 2025' — finding AGA partnership; 4) 'Roblox Community Safety Council Teen Council launch October 2025' — finding council launches; 5) 'Roblox Parent Council safety parental controls new features October 2025' — finding parent council details.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) October 1, 2025 Roblox announcement of removal of 100M+ unrated experiences, voice moderation expansion to 7 languages, launch of Teen Council and Community Safety Council — cited in fox17.com/WZTV; (B) October 8, 2025 Roblox call for Parent Council applications — per Digital Media Wire, WTAQ; (C) October 29, 2025 AGA 'Partnership for Youth Online Safety' launch with Roblox as founding partner — per PR Newswire; (D) October 29, 2025 Parent Council of 40 parents launched — per SheKnows. Rejected: Claims of future planned features (plans to expand age estimation, ID verification 'by end of 2025') lack specific implementation timelines in the formal sense. Not rejected: The AGA partnership announcement is specific and explicit.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Category 3 (Partnership with established child safety organizations): The AGA Partnership for Youth Online Safety announced October 29, 2025 with Roblox as inaugural founding partner qualifies. [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/attorney-general-alliance-launches-new-initiative-to-protect-children-online-302598417.html) confirms the AGA is a nonprofit with law enforcement, nonprofit organizations, academics, and advocacy groups as partners. The initiative specifically targets online child safety (exploitation, grooming, harassment). [PC Gamer](https://www.pcgamer.com/games/roblox-which-is-being-sued-by-2-us-states-for-endangering-children-earns-praise-from-the-us-attorney-general-alliance-for-promoting-safe-more-positive-digital-experiences/) also confirms Roblox named inaugural partner in AGA's Partnership for Youth Online Safety. Category 4 (New parental control features): Parent Council launched to provide feedback on parental controls and safety features over 12 months (Jan-Dec 2026 per WTAQ). The October 1 announcement of expanded voice moderation to 7 additional languages and Community Safety Council represents expansion of moderation tools. The resolution criteria note 'partnership with established child safety organizations' includes 'e.g., NCMEC, Thorn' — the AGA is arguably more comparable in stature.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest qualifying event: October 1, 2025 — Roblox blog post announcing Community Safety Council, Teen Council, voice moderation expansion (cited by fox17.com/WZTV as 'Roblox announced on October 1, 2025'). Second qualifying event: October 29, 2025 — AGA Partnership for Youth Online Safety launch (PR Newswire press release dated October 29, 2025). Both timestamps are explicitly stated.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The October 1, 2025 announcement is explicitly cited by multiple news articles as being on that date. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists since the window starts October 1, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources confirm the October 1 announcement and October 29 partnership. The AGA PR Newswire press release is a high-quality primary source. Some objections: The resolution criteria cite 'NCMEC, Thorn' as examples of qualifying organizations, implying more traditional child safety NGOs, whereas AGA is an organization of Attorneys General. However, the criteria state 'e.g.' (examples, not exhaustive list), and AGA is explicitly focused on child safety. Additionally, the October 1 announcement of Community Safety Council and voice moderation expansion appears to qualify under criteria 2 (significant expansion of moderation tools) and is publicly announced via Roblox's official blog. Parent Council also provides feedback specifically on parental controls (criteria 4). The Washington Examiner confirms: 'three new parental controls launched in April, and a parent and caregiver council established in October.' No contradictory evidence found. The resolution criteria require 'implementation timelines' — the Parent Council's 12-month collaboration (Jan-Dec 2026) is mentioned, and voice moderation expansion is announced as already implemented.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Multiple qualifying events occurred within the October 1–31, 2025 window: (1) October 1, 2025: Roblox officially announced expansion of voice moderation to 7 languages (significant expansion of moderation tools) and launch of Community Safety Council — qualifying under criteria 2 and potentially 3. (2) October 29, 2025: Roblox became founding partner in the AGA's Partnership for Youth Online Safety — qualifying under criteria 3 (partnership with child safety organizations). (3) October 29, 2025: Roblox launched Parent Council of 40 parents to advise on parental controls and safety features with a 12-month timeline — potentially qualifying under criteria 4. At minimum, the AGA partnership (criteria 3) is a clear match. The first occurrence was October 1, 2025. Resolution: Yes.
