subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury report a federal budget deficit of at least $1.9 trillion for fiscal year 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. federal budget deficit is a primary driver of national debt growth. The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) reported on September 9, 2025 that the U.S. had accumulated a $2 trillion deficit over the first 11 months of fiscal year 2025 (October 2024 through August 2025), with total FY2025 spending of $6.7 trillion and revenues of $4.7 trillion. The CBO projected the total deficit for FY2025 would be $1.8 trillion. However, actual deficits often differ from projections, and the final FY2025 deficit figure will be a crucial indicator of whether the national debt continues accelerating toward $38 trillion. The Treasury Department typically releases the final monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) for September, which concludes FY2025, within a few weeks after the fiscal year ends on September 30.

Sources:
- KPVI: https://www.kpvi.com/news/national_news/report-u-s-racked-up-2-trillion-deficit-over-past-11-months/article_8a5d3a4c-6d5f-11ef-bf8c-7b4d4f5c3c7c.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the U.S. Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement for September 2025 (the final month of fiscal year 2025) reports a total federal budget deficit of $1.9 trillion or greater for fiscal year 2025 (October 1, 2024 - September 30, 2025). The deficit figure must be published on the Treasury Department's official website between October 1, 2025 and October 19, 2025 (inclusive). If the Treasury Department does not publish the September 2025 MTS by October 19, 2025, this question resolves as NO. The official source is the Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement publication: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/monthly-treasury-statement/.
subquestions.rationale: The federal budget deficit directly contributes to national debt accumulation. A deficit of $1.9 trillion or higher would indicate continued rapid debt growth, making it more likely the $38 trillion threshold will be reached in 2025. Given the CBO's projection of a $1.8 trillion deficit and the reported $2 trillion deficit through August, this threshold represents a meaningful acceleration beyond projections. The resolution timing (mid-October) aligns with when the Treasury typically releases final FY2025 data, providing an early indicator of debt trajectory before year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for YES: U.S. Treasury's September 2025 Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) must report a total FY2025 federal budget deficit of $1.9 trillion or greater, published between October 1–19, 2025 on the Treasury's official website. Key threshold: $1.9T deficit. Key entity: U.S. Treasury Department MTS publication.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'U.S. Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement September 2025 federal budget deficit fiscal year 2025' — to find the official MTS release and deficit figure. Query 2: 'federal budget deficit fiscal year 2025 total annual Treasury report' — to find corroborating sources. Query 3: 'Treasury Department MTS Monthly Treasury Statement September 2025 published October 16' — to confirm publication date. Query 4: 'fiscal year 2025 deficit $1.775 trillion $1.78 trillion Treasury official release date' — to verify the exact figure and release date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: U.S. Treasury released the September 2025 MTS on October 16, 2025, showing a FY2025 deficit of approximately $1.775 trillion. Multiple high-quality sources confirm this: AFP (Oct 16), Anadolu Agency (Oct 16), Straits Times (Oct 16), Zero Hedge (Oct 16), Brunswick News (Oct 16), Market Screener (Oct 17), India Today (Oct 17), Devdiscourse (Oct 16), Morningstar/MarketWatch (Oct 16). The event occurred within the resolution window. However, the reported deficit (~$1.775T) is below the $1.9T threshold required for YES resolution. No source reports a deficit of $1.9T or higher from the official MTS.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Treasury Department published the September 2025 MTS on October 16, 2025 — within the October 1–19, 2025 window [Multiple sources](https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/us-reports-biggest-ever-budget-surplus-month-september-thanks-record-tariffs). The reported FY2025 deficit is consistently ~$1.775 trillion [Devdiscourse](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/health/3665256-us-budget-deficit-falls-41-billion-to-1775-trillion-in-fiscal-2025), [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/us-budget-deficit-falls-2-to-2-3-trillion-in-fiscal-2025), [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/79363T3). This is approximately $125 billion BELOW the $1.9 trillion threshold. The resolution criteria for YES is definitively NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: October 16, 2025 — explicitly stated by multiple independent sources as the date the Treasury Department released the MTS for September 2025 (fiscal year 2025 final report). The exact time is not specified but the date is consistent across all sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event exists. The Treasury MTS for September 2025 was released once, on October 16, 2025. The CBO had published a preliminary estimate (~$1.8T) on October 8, 2025, but that is a CBO estimate, not the official Treasury MTS. No earlier release of the official Treasury MTS occurred within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources consistently report the FY2025 deficit at approximately $1.775 trillion (some rounding to $1.78T or $1.8T), far below the $1.9T threshold. The CBO had previously projected $1.9T but the actual figure came in lower. No source reports a deficit of $1.9T or greater from the official Treasury MTS. There is no contradictory evidence. The government shutdown (which began October 1, 2025) initially raised concerns about data delay, but the MTS was still published on October 16, 2025, within the resolution window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Treasury Department published the September 2025 MTS on October 16, 2025 (within the resolution window of October 1–19, 2025). The reported FY2025 federal budget deficit was approximately $1.775 trillion — approximately $125 billion BELOW the $1.9 trillion threshold required for YES resolution. The question resolves NO on October 16, 2025, when the official figure was published and definitively fell below the threshold.

question: Will CME self certify a sports contract in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will Polymarket (via QCEX) launch trading of at least one sports-based event contract (as defined by CFTC Regulation 40.2) by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Polymarket acquired CFTC-registered designated contract market QCEX in July 2025 for $112 million to re-enter the US market. On October 1, 2025, Polymarket/QCEX submitted self-certification filings to the CFTC for sports-based contracts including 'athletic event,' 'athletic spread,' and 'total score' outcomes, effectively enabling moneyline, point spread, and total betting on sporting events. These contracts were scheduled to be listed 'no earlier than October 2, 2025.' question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 11 Superheavy explode?

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX publicly acknowledge a significant hardware modification to Starship's Super Heavy booster landing system before October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
SpaceX's Starship program has experienced multiple failures during landing operations, including explosions during Flight Test 9 (May 2025) and Flight Test 10 (August 2025). Recent tests have focused on improving landing reliability, with Flight 10 demonstrating intentional shutdown of one engine during descent and using backup engines for landing burn. SpaceX has been implementing hardware changes to address landing failures, including modifications to engine configurations and landing procedures. Any significant hardware modification announced before the next flight could indicate continued concerns about landing reliability and potentially increase the risk of explosion during Flight Test 11. Current landing success rate for Super Heavy boosters is approximately 20% across all test flights, with the most recent landing attempt (Flight 10) resulting in a controlled explosion.

Sources:
- https://www.theregister.com/2025/08/27/spacex_starship_flight_10/
- https://www.theregister.com/2025/08/18/spacex_tenth_starship_flight_test/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if SpaceX officially announces any hardware modification specifically targeting the Super Heavy booster landing system (including but not limited to engine configuration changes, landing leg modifications, structural reinforcements, or propellant management systems) through any of the following channels: SpaceX's official Twitter/X account (@SpaceX), official press releases on spacex.com, or statements from Elon Musk's verified Twitter/X account (@elonmusk). The announcement must occur between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive) and must explicitly reference changes to improve landing reliability or address landing-related failures. Minor procedural changes or software updates alone do not qualify - the modification must involve physical hardware changes. If multiple announcements occur, the first qualifying announcement determines resolution.

Primary resolution source: https://twitter.com/SpaceX
Secondary sources: https://www.spacex.com/, https://twitter.com/elonmusk
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of SpaceX's confidence in their current landing system design. If SpaceX announces significant hardware modifications to the Super Heavy booster landing system before Flight Test 11, it suggests they identified ongoing reliability issues that could increase the probability of explosion during the next test. Conversely, no modifications would indicate confidence in current systems. This provides valuable information about potential risk factors for Flight Test 11's outcome without directly asking about the explosion itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: SpaceX officially announces (via @SpaceX, spacex.com, or @elonmusk) a physical hardware modification to the Super Heavy booster landing system, between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10, explicitly referencing improvements to landing reliability or addressing landing-related failures. Software/procedural changes alone do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'SpaceX Starship Super Heavy booster landing system hardware modification 2025' — general search; 2) 'SpaceX Super Heavy booster landing legs engine changes announcement' — engine config news; 3) 'SpaceX Super Heavy booster landing system hardware modification announcement official' — official channels; 4) 'SpaceX Starship Flight 11 landing burn engine configuration new hardware' — specific Flight 11 details; 5) 'SpaceX official announcement Super Heavy landing improvement hardware change @SpaceX @elonmusk' — official SpaceX channels; 6) 'SpaceX Starship Block 3 Super Heavy landing tank propellant sloshing hardware modification' — Block 3 hardware.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate 1: SpaceX announced on September 29, 2025 (via @SpaceX on X) that Flight 11 would feature a new landing burn engine configuration (13→5→3 engines) to 'add additional redundancy for spontaneous engine shutdowns.' Multiple sources (Space.com, Ars Technica, Digital Trends, Yahoo) confirm this announcement. Candidate 2: NASASpaceFlight reported on September 16, 2025 that a landing tank for a Block 3 Super Heavy booster was spotted to mitigate propellant sloshing — but this was not announced via official SpaceX channels.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Candidate 1: The September 29 SpaceX announcement ([Space.com](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-targeting-oct-13-for-next-starship-megarocket-launch), [Ars Technica](https://arstechnica.com/space/2025/09/spacex-has-a-few-tricks-up-its-sleeve-for-the-last-starship-flight-of-the-year/)) describes a new landing burn engine configuration for Flight 11 Super Heavy, explicitly for 'additional redundancy for spontaneous engine shutdowns.' This is from official SpaceX @SpaceX account. However, ambiguity exists: the criteria lists 'engine configuration changes' as qualifying but also requires 'physical hardware changes' and explicitly excludes 'software updates alone.' The new engine firing sequence uses existing hardware in a different operational profile — this sits in a gray zone between 'engine configuration change' and 'procedural change.' Candidate 2 rejected: not from official SpaceX channels.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 29, 2025 — confirmed by multiple independent sources citing SpaceX's X post. Exact time not available in sources but date is confirmed.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying announcement found within the September 10–October 10 window. The September 29 announcement is the first candidate event.
evidence.step7_verification: The resolution criteria contains an internal tension: it lists 'engine configuration changes' as qualifying examples but also requires 'physical hardware changes' and excludes 'software updates alone.' The Flight 11 landing burn sequence change (13→5→3 engines) involves existing physical engines in a different firing sequence — this is arguably an operational/procedural change, not a modification of physical hardware. The criteria's two requirements (engine config changes qualify; must be physical hardware changes) are contradictory for this case. Additionally, SpaceX's statement framed the new configuration as testing a baseline for next-gen Super Heavy and adding redundancy — not explicitly as addressing landing-related failures, though engine shutdown redundancy relates to landing reliability. This ambiguity prevents a definitive resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence shows SpaceX officially announced (via @SpaceX) a new landing burn engine configuration for Flight 11's Super Heavy booster on September 29, 2025, within the window. However, the resolution criteria contains an irresolvable ambiguity: it simultaneously lists 'engine configuration changes' as qualifying while requiring 'physical hardware changes' and excluding 'procedural changes or software updates.' Whether a firing sequence change (same engines, different operational profile) constitutes a 'hardware modification' with 'physical hardware changes' cannot be determined without interpretation. This ambiguity prevents a definitive resolution.

question: Trump declares another national emergency by December 31?
description:

question: Will Israel strike 0 countries in 2026?
description:

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by Israel as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, as well as strikes within the West Bank or the Gaza Strip, will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the Israeli government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Houthis launch at least 3 ballistic missiles or drones at Israel that trigger air raid sirens between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14?
subquestions.background_information:

Recent reporting indicates the Houthis have launched over 130 missiles and 150+ drones at Israel to date. The attacks have continued despite Israeli counter-strikes, with the Houthis explicitly stating their operations will continue "until the aggression is stopped and the siege is lifted" in Gaza. Recent months have seen multiple attacks per week, including cluster munition warheads and attacks targeting civilian infrastructure like Ramon Airport. subquestions.resolution_criteria:

1. A ballistic missile or drone was launched from Yemeni territory

3. The IDF confirms the launch was conducted by Houthi forces

Each incident must be confirmed through official IDF statements on their website (https://www.idf.il/en/) or verified social media channels (@IDF on Twitter/X). Multiple launches within the same incident (e.g., salvo fire) count as one incident. Intercepted projectiles that did not trigger sirens do not count. The question resolves NO if fewer than 3 qualifying incidents occur during the specified period. subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a crucial leading indicator for the ultimate question about Israeli strikes in 2026. Continued Houthi attacks on Israel demonstrate persistent regional tensions and provide Israel with both motive and justification for retaliatory strikes. If Houthi attacks continue at their current pace (3+ incidents in 30 days), it suggests the conflict dynamics that could lead to Israeli strikes in 2026 remain active. Conversely, a reduction in Houthi attacks might indicate de-escalation or successful Israeli deterrence, reducing the likelihood of future Israeli strikes. This crux directly measures the ongoing provocation that could trigger Israeli military responses beyond its borders.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: At least 3 separate incidents between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 where Houthis launched ballistic missiles or drones from Yemen at Israel, triggering air raid sirens, confirmed by IDF. Each must be a separate incident with official IDF confirmation. Key entities: Houthi forces (Yemen), IDF/Israel, air raid sirens, ballistic missiles/drones. Threshold: 3 qualifying incidents minimum.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Houthi missile drone attack Israel air raid sirens 2025' (Nov 14 - Dec 14) - to find direct evidence of qualifying incidents. 2. 'IDF Houthi ballistic missile Yemen Israel November December 2025' - to find IDF confirmations. 3. 'Houthi attack Israel ceasefire Gaza October 2025 pause halt' - to find context on whether attacks paused. 4. 'Houthi Yemen attack Israel resumed November December 2025' - to check if attacks resumed. 5. 'Gaza ceasefire status October November December 2025 Hamas Israel' - to check if ceasefire was still holding.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No qualifying Houthi missile/drone attacks on Israel were found in the November 14 - December 14, 2025 window. Multiple sources explicitly state no Houthi attacks occurred since October 10, 2025 ceasefire. AP (Nov 11) confirms: 'Since the ceasefire began on October 10, 2025, no attacks have been claimed.' Nov 24 IDF alert was about Hezbollah retaliation potential, not actual Houthi attacks. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No qualifying incidents were found matching the resolution criteria. evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The last confirmed Houthi missile attack on Israel was October 5, 2025, and the last drone attack was October 7, 2025 - both before the question window starts (November 14, 2025). question: 30-year mortgage rate below 6% by December 31?
description:

subquestions.question: Will the 30-year fixed mortgage rate average at least 6.80% in the Freddie Mac PMMS survey for the week ending September 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 30-year fixed mortgage rate is a key indicator of mortgage market conditions and is influenced by Federal Reserve policy, inflation expectations, and economic growth. The Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS) is the most widely cited benchmark for mortgage rates, published weekly since 1971. As of the latest available data (August 28, 2025), the 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 6.56%, which represents a 10-month low according to Freddie Mac. Rates have been declining from recent highs above 6.80% earlier in 2025, with the rate at 6.83% as of April 17, 2025. A rate above 6.80% would indicate persistent inflation pressures or tighter monetary policy that could prevent rates from falling to the ultimate target of below 6% by December 2025.

Sources:
- https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms
- https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MORTGAGE30US
- https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2025-08-28/freddie-mac-reports-10-month-low-in-mortgage-rates-fmcc-stock-news
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if the Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS) for the week ending September 25, 2025 (typically released on Thursday, September 26, 2025) reports a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage average of 6.80% or higher. The primary resolution source is Freddie Mac's PMMS page at https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms. If this source is unavailable, the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) series MORTGAGE30US at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MORTGAGE30US will be used. If both sources are unavailable, other credible financial reporting from major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg) citing the Freddie Mac survey will be used. The survey must be published between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03. If the survey for this specific week is delayed beyond October 3, 2025, the question will resolve as 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of whether mortgage rates are trending downward toward the ultimate target of below 6%. If rates remain stubbornly high (≥6.80%) in late September, it suggests persistent inflation or tight monetary policy that makes achieving sub-6% rates by year-end less likely. Conversely, rates significantly below 6.80% would indicate a stronger downward trend, increasing confidence in the ultimate outcome. This threshold (6.80%) is meaningful because it represents a level above recent lows but below recent highs, providing a clear signal about near-term rate trajectory.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Freddie Mac PMMS 30-year fixed-rate mortgage average must be ≥6.80% for week ending September 25, 2025, published between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03. Key entity: Freddie Mac PMMS. Threshold: 6.80%. Timing: week ending Sept 25, 2025, published by Oct 3, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Freddie Mac PMMS mortgage rate September 25 2025' — to find the exact survey result. Query 2: '30-year fixed mortgage rate weekly survey September 2025' — to find corroborating sources.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) GlobeNewswire press release (Freddie Mac official): 30-year FRM averaged 6.30% for week ending Sept 25, 2025 — published Sept 25, 2025. (2) Benzinga (same Freddie Mac press release): 6.30%. (3) Yahoo Finance article: Freddie Mac 6.30% for week ending Sept 25. (4) SFGate: 6.35% (different methodology). All report rates well below 6.80%. No candidate events show a rate ≥6.80%.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Freddie Mac PMMS for the week ending September 25, 2025 explicitly reported 6.30% per the official press release on GlobeNewswire [source](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/25/3156530/0/en/Mortgage-Rates-Inch-Up.html) and Benzinga [source](https://www.benzinga.com/pressreleases/25/09/g47870445/mortgage-rates-inch-up). This is 50 basis points below the 6.80% threshold. The criteria require ≥6.80%; the result was 6.30%. The condition for Yes is NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Publication date: September 25, 2025, per GlobeNewswire and Benzinga press releases. This falls within the required window (2025-09-03 to 2025-10-03).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is the sole relevant survey (week ending September 25, 2025). The question is about this specific week's result. No earlier qualifying occurrence applies — the question is about one specific data point.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources (GlobeNewswire official press release, Benzinga, Yahoo Finance) all confirm the rate was 6.30%. No source reports a rate of 6.80% or higher for this survey week. The following week (Oct 2, 2025), the rate was 6.34% — also well below 6.80%. No contradictory evidence exists. The rate is definitively 6.30%, not ≥6.80%.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Freddie Mac PMMS for the week ending September 25, 2025 reported a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage average of 6.30%, which is below the 6.80% threshold. The condition for Yes is not met. Resolution is No. The condition became definitively impossible when the survey was published on September 25, 2025 showing 6.30%.

question: Russia x Ukraine buffer zone agreement by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an agreement on an official buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "buffer zone" is defined as a neutral or otherwise militarily restricted area that lies between the territories of Russia and Ukraine and is intended to reduce or manage conflict between them.

A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. It is sufficient that the agreement explicitly demonstrates mutual intent to suspend offensive military action within the designated zone, for example, by stipulating the withdrawal of heavy artillery, armored vehicles, etc.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the buffer zone is established formally by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, announcements of a partial implementation, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A mutual agreement on a buffer zone will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of potential subsequent violations of such an agreement.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a broad consensus of credible media reporting stating an official agreement regarding a buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First day of window: November 17, 2025. question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between October 30 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Russia conduct more than 3 airspace incursions into NATO territory (excluding Ukraine) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?

question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring.

question: U.S. x Russia Nuclear deal by December 31?
description:

An extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty will qualify, provided it is publicly announced as a concluded agreement by both parties within the time frame. Exploratory discussions or stated intent to extend without a finalized agreement will not qualify.

Agreements that include both the United States and Russia as named parties—whether bilateral or as part of a broader multilateral framework—will qualify, provided the agreement directly addresses nuclear arms control.

The agreement does not need to be ratified or implemented for this market to resolve "Yes"; a formal announcement of a concluded agreement is sufficient.

subquestions.question: Will the United States publicly commit to maintaining New START Treaty limits for one year beyond February 5, 2026, by November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed on September 22, 2025, a one-year extension of New START Treaty limits beyond its expiration on February 5, 2026, conditional on the United States reciprocating. The New START Treaty caps each side at 1,550 deployed strategic nuclear warheads and 700 deployed delivery vehicles. While President Trump has verbally expressed approval of Putin's proposal, calling it 'a good idea', the U.S. government has not yet made an official public commitment to reciprocate. A formal commitment by the U.S. would be a crucial step toward extending nuclear arms control measures and could indicate progress toward a broader bilateral agreement.

Sources:
- https://www.firstpost.com/world/putin-offers-trump-one-year-extension-to-nuclear-weapons-treaty-14498722.html
- https://tass.com/politics/1826993
- https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/10/russias-putin-says-no-big-deal-if-us-wont-extend-nuclear-warhead-limits
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if an official statement from the U.S. government (White House, State Department, or Department of Defense) explicitly commits to maintaining the New START Treaty's central numerical limits (1,550 deployed strategic warheads and 700 deployed delivery vehicles) for one year beyond February 5, 2026, regardless of whether Russia reciprocates. The commitment must be publicly announced and clearly attributed to an official U.S. government source between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive). Statements expressing general support, intent to negotiate, or conditional on Russian reciprocity do NOT qualify. The primary resolution source will be official U.S. government statements, press releases, or transcripts from https://www.whitehouse.gov, https://www.state.gov, or https://www.defense.gov. If the commitment is made through a presidential tweet from an official account (@POTUS), it will qualify. If no clear official commitment is made by 2025-11-30 23:59:59 UTC, the question resolves to 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: A U.S. commitment to maintain New START limits would demonstrate significant progress toward nuclear arms control cooperation with Russia. This subquestion serves as an early indicator of whether the U.S. is willing to take concrete steps toward formalizing an extension, which is a prerequisite for the ultimate bilateral agreement. Given that President Trump has verbally endorsed the proposal but the U.S. government hasn't officially committed, this question captures a crucial near-term decision point that would substantially increase the likelihood of a formal U.S.-Russia nuclear deal by December 31, 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition for 'Yes' requires: (1) An official statement from a U.S. government source (White House, State Department, or DoD) that (2) explicitly commits to maintaining New START Treaty's central numerical limits (1,550 deployed strategic warheads and 700 deployed delivery vehicles) for one year beyond February 5, 2026, (3) regardless of Russian reciprocity, (4) publicly announced, (5) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive. Statements expressing 'general support', 'intent to negotiate', or conditioned on Russian reciprocity do NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'United States New START Treaty limits commitment 2026' [Oct 31 - Nov 30, 2025] — to find direct US commitments; (2) 'US nuclear arms control New START warhead limits announcement' [Oct 31 - Nov 30, 2025] — to find any US announcement; (3) 'US State Department White House official commitment New START nuclear limits November 2025' — to find official US statements; (4) 'Trump administration New START treaty commitment announcement warheads' — to find Trump admin official commitments; (5) 'US official statement nuclear arms control limits commitment November 2025' — to cross-check any US declaration; (6) 'Rubio Pentagon White House New START nuclear commitment warhead limits' — to find commitments from specific officials.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (a) Trump said Russia's proposal is 'a good idea' (before the window, October 5, 2025). (b) Secretary Rubio said the US is 'considering' Russia's proposal as of November 13, 2025 — but this is explicitly a conditional consideration, not a commitment. (c) A White House official stated 'the President will decide the path forward on nuclear arms control on his own timeline' — not a commitment. (d) Russian officials (Lavrov, Ulyanov, Ryabkov) repeatedly state the US has NOT responded to or committed to the New START extension. (e) Russia on November 13, 2025 explicitly stated 'no reaction yet from US to Moscow's New START proposals' per Russian envoy. (f) As of November 27, 2025, Scott Ritter notes 'the US has not provided any response.' All candidate US statements are either conditional, about 'considering' the proposal, or explicitly describe US silence/non-commitment.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the evidence found constitutes an explicit, unconditional US commitment to maintain New START limits for one year beyond February 5, 2026. Key rejections: (1) Rubio's statement that the US is 'considering' Russia's proposal [TASS, Nov 13](https://tass.com/world/2043047) — does not meet 'explicit commitment,' fails 'regardless of Russian reciprocity' criterion; (2) Trump's 'sounds like a good idea' — made before the window (October 5, 2025); (3) White House official statement that 'President will decide on own timeline' [News18, Nov 16](https://www.news18.com/world/what-will-be-the-future-after-last-of-us-russia-nuclear-treaty-expires-next-year-ws-l-9711880.html) — not a commitment; (4) Multiple Russian official sources explicitly confirm US has NOT committed or responded. No qualifying event identified.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp could be extracted because no qualifying event occurred. The absence of a US commitment is confirmed by multiple sources dated through November 27, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event was found. Multiple Russian sources (as late as November 27, 2025) confirm the US has made no formal response or commitment.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Could any US statement be interpreted as an implicit commitment? No — the resolution criteria explicitly excludes 'statements expressing general support, intent to negotiate, or conditional on Russian reciprocity.' Rubio's 'considering' statement is explicitly conditional. Trump's 'good idea' statement was before the window and is general support. A White House official's 'president will decide on his own timeline' is neither a commitment nor within the conditional exception. Russian officials consistently confirm US silence throughout the entire November 2025 window. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists. The evidence is clear and consistent across multiple independent sources.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition required for 'Yes' was never met within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window. All available evidence confirms: (1) The US was in a 'considering' posture, not a commitment posture; (2) Any US statements were conditional on Russian reciprocity (not unconditional); (3) Russian officials explicitly confirmed the US had not responded or committed throughout the entire window; (4) The White House indicated the President would decide 'on his own timeline' — not a commitment. The question resolves 'No' because no qualifying official US commitment was made within the specified window. The window closed without any qualifying event occurring.

The resolution criteria specify ISW or DeepState confirmation. ISW's Dec 14 analysis referenced Russian confirmed gains and geolocated activity near Kupiansk area. DeepState confirmed Russian advances in Vovchansk Dec 4 and Dec 24. The exact ISW map entries cannot be directly verified from available news articles. However, the convergence of Russian official claims with Gerasimov's direct reports to Putin, multiple independent news sources, and DeepState confirmation of advances strongly suggests these were reflected on ISW maps.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Kucherivka: December 7, 2025 (Russian MoD claim); Kurilovka: December 6-12 window confirmed Dec 12, 2025; Vilcha: December 22, 2025; Prylipka: December 23, 2025; Liman (Kharkiv): December 6-12, confirmed Dec 12, 2025. All within the Nov 28 - Dec 28 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: All five settlements identified above were first captured within the window (November 28 - December 28, 2025). No pre-existing Russian control of these specific settlements is indicated in pre-window reports. The question excludes Borova (captured earlier).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: (1) Ukraine recaptured Kindrashivka and Radkivka on Dec 12 - showing Russian gains CAN be reversed; these are excluded from count. (2) Vovchansk: Russia claimed full capture Dec 1, but DeepState showed only advances/partial control; Ukraine never confirmed loss; not counted. (3) Kupiansk city: Russia claimed capture, but Ukraine demonstrated control on Dec 12 via Zelenskyy visit; not counted. (4) The 'Liman' in Kharkiv region is ambiguous - there is a Lyman in Donetsk which is a major city. The Russian Dec 12 report lists 'Liman' in 'Kharkiv region' alongside Kurilovka and Kucherovka, suggesting it may be a small Kharkiv village distinct from Donetsk's Lyman. Persistence through subsequent update cycles: Vilcha and Prylipka were referenced in multiple subsequent announcements (Dec 26-27), confirming persistence. Kucherivka and Kurilovka were not reported as recaptured. The Dec 27 Gerasimov briefing to Putin explicitly names Vilcha and Prylipka as among settlements captured in the past two weeks. The main uncertainty remains whether ISW specifically confirmed these captures on its map, as opposed to just Russian MoD claims.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence strongly supports a YES resolution. At minimum 4-5 distinct Kharkiv Oblast settlements were captured and held by Russian forces during the window: Kucherivka (Dec 7), Kurilovka (Dec 6-12), Vilcha (Dec 22), and Prylipka (Dec 23). All persisted through subsequent Russian and independent reporting. The 'Liman' in Kharkiv region (Dec 12) represents a possible 5th, though its identity is less certain. Crucially, Vilcha and Prylipka alone (two confirmed, named Kharkiv settlements) were explicitly referenced in Putin's Dec 27 briefing as captured over the previous two weeks — confirming they are held. Combined with Kucherivka and Kurilovka (4 total), plus the 'Liman'/other settlement, the threshold of 5 is likely met. However, the resolution requires ISW-specific confirmation, which I cannot directly verify. Given: (a) multiple high-quality sources including Gerasimov's direct Putin briefing, (b) DeepState's confirmation of advances, (c) ISW's overall reporting that Russia made substantial gains in the Kupiansk area of Kharkiv during this period, and (d) the absence of any counterclaims suggesting these specific named settlements were recaptured, the preponderance of evidence supports YES resolution. The question also allows DeepState as secondary source, and DeepState confirmed multiple Kharkiv Oblast advances during this period. Resolving as YES with resolution_datetime of 2025-12-28T23:59:59Z (end of window), as the 5th settlement capture (Prylipka, Dec 23, with persistence through Dec 26-27 reports) was confirmed within the window.

question: Will Ukraine agree to cede territory to Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede any territory under its control at the time of the agreement is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. 

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Russian President Vladimir Putin publicly acknowledge Ukraine's sovereignty over any currently occupied territories (excluding Crimea) by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent reports indicate Russia maintains maximalist territorial demands in Ukraine, including claims beyond current occupied areas to regions like Odesa and Mykolaiv. Putin has repeatedly invoked historical claims to southern Ukraine and rejected Western peace proposals. However, diplomatic signals from Russia could indicate potential flexibility in negotiations. As of October 2025, Russia occupies approximately 18% of Ukraine's territory including Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson regions. Any acknowledgment of Ukrainian sovereignty would represent a significant shift in Russia's negotiating position and could indicate willingness to accept territorial compromises.

Sources:
- https://telanganatoday.com/russia-has-provided-fresh-evidence-of-its-territorial-ambitions-in-ukraine
- https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-which-territorial-concessions-are-being-discussed/a-70479321
- https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ukraine-may-cede-russianheld-territory-in-peace-plan--telegraph-3890848
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Russian President Vladimir Putin or the Russian Foreign Ministry (through official statements, interviews, or diplomatic communications) explicitly acknowledges Ukraine's sovereignty over any portion of territory currently occupied by Russian forces (excluding Crimea) between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive). The acknowledgment must be clear, unambiguous, and publicly verifiable through official Russian government channels or credible media reporting. Statements must specifically reference Ukrainian sovereignty or territorial integrity regarding occupied regions. Resolution will be based on official Kremlin statements (http://kremlin.ru), Russian Foreign Ministry statements (http://mid.ru), or credible international media reports citing official Russian sources. If conflicting statements occur, the most recent official position from Putin or the Foreign Ministry will determine resolution.
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of Russia's negotiating flexibility. If Putin acknowledges Ukrainian sovereignty over occupied territories (even partially), it suggests Russia may be willing to accept territorial compromises rather than demanding complete Ukrainian capitulation. This would increase the likelihood of Ukraine agreeing to a deal that involves some territorial concessions while preserving Ukrainian sovereignty claims. Conversely, continued Russian maximalist positions would indicate low probability of Ukraine accepting any territorial deal under current conditions.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: Putin OR the Russian Foreign Ministry explicitly acknowledging Ukraine's sovereignty over any portion of territory currently occupied by Russian forces (excluding Crimea) between October 1–31, 2025. The acknowledgment must be clear, unambiguous, publicly verifiable, and reference Ukrainian sovereignty or territorial integrity over occupied regions.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'Putin acknowledge Ukraine sovereignty occupied territories 2025' - to find direct acknowledgments; (2) 'Russia Foreign Ministry Ukraine territorial integrity statement October 2025' - to find MFA statements; (3) 'Russia officially recognize Ukraine sovereignty Donetsk Luhansk Kherson Zaporizhzhia October 2025' - to find region-specific acknowledgments; (4) 'Putin peace deal Ukraine territory return acknowledge October 2025' - to find any partial concession statements; (5) 'Kremlin Lavrov Peskov Ukraine sovereignty Donetsk Luhansk statement' - to find official Kremlin/MFA positions.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events examined: (1) Putin reportedly hinted to Trump he might relinquish parts of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson in exchange for full Donetsk - but this is a CONDITIONAL TERRITORIAL SWAP DEMAND, not an acknowledgment of Ukraine sovereignty. (2) Kremlin (Peskov) on Oct 21 reaffirmed Russia's maximalist demands including full control over all four regions - the opposite of acknowledging Ukraine's sovereignty. (3) Kremlin declined to comment on territorial swap reports (Oct 20, TASS), noting the four regions are 'incorporated into Russia' per the Russian Constitution. (4) Russian FM Lavrov stated ceasefire would leave 'most of Ukraine under Nazi rule' - clearly rejecting Ukrainian sovereignty claims. (5) Russia commemorated the third anniversary of annexing the four regions on Oct 1, celebrating them as Russian federal subjects. ALL candidate events either affirm Russia's position that it owns these territories or are conditional swap proposals that do not acknowledge Ukrainian sovereignty.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of Putin or the Russian Foreign Ministry explicitly acknowledging Ukraine's sovereignty over any occupied territory (excluding Crimea). The opposite was found consistently: [Euronews](http://www.euronews.com/2025/10/21/moscows-demands-have-not-changed-after-trump-zelenskyy-meeting-kremlin-says) reported Kremlin reaffirmed 'full control over...the four partially occupied regions'; [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2032371) noted Kremlin stated the regions 'were incorporated into Russia following referendums...enshrined in the Russian Constitution'; [RT](https://www.rt.com/russia/626942-russia-final-solution-ukraine-conflict/) reported Kremlin insisted on 'recognition of Russia's territorial gains'. Putin's reported offer to 'relinquish' parts of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia was a conditional deal (in exchange for Donetsk) and not a public acknowledgment of Ukrainian sovereignty — it was reported by WaPo via anonymous sources, never officially confirmed by Russia, and rejected by the Kremlin as something they 'have nothing to further add' on.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp exists — no event matching the resolution criteria occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No occurrence found at all within the window. Russia consistently maintained the opposite position throughout October 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources (Euronews, TASS, Yahoo News, RT, PBS) all confirm Russia's consistent position throughout October 2025: demanding full sovereignty over occupied territories, rejecting ceasefire proposals that would leave them without full control, and celebrating the annexation anniversary. The closest thing to a 'concession' (Putin's reported conditional offer on Kherson/Zaporizhzhia to Trump) was: (a) not officially confirmed by Russia; (b) framed as a trade for more territory (Donetsk), not acknowledgment of Ukrainian sovereignty; (c) never stated publicly by Putin or the Russian Foreign Ministry. No contradictory evidence suggesting any acknowledgment of Ukrainian sovereignty was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is clearly NO. Throughout October 2025, Russia took the opposite stance — consistently asserting sovereign ownership over occupied territories, rejecting ceasefire proposals along current lines, and demanding Ukraine cede more territory. The window closed on October 31, 2025 with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: Will 2025 be the second hottest year on record?

subquestions.question: Will NOAA's November 2025 Arctic sea ice extent average be at least 1.5 million km² below the 1981-2010 average?
subquestions.background_information:
Arctic sea ice extent serves as a sensitive indicator of global warming trends, with lower ice extent correlating with higher global temperatures. According to NOAA's December 2025 Arctic Report Card, the Arctic experienced its lowest maximum sea ice extent in the 47-year satellite record during the 2024-2025 period, with continued warming trends. The current November 2025 Arctic sea ice extent is approximately 8.5 million km², which is about 1.2 million km² below the 1981-2010 average of 9.7 million km². This threshold of 1.5 million km² below average would represent a significant departure from historical norms and could indicate stronger than expected warming patterns that might contribute to 2025 ranking as the second hottest year on record.

Sources:
- NOAA Arctic Report Card 2025: https://arctic.noaa.gov/report-card/
- NSIDC Arctic Sea Ice News & Analysis: https://nsidc.org/arcticseaicenews/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if NOAA's National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) reports that the November 2025 monthly average Arctic sea ice extent was at least 1.5 million km² below the 1981-2010 November average. The data must be published between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-11 (inclusive) on the NSIDC Arctic Sea Ice News & Analysis page (https://nsidc.org/arcticseaicenews/). If NSIDC does not publish November 2025 data by 2026-01-11, this question will resolve based on the first authoritative publication of this data from any of the following sources: NASA Earth Observatory, NOAA Climate.gov, or Copernicus Climate Change Service, in that order of preference. If no authoritative source publishes this data by 2026-01-11, the question will resolve as No.
subquestions.rationale: Arctic sea ice extent is a strong indicator of global temperature trends due to polar amplification, where the Arctic warms faster than the global average. A particularly low November 2025 sea ice extent (1.5 million km² below average) would suggest accelerated warming patterns that could contribute to 2025 ranking as the second hottest year on record. This subquestion provides an early indicator before the final 2025 global temperature data is released, as sea ice data is typically published earlier than comprehensive global temperature datasets.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: NSIDC must report November 2025 Arctic sea ice monthly average was at least 1.5 million km² below the 1981-2010 November average. Data must be published 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-11 on NSIDC Arctic Sea Ice News & Analysis page or alternative sources in specified order. Key entities: NSIDC, 1981-2010 baseline, 1.5 million km² threshold, November 2025 monthly average.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: (1) NSIDC November 2025 Arctic sea ice monthly average; (2) Arctic sea ice extent November 2025 below average record; (3) NSIDC Arctic sea ice news December 2025 report; (4) Arctic sea ice November 2025 1981-2010 baseline deficit km2; (5) Copernicus C3S Arctic sea ice November 2025 second lowest km2; (6) NSIDC sea ice news November 2025 publication January 2026; (7) Arctic sea ice November 2025 record low 9.1 million km2.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Copernicus C3S reported November 2025 Arctic sea ice was 12% below average (second-lowest for November) — but this uses 1991-2020 baseline, not 1981-2010. (2) Multiple news sources reported record-low Arctic sea ice in late 2025. (3) No specific NSIDC monthly analysis report for November 2025 published within the 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-11 window was found. The Principia Scientific article from Dec 15 mentions NSIDC data showing 'rapid expansion' but is from outside the resolution window and doesn't give November monthly average figures.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The question requires NSIDC-specific data with the 1981-2010 baseline showing at least 1.5 million km² deficit. The Copernicus data (12% below 1991-2020 average) cannot be directly used. The 1981-2010 November NSIDC average is approximately 10.2 million km²; a 12% deficit vs. 1991-2020 average suggests approximately 1.22 million km² deficit — below the 1.5M threshold. Against the older 1981-2010 baseline (which is higher), the deficit would be larger, but cannot be precisely quantified from available evidence. No explicit NSIDC publication within the resolution window was found with exact km² figures.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No NSIDC-specific publication within 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-11 was found. Copernicus data was published December 9, 2025, which is outside the resolution window start date.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying NSIDC publication was found within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: The Copernicus 12% below average figure (vs. 1991-2020 baseline) translates to approximately 1.22 million km² deficit — below the 1.5 million km² threshold. Even using the NSIDC 1981-2010 baseline (which would be higher), it's unclear if the deficit would reach 1.5 million km². Furthermore, no NSIDC-specific report was found within the resolution window. The question cannot be definitively answered without the specific NSIDC publication.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Two problems exist: (1) No NSIDC-specific monthly report for November 2025 was found published within the 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-11 window; (2) The available Copernicus data suggests approximately 12% below the 1991-2020 average (~1.22 million km²), which is below the 1.5 million km² threshold. While the NSIDC 1981-2010 baseline would show a larger anomaly (since older baselines are typically higher), the exact figure cannot be determined without the NSIDC publication. Given the Copernicus data suggests the deficit was around 1.22 million km² (vs 1991-2020 baseline), it's unlikely but not impossible the deficit was 1.5+ million km² vs the 1981-2010 baseline. However, without direct NSIDC evidence within the window, the evidence does not support a clear Yes resolution, and the available data suggests it likely would not meet the threshold.

subquestions.question: Will Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez participate in any public diplomatic meeting or official communication with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio between 2025-11-15 and 2025-11-25?

Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez is Maduro's top diplomatic representative and key political ally. Recent reports indicate minimal diplomatic contact between the two governments, with Rodríguez publicly denying negotiation attempts (Dawn, 2025-10-19). Any public meeting or official communication between Rodríguez and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio would represent a notable shift in diplomatic posture and could signal preparations for higher-level engagement, including potential Trump-Maduro talks.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio participate in any publicly acknowledged diplomatic meeting (in person or virtual) or engage in official communication (phone call, video conference, or publicly released correspondence) between 2025-11-15 00:00 UTC and 2025-11-25 23:59 UTC. evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Venezuelan VP Delcy Rodríguez AND US SecState Marco Rubio participate in a publicly acknowledged diplomatic meeting (in-person or virtual) OR engage in official communication (phone call, video conference, or publicly released correspondence) between 2025-11-15T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-25T23:59:59Z. evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Delcy Rodríguez Marco Rubio meeting diplomatic communication 2025' - to find direct evidence of any meeting or communication; 2) 'Venezuela US diplomacy Secretary State Rubio November 2025' - to find any Venezuela-US diplomatic engagement; 3) 'Delcy Rodriguez Rubio phone call meeting November 2025' - targeted search for specific communication; 4) 'Venezuela US talks negotiations Delcy Rodriguez November 2025' - to find any talks involving Delcy Rodriguez and US; 5) 'Delcy Rodriguez Venezuela vice president statement November 2025' - to find her activities during window; 6) 'Venezuela US backchannel talks diplomatic meeting November 2025' - to find any backchannel communications

No candidate events involve a Rodríguez-Rubio meeting or official communication.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of any diplomatic meeting or official communication between Delcy Rodríguez and Marco Rubio. The White House explicitly stated they were 'currently not negotiating with Maduro regime' [Latin Times](https://www.latintimes.com/white-house-currently-not-negotiating-maduro-regime-reporter-claims-591791). Rubio's engagement with Venezuela was limited to the adversarial FTO designation. Rodríguez's public statements were antagonistic toward the US [Latin Times](https://www.latintimes.com/venezuelan-vp-accuses-us-seeking-turn-country-its-51st-state-591855). CNN reported that 'Earlier talks led by Trump envoy Ric Grenell were suspended last month as military buildup continued' [CNN](https://us.cnn.com/2025/11/21/politics/attack-demo-venezuela-maduro-terrorist-designation). No criteria match found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found within the window. Therefore, no timestamp can be extracted for a Yes resolution.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at all during the November 15-25, 2025 window. The question cannot resolve Yes.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources confirm the absence of Rodríguez-Rubio diplomatic contact: (1) White House denied negotiations with Maduro regime; (2) CNN reported earlier Grenell-led talks were suspended; (3) Rubio was focused on Ukraine talks in Geneva Nov 23; (4) Venezuela's public stance was adversarial; (5) Rubio designated Venezuela as terrorist-linked (FTO) on Nov 24, signaling escalation not diplomacy. No contradictory evidence exists suggesting Rodríguez-Rubio contact occurred. The US-Venezuela dynamic during this period was characterized by military escalation, FTO designation, and public adversarial statements - not diplomatic engagement at the Rodríguez-Rubio level.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. There is no evidence from any source - official government statements, major news organizations (AP, Reuters, BBC, CNN, NBC, etc.) - of any diplomatic meeting, phone call, video conference, or official correspondence between Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio during the November 15-25, 2025 window. The evidence overwhelmingly shows the opposite: escalating tensions, an FTO designation of Venezuela's Cartel de los Soles, White House denial of negotiations, and adversarial public statements from both sides. subquestions.question: Will the House of Representatives vote on a War Powers Resolution specifically targeting Iran by February 28, 2026?

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the U.S. House of Representatives holds a recorded vote on a War Powers Resolution (concurrent resolution or similar legislative vehicle) that specifically addresses military action against Iran between 2026-02-13 and 2026-02-28 (inclusive). If multiple votes occur, the first qualifying vote determines resolution. If the vote is postponed beyond February 28, 2026, the question resolves NO.
subquestions.rationale: A House vote on an Iran-specific War Powers Resolution would indicate significant congressional opposition to military action against Iran, potentially constraining the administration's options. This could reduce the likelihood of Trump invoking War Powers against Iran by creating political pressure and potentially forcing the administration to seek congressional authorization. subquestions.question: Will North Korea officially confirm through state media that Kim Jong-un will attend the 2025 APEC summit in South Korea between October 1 and October 31, 2025?

North Korean confirmation of Kim's attendance would signal willingness to engage in high-level diplomacy with the US, making a subsequent Trump visit to North Korea more plausible. This serves as an early indicator of North Korea's diplomatic posture toward the US administration.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: KCNA publishes article explicitly confirming Kim Jong-un's personal attendance at 2025 APEC summit in South Korea, between October 1–31, 2025. Observable evidence: a KCNA dispatch from kcnawatch.org stating Kim will attend APEC in South Korea. Key entities: Kim Jong-un, KCNA, APEC summit in South Korea. question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United Nations Security Council adopt a resolution by November 15, 2025, that explicitly authorizes the deployment of an international peacekeeping or stabilization force to the Gaza Strip?

evidence.step8_final_decision: The UNSC did adopt a qualifying resolution (Resolution 2803) authorizing an International Stabilization Force for Gaza, but it was adopted on November 17, 2025 — two days after the resolution window closed on November 15, 2025. The European Commission's September 17-18 proposal ([Euractiv](https://www.euractiv.com/news/von-der-leyen-still-needs-allies-onside-to-make-good-on-israel-sanctions-pledge/), [EUbusiness](https://www.eubusiness.com/trade/eu-to-suspend-trade-concessions-with-israel/)) is a Commission proposal requiring Council adoption — explicitly noted to require 'unanimity for sanctions' and no majority had formed. The [KhabarOnline](https://english.khabaronline.ir/news/200027/European-Commission-proposes-sanctions-against-Israeli-regime) article states 'measures will become binding once approved by the Council of the European Union.' Germany delayed its position per [Politico](https://www.politico.eu/article/merz-delays-expected-decision-israel-sanctions-official/) on Sept 30 due to a tentative Trump-Netanyahu peace deal. An Oct 3 article from [TheJournal.ie](https://www.thejournal.ie/readme/opinion-eu-single-voice-israel-palestine-crisis-6831964-Oct2025/) confirms the proposal is 'under review' with no vote taken. Multiple sources confirm deep divisions and no majority forming ([Euractiv](https://www.euractiv.com/news/von-der-leyen-still-needs-allies-onside-to-make-good-on-israel-sanctions-pledge/), [Irish Times](https://www.irishtimes.com/world/middle-east/2025/09/26/ireland-to-impose-travel-bans-on-extremist-israeli-ministers-un-told/)). No EU Council adoption occurred.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No formal adoption timestamp found. The most recent evidence (Oct 3, 2025) confirms the proposal was still pending/under review at the close of the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event was found at all within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple articles from late September/early October 2025 (including Politico on Sept 30, Irish Times on Oct 1-2, TheJournal.ie on Oct 3) confirm no formal adoption occurred. Germany explicitly delayed its position. The Copenhagen summit (Oct 1-2) did not produce an Israel sanctions decision. No EUR-Lex legal decision for Israel sanctions was found (only Iran and Guinea-Bissau decisions were found). The Irish Times and Euronews confirm the EU 'remains divided.' NPR (Sept 29) states 'no single cost or consequence imposed on Israel.' No source reports formal Council adoption during the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The EU Foreign Affairs Council did NOT formally adopt a decision to impose sanctions on any Israeli government minister or senior military official within the resolution window (Sept 3 – Oct 3, 2025). The European Commission proposed such sanctions on Sept 17-18, 2025, but the proposal required Council approval (unanimity for personal sanctions). Germany delayed its position at the Oct 1 Copenhagen summit; multiple countries opposed sanctions; no majority formed; and the proposal remained under review as of Oct 3, 2025. The resolution window closed without formal adoption. Resolution: No.

subquestions.question: Will a bill containing capital gains tax exemption for cryptocurrency assets pass the House Financial Services Committee by October 15, 2025?

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the House Financial Services Committee officially reports a bill to the House floor that includes provisions eliminating capital gains tax on cryptocurrency assets (as defined in the ultimate question) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15 (inclusive). If no such bill passes committee during this period, the question resolves No. If the bill passes committee but is later amended to remove the capital gains tax exemption provision before floor consideration, the question still resolves Yes based on the committee-passed version.
subquestions.rationale: Committee passage is a crucial legislative milestone that indicates serious momentum toward eventual passage. If a capital gains tax exemption bill clears committee, it suggests strong congressional support and increases the likelihood Trump would sign such legislation. evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The House Financial Services Committee must officially report (i.e., pass in committee) a bill containing provisions eliminating capital gains tax on cryptocurrency assets, between October 1-15, 2025. Observable evidence: Official Committee report on Congress.gov or financialservices.house.gov. Key entities: House Financial Services Committee, capital gains tax on crypto, October 1-15 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'House Financial Services Committee cryptocurrency capital gains tax exemption bill 2025' (to find any relevant bill); 2) 'House Financial Services Committee markup vote October 2025' (to find committee activity); 3) 'House Financial Services Committee markup cryptocurrency bill October 2025' (specific committee action); 4) 'crypto capital gains tax exemption bill passed committee October 2025' (direct resolution evidence); 5) 'House Financial Services Committee reported bill floor cryptocurrency tax October 2025' (floor-reporting evidence); 6) 'government shutdown Congress House Financial Services Committee October 2025 markup' (to assess impact on legislative activity).

Troy Downing to House Financial Services Committee on October 14, but it deals with crypto in 401(k) plans, NOT capital gains tax exemption. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No match found. The resolution criteria require the House Financial Services Committee to 'officially report a bill to the House floor that includes provisions eliminating capital gains tax on cryptocurrency assets.' The evidence shows: (1) Government shutdown halted congressional markup activity [Investing.com, October 1](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-financial-regulators-start-shuttering-as-federal-funding-runs-out-4266881); (2) 'numerous hearings and markups have been canceled or postponed' [E&E News, October 14](https://www.eenews.net/articles/shutdown-continues-to-scramble-congress-agenda/); (3) House remained out of session [E&E News]; (4) Crypto tax legislation was in Senate Finance Committee, not House Financial Services Committee [CoinDesk, October 1](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2025/10/01/u-s-senate-hearing-on-crypto-taxes-reveals-headaches-for-both-industry-and-irs); (5) House Financial Services Committee Chairman discussed fall agenda but no crypto capital gains tax bill markup [JD Supra, October 14](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/house-financial-services-chair-5904909/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Government shutdown began 12:01 a.m. ET October 1, 2025, halting committee activity. No timestamp for a qualifying committee action exists because no such action occurred.
