question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by December 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla receive approval from the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to operate an autonomous vehicle pilot program without a safety driver by September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Tesla's robotaxi ambitions face significant regulatory hurdles, particularly in California where the CPUC governs autonomous vehicle deployment. Recent news indicates Tesla attempted to launch a human-monitored service in San Francisco but was rebuffed by the CPUC, which stated Tesla lacks the required permit for autonomous vehicle operations even with a safety driver (Business Insider, Planetizen). The CPUC's Autonomous Vehicle Passenger Service pilot program allows companies to test autonomous vehicles without a driver under specific conditions, but Tesla has not yet obtained this permit. Regulatory approval in California is crucial for Tesla's nationwide robotaxi strategy, as California represents a major market and its regulations often set precedents for other states. Currently, Tesla does not appear on the CPUC's list of permitted autonomous vehicle deployment companies (CPUC AV Permits).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Tesla appears on the California Public Utilities Commission's official list of companies permitted to deploy autonomous vehicles without a driver in a passenger service pilot program by September 8, 2025, 11:59 PM PT. The resolution will be determined using the CPUC's official Autonomous Vehicle Permits webpage (https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/industries-and-topics/electrical-energy/electric-vehicles/autonomous-vehicle-permits). If Tesla is listed under 'Permitted Autonomous Vehicle Deployment - Drivered' or 'Permitted Autonomous Vehicle Deployment - Driverless' sections with an active permit status, this resolves YES. If Tesla remains absent from these lists or is only listed under 'Permitted Autonomous Vehicle Testing' categories, this resolves NO. Any permit approval must be publicly visible on the CPUC website before the deadline. If the CPUC website becomes unavailable or stops updating during the resolution period, resolution will be based on the last available archived version from web.archive.org.
subquestions.rationale: Regulatory approval is a critical prerequisite for Tesla's driverless robotaxi ambitions. The CPUC's rejection of Tesla's current approach suggests significant regulatory barriers. If Tesla cannot obtain approval in California - a state with relatively progressive AV regulations - by early September, it indicates serious challenges in meeting regulatory requirements nationwide. This would substantially decrease the probability of a successful public driverless launch by year-end, as regulatory processes typically take months and Tesla would need to demonstrate robust safety performance to gain approval.

question: Will there be no US government shutdown by January 31 and will the Republican Party win the House in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of whether there will be another US government shutdown by January 31 (https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-another-us-government-shutdown-by-january-31?) and according to which party will win the House in 2026 (https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026?).

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Will there be another US government shutdown by January 31?
This market will resolve according to whether the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces another federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown.

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

2. Which party will win the House in 2026?
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

subquestions.question: Will the House of Representatives vote on and pass at least one of the nine remaining FY2026 appropriations bills by January 27, 2026?
subquestions.background_information: As of January 9, 2026, Congress faces a January 30 deadline to pass nine remaining appropriations bills to avoid a partial government shutdown. House and Senate appropriators have reached bipartisan agreements on top-line spending levels, and a $174 billion minibus package covering Commerce, Justice, Energy, Water, Interior, and EPA has been unveiled. However, passage remains uncertain due to internal Republican divisions and potential Democratic holds. The House Rules Committee is scheduled to meet on January 7, 2026, with a final House vote possible on January 9. Progress on these bills is a critical indicator of whether Congress can avoid another shutdown, as successful passage would demonstrate legislative momentum and bipartisan cooperation. Sources: https://www.oann.com/newsroom/congress-debuts-174b-spending-package-as-jan-30-govt-shutdown-deadline-looms/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the House of Representatives votes on and passes at least one of the nine remaining FY2026 appropriations bills (as listed by the House Appropriations Committee) between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-27 (inclusive). Passage is defined as a majority of voting members voting in favor. The resolution will be determined using the official House vote records from Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/roll-call-votes). If no vote occurs or if the vote fails, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is highly relevant to the ultimate question because successful passage of appropriations bills is a direct indicator of Congress's ability to fund the government and avoid a shutdown. If the House cannot pass any bills by January 27, it suggests significant legislative gridlock, increasing the likelihood of a shutdown. Additionally, Republican success in passing bills could signal party cohesion and effectiveness, which may correlate with their chances of retaining the House in 2026. Conversely, failure might indicate internal divisions that could harm their electoral prospects.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The House of Representatives must vote on AND pass (majority voting in favor) at least one of the nine remaining FY2026 appropriations bills between January 9, 2026 and January 27, 2026 (inclusive). The 'nine remaining' bills are those not already enacted before January 9, 2026. Key entities: U.S. House of Representatives; FY2026 appropriations bills; House Appropriations Committee list. The three bills already enacted before the window were: Agriculture, Military Construction/Veterans Affairs, and Legislative Branch (signed November 2025). Observable evidence: official vote records from Congress.gov showing passage of at least one appropriations bill.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'House of Representatives FY2026 appropriations bills vote January 2026' — to find any House votes on appropriations bills in the window. 2. 'House vote appropriations bill passed 2026 spending' — same purpose, different phrasing. 3. 'House vote FY2026 appropriations bill January 9 2026 Energy Interior Commerce' — to find the specific earliest vote in window. 4. 'House appropriations bills remaining nine FY2026 list January 2026' — to identify which bills counted as 'nine remaining.' 5. 'January 8 OR January 9 House vote appropriations 397-28 2026 exact date' — to resolve date discrepancy.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) House vote 397-28 on three-bill package (Commerce/Justice/Science, Energy/Water, Interior/Environment) — multiple sources say January 8, 2026 (The Hill, Washington Times, CBS News), while others say January 9, 2026 (E&E News, News 9, Feedstuffs). (2) House vote 341-79 on two-bill package (State/Treasury) on January 14, 2026 — multiple concordant sources. (3) House votes on DHS (220-207) and Defense/Labor-HHS/Transportation package (341-88) on January 23, 2026 — multiple concordant sources. Event (1) has a date dispute near the window boundary but events (2) and (3) are clearly within the window. None of these events require inference — all are explicitly stated.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The January 14, 2026 vote (341-79) on State Department/National Security and Treasury/Financial Services bills is within the window. [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5689765-house-passes-two-bill-package-to-fund-treasury-state-departments/) explicitly states 'The U.S. House of Representatives passed a bipartisan two-bill spending package on January 14, 2026, with a 341-79 vote.' The [Washington Times](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/jan/14/house-passes-spending-bill-foreign-aid-financial-services/) confirms this. These are FY2026 appropriations bills from among the nine remaining. The vote was 341-79, clearly a majority in favor. The January 23, 2026 votes are similarly well-documented: [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-house-passes-final-appropriations-bills/3808417) explicitly confirms the House passed four bills on January 23, 2026. Additionally, the three-bill vote possibly on January 9, 2026 (within window) or January 8, 2026 (outside window) adds possible first-occurrence complexity, but the January 14 vote is unambiguous.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The most reliable earliest timestamp within the window is January 14, 2026 for the 341-79 vote on Treasury/State appropriations bills — reported consistently by multiple high-quality sources (The Hill, Washington Times, RedState, Washington Examiner). The date dispute centers on whether the first appropriations vote was January 8 or January 9, but in any case the January 14 vote is clearly within the window and uncontested.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: If the three-bill vote (397-28) occurred on January 9 rather than January 8, that would be the earliest qualifying event (January 9, 2026). However, there is conflicting evidence: The Hill, Washington Times, CBS News, and Arkansas Advocate place the vote on Thursday January 8, 2026 (indeed January 8, 2026 was a Thursday), while E&E News, News 9, and Feedstuffs report it on January 9, 2026. Because there is conflicting evidence on the exact date of that vote, and since the window starts January 9, I cannot definitively confirm January 9 as the first occurrence. However, this does NOT affect resolution — the January 14, 2026 vote is unambiguous and within the window, as are the January 23 votes.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: No source contradicts the January 14 vote occurring on that date or disputes it as a passage of FY2026 appropriations bills. All sources agree the Treasury and State Department spending bills passed the House 341-79 on January 14, 2026. These bills were part of the nine remaining FY2026 appropriations bills (the nine not yet enacted before January 9). The Washington Times explicitly states: 'The U.S. House of Representatives passed a $77 billion two-bill spending package on January 14, 2026, funding foreign aid and financial services agencies.' The RedState article confirms 'three of twelve required appropriations bills had passed the House' before January 14 (the three being the November 2025 enacted ones), and that the new package was 'passing' additional bills, making these the 4th and 5th bills to pass the House. These are clearly among the nine remaining bills. No alternative interpretation: the criteria specifically asks for House passage of appropriations bills, not full enactment into law. All articles confirm the House voted and passed at least two FY2026 appropriations bills on January 14, well within the January 9-27 window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is YES. On January 14, 2026, the House of Representatives voted on and passed at least one (actually two) of the nine remaining FY2026 appropriations bills (Treasury/Financial Services and State/National Security) by a 341-79 majority vote. This is explicitly confirmed by multiple high-quality news sources. This occurred within the January 9-27, 2026 window. Additional appropriations bills were also passed on January 23, 2026. The first unambiguous qualifying event within the window is the January 14, 2026 vote. (Note: There may have been a qualifying vote on January 9, 2026 as well, but that date is uncertain due to conflicting reports; regardless, January 14 is clearly within the window.)

subquestions.question: Will initial jobless claims (seasonally adjusted) exceed 250,000 for any week between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-29?
subquestions.background_information:
Initial jobless claims are a leading indicator of labor market health and broader economic conditions. A significant rise in claims often precedes economic contractions as layoffs increase. The current level of initial jobless claims is around 215,000-220,000 (as of late October 2025), with recent data showing relative stability in the labor market. A surge to 250,000+ would represent a notable deterioration from current levels and could signal weakening economic momentum heading into Q4 2025. Historically, claims above 250,000 have often coincided with or preceded periods of economic weakness. The Department of Labor releases weekly unemployment insurance claims data every Thursday at 8:30 AM ET.

Sources:
- U.S. Department of Labor Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report: https://www.dol.gov/ui/data.pdf
- Current claims data (October 2025): https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/OPA/newsreleases/ui-claims/2025/20251024.pdf
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the seasonally adjusted initial jobless claims number reported by the U.S. Department of Labor for any week between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-29 (inclusive) equals or exceeds 250,000. Only the initial reported number will be used (no subsequent revisions). The data must come from the official U.S. Department of Labor Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report published at https://www.dol.gov/ui/data.pdf. If the report is delayed beyond the resolution window or data becomes unavailable, the question will resolve based on the most recent available data within the window. If no data is published during the window, the question will resolve to 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Initial jobless claims are a highly sensitive leading indicator of economic health. A significant increase in layoffs (claims exceeding 250,000) within the next month would suggest deteriorating labor market conditions that could foreshadow negative GDP growth in Q4 2025. This provides an early warning signal about economic momentum before the Q4 GDP data becomes available.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: seasonally adjusted initial jobless claims reported by U.S. DOL for ANY week between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-29 equals or exceeds 250,000. Observable evidence: official DOL Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report data. Key threshold: 250,000. Timing: any week within the inclusive window. Only the initial reported number (no revisions).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'initial jobless claims weekly unemployment insurance November 2025' to find all weekly data in window. 2) 'Department of Labor unemployment claims weekly report 250000 2025' to find any report at/above threshold. 3) 'jobless claims week ending October 25 November 1 November 8 2025 seasonally adjusted' to find specific weeks. 4) 'initial jobless claims backfill shutdown weeks official data 2025' to find backfilled shutdown data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified from official DOL reports published within the window: (1) Week ending Oct 18: 232,000 (published ~Nov 18, 2025 — released as backfill after shutdown). (2) Shutdown-period backfill weeks (Oct 25 – Nov 7): AP News confirmed 'data for the weeks during the shutdown also stayed within the 200,000–250,000 range' — no specific value at/above 250,000 reported. (3) Week ending Nov 8: 228,000 (published Nov 20, 2025). (4) Week ending Nov 15: 220,000 (published Nov 20, 2025). (5) Week ending Nov 22: 216,000 (published Nov 26, 2025). Goldman Sachs estimated ~228,000 for week ending Nov 1 (not official). No week shows SA initial claims at or exceeding 250,000.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All officially reported SA initial jobless claims values within the resolution window are well below 250,000: 232,000 [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/initial-us-jobless-claims-for-oct-18-at-232-000/3747248), 228,000 for week Nov 8 [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202511206147/first-post-shutdown-jobless-claims-report-shows-no-alarming-uptick), 220,000 for Nov 15 [CalculatedRisk](http://www.calculatedriskblog.com/2025/11/weekly-initial-unemployment-claims.html), and 216,000 for Nov 22 [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-initial-jobless-claims-down-6-000-last-week-below-expectations/3754735). AP News explicitly confirmed all shutdown-period weeks stayed 'within the 200,000–250,000 range' [AP](https://apnews.com/article/unemployment-benefits-jobless-claims-layoffs-labor-cabeb44e6d8285cf9550f35822699477). No value reached or exceeded 250,000.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The resolution window closes on 2025-11-29T23:59:59Z. The final data point in the window was published 2025-11-26 (week ending Nov 22: 216,000). All data is explicitly reported within the window and none meets or exceeds 250,000.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (≥250,000) was found in any week within the resolution window. Therefore, the first occurrence condition is moot — the threshold was never reached.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification attempts: (1) Checked for any estimates or partial data above 250,000 — Goldman Sachs estimated ~228,000 for Nov 1 week, well below threshold. (2) AP News report explicitly states all shutdown weeks stayed 'within the 200,000–250,000 range,' meaning none reached 250,000. (3) The highest confirmed official figure was 232,000 (week ending Oct 18), significantly below 250,000. (4) The trend was declining: 232,000 → 228,000 → 220,000 → 216,000. No contradictory evidence found suggesting any week hit 250,000. (5) Morningstar MarketWatch noted one article mentioned 264,000 as 'prior week' in a confusing context related to a misreading — but this refers to the 4-week average distortion during the shutdown, not an actual claims figure.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All available official DOL data for weeks within the resolution window shows SA initial jobless claims consistently below 250,000: the highest reported figure was 232,000 (week ending Oct 18, 2025). Multiple sources from the full window coverage confirm no week reached the 250,000 threshold. The question resolves No. The resolution_datetime is 2025-11-29T23:59:59Z as the window closed without the condition being met.

subquestions.question: Will Azerbaijan's Foreign Minister or President hold an official meeting with Israel's Foreign Minister or Prime Minister between October 1-31, 2025?

question: Will Trump visit Gaza by Dec 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if U.S. President Donald Trump visits the Gaza Strip by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip. Whether or not Trump enters the Gaza Strip's airspace or maritime territory during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on this market's resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, or official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a Gaza Strip border crossing (Rafah, Kerem Shalom, or Erez) reopen for civilian transit before November 13, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The reopening of Gaza border crossings is a critical indicator of normalization and security conditions in Gaza, which would be prerequisites for a presidential visit. Currently, all major crossings into Gaza are closed or severely restricted. The Rafah crossing with Egypt has been closed since May 2024 when Israel took control of it, blocking humanitarian aid. The Kerem Shalom crossing with Israel has been periodically closed due to security concerns. The Erez crossing remains closed for civilian transit. Recent peace negotiations and the Trump-brokered ceasefire have created conditions where border reopening is being discussed as part of the peace process implementation. A reopening would signal improved security conditions and diplomatic progress, making a presidential visit more feasible.

Current status (as of October 2025):
- Rafah crossing: Closed since May 2024 (Israeli control)
- Kerem Shalom: Periodically closed for security
- Erez: Closed for civilian transit

Sources:
- https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/us-senate-delegation-arrives-in-egypt-ahead-of-gazas-rafah-crossing-visit/3573740
- https://www.newsweek.com/trumps-envoy-enters-gaza-israel-hamas-ceasefire-holds-2034567
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if any of the following border crossings into the Gaza Strip (Rafah, Kerem Shalom, or Erez) officially reopens for civilian transit between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 (inclusive). Civilian transit includes passage of Palestinian civilians, international aid workers, journalists, or diplomats. Official reopening means:

1. An official announcement by the controlling authorities (Israel, Egypt, or Palestinian authorities) stating the crossing is open for civilian transit
2. Confirmed by at least two independent credible news sources reporting actual civilian movement through the crossing
3. The crossing must remain operational for at least 72 consecutive hours during the resolution period

If multiple crossings reopen, the first one to meet these criteria determines the resolution.

Primary resolution sources:
- Official government statements from Israel, Egypt, or Palestinian authorities
- UN OCHA Gaza Crossings database: https://www.ochaopt.org/data/crossings
- Major news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC, CNN) reporting on crossing status

If a crossing opens and closes multiple times, it must have at least 72 consecutive hours of operation to count. Temporary humanitarian openings that don't meet the 72-hour threshold do not count.
subquestions.rationale: The reopening of Gaza border crossings is a strong indicator of improved security conditions and diplomatic normalization in the region. If crossings remain closed through mid-November 2025, it suggests ongoing security concerns that would make a presidential visit highly unlikely. Conversely, if crossings reopen, it indicates sufficient stability and diplomatic progress to potentially facilitate high-level visits. This question provides an early signal about whether the conditions necessary for a Trump visit to Gaza are developing, without simply being the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for YES: Any of Rafah, Kerem Shalom, or Erez border crossings officially reopens for civilian transit (Palestinian civilians, international aid workers, journalists, or diplomats as people physically crossing) between Oct 14 - Nov 13, 2025, confirmed by at least two independent credible news sources reporting actual civilian movement, with at least 72 consecutive hours of operation. evidence.step8_final_decision: No: Throughout the entire Oct 14 - Nov 13, 2025 window, none of the three named border crossings (Rafah, Kerem Shalom, Erez) reopened for civilian transit meeting all resolution criteria. Rafah remained closed 'until further notice' per Netanyahu. Kerem Shalom/Kissufim operated for humanitarian aid goods but were interrupted (closed Oct 19, reopened Oct 20), the 72-hour continuous operation requirement was not met, and there is no confirmed civilian people transit through these crossings. Erez remained closed. The question resolves No as the window closed with no qualifying event. Since no discrete 'definitively impossible' event occurred earlier — the situation remained contingent throughout — the resolution datetime is the end of the window.

question: Will Iran withdraw from the NPT in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran formally notifies the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), pursuant to Article X of the treaty by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

To qualify, the Iranian government must issue an official written notice that explicitly states its intention to withdraw under Article X of the NPT.

The resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Iran's parliament formally approve a bill to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Recent news reports indicate that Iran's parliament has begun drafting legislation to withdraw from the NPT in response to European countries triggering snapback sanctions. According to Iranian lawmakers, a bill for NPT withdrawal is expected to be presented and voted on within the next week. Parliamentary approval of such legislation would represent a significant escalation in Iran's nuclear policy and could indicate a formal withdrawal process is underway. Current parliamentary procedures in Iran typically involve bill introduction, committee review, and final approval by the Majlis (parliament). The Iranian parliament has previously used legislative action to signal policy shifts on nuclear matters, such as when it passed the Strategic Action Plan to Lift Sanctions in 2020. Parliamentary approval of withdrawal legislation would be a strong indicator of Iran's intent to follow through with formal NPT withdrawal.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Iran's parliament (Majlis) officially approves a bill specifically authorizing withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive). Approval must be confirmed through official parliamentary records, state media reports from Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA) or official parliament website announcements. The bill must explicitly mention withdrawal from the NPT or Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. If multiple parliamentary approvals occur, the first approval date within the resolution window determines the outcome. If parliamentary approval occurs but is subsequently vetoed or overturned by other government bodies, the question still resolves YES based on the parliamentary approval. Resolution will be determined using official sources including IRNA (https://en.irna.ir/), the Iranian parliament official website (https://en.parliran.ir/), and official state media reports.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly addresses whether Iran's legislative body takes the formal step of approving withdrawal legislation, which would be a crucial precursor to actual NPT withdrawal. Parliamentary approval would indicate serious government commitment to withdrawal and would likely precede any formal notification to the UN. Given the recent parliamentary activity reported in news articles and the stated timeline for consideration, this question provides an early indicator of whether Iran is moving forward with withdrawal procedures within the next month.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Iran's Majlis must formally approve (pass a vote on) a bill explicitly authorizing NPT withdrawal between September 1–October 1, 2025. Observable evidence: Official parliamentary vote result, IRNA or state media report confirming approval. Key entities: Iranian Parliament (Majlis), NPT withdrawal bill. Threshold: Formal approval by full parliament (not just committee).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Iran parliament Majlis NPT Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty withdrawal bill 2025' (general search); 2) 'Iran NPT withdrawal bill approved September 2025' (specific approval search); 3) 'Iran Majlis parliament vote NPT withdrawal approved passed October 2025' (vote result search); 4) 'Iran parliament NPT withdrawal bill vote result September 2025' (vote outcome search); 5) 'Iran Majlis NPT nuclear treaty withdrawal approved October 2025' (broader window search)
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Sept 7: Parliament set to debate bill under 'triple urgency' - no vote result reported; (2) Sept 22: Motion 'finalized, ready for vote' per Tasnim - not yet on agenda; (3) Sept 28: Parliament convened closed-door session to discuss NPT withdrawal after snapback sanctions took effect - no vote reported; (4) Sept 29: Commission finalized draft but 'not yet placed on Parliament's agenda' (multiple sources); (5) Oct 1: Committee met with SNSC Secretary Larijani to discuss nuclear file - draft 'not yet placed on parliamentary agenda'. All events rejected as qualifying events because none represent a formal parliamentary vote/approval of the NPT withdrawal bill.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence matches the resolution criteria. Multiple sources from September 29 explicitly state the draft had 'not yet been placed on Parliament's agenda' ([Mehr News Agency](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/237113/Draft-on-Iran-s-NPT-exit-finalized-Parliament-to-decide), [Tasnim](https://www.tasnimnews.com/en/news/2025/09/29/3411045/commission-finalizes-draft-on-iran-s-npt-withdrawal-parliament-yet-to-decide), [Tehran Times](https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/518600/Lawmakers-urge-stronger-coordination-on-nuclear-issue-in-meeting)). October 1 articles confirm the draft was still not on the agenda. [AP report](https://apnews.com/article/iran-snapback-sanctions-nuclear-us-israel-war-c3864332df26e886eaa2922f807e0ec5) from Sept 28 confirms parliament entered closed-door session to 'discuss' NPT withdrawal — not vote on it.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a formal parliamentary approval because no such approval occurred within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (formal parliamentary approval of NPT withdrawal bill) was found in the entire resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources (AP, Mehr News Agency, Tasnim, Tehran Times, Adnkronos, Euronews) consistently report that as of September 29–October 1, 2025, the NPT withdrawal bill had been drafted and finalized by committee but had NOT been placed on the parliamentary agenda for a full vote. President Pezeshkian also publicly ruled out NPT withdrawal. No source reports a formal parliamentary vote approval. The evidence is consistent and unambiguous.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves NO. The Iranian parliament did NOT formally approve a bill to withdraw from the NPT between September 1 and October 1, 2025. While there was significant parliamentary activity around the issue — debate, committee drafting, urgency designations, and closed-door sessions — the bill was never formally voted on by the full parliament within the resolution window. As of October 1, 2025, multiple credible sources confirm the draft had not yet been placed on parliament's agenda for a vote. The window closed on October 1, 2025.

question: Will less than 12 named storms occur in the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season?
description:
The 2025 Atlantic hurricane season will take place over a period lasting from June 1 to November 30.

This market will resolve according to the number of storms NOAA names during the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season.

Storms that form before the designated period but which are active during it will count towards this market's resolution.

If a number of storms exceeding a bracket's number are named within this market's timeframe, that bracket may immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be NOAA’s list of named storms during the Atlantic hurricane season (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/) and/or their data on individual storms.

If there is a potential named storm that has not yet been classified by Nov 30, 11:59 PM ET, the market may remain open until Dec 1, 12:00 PM ET to determine if a classification was made prior to midnight.

subquestions.question: Will NOAA issue a Potential Tropical Cyclone Advisory for a system in the Atlantic Basin with at least a 50% chance of tropical cyclone formation within 48 hours between October 1-11, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Potential Tropical Cyclone (PTC) advisories are issued by NOAA's National Hurricane Center for systems that are not yet tropical cyclones but pose a threat of tropical storm or hurricane conditions to land areas within 48 hours. This allows for earlier watches and warnings. The current 2025 Atlantic hurricane season has been predicted to be above-average with 13-19 named storms forecasted. As of October 1, 2025, there have been only 6 named storms (Erin and 5 others based on the naming sequence), which is below the seasonal average pace. A PTC advisory during October 1-11 would indicate active tropical development during what is typically still peak season, potentially contributing to the total named storm count. The Atlantic hurricane season typically remains active through October, with historical records showing many late-season storms. Sources: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/aboutprodday.shtml, https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/text/refresh/MIATCPAT1+shtml/010233.shtml
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if NOAA's National Hurricane Center issues a Potential Tropical Cyclone Advisory (product identifier MIATCPAT1-5) for any system in the Atlantic Basin (including Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico) between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-11 23:59:59 UTC, where the advisory text indicates at least a 50% chance of tropical cyclone formation within 48 hours. The advisory must be publicly available on the NHC website (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/text/). If multiple advisories are issued for the same system, only the first advisory meeting the criteria counts. Resolution will be determined using the official NHC advisory archive (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2025/).
subquestions.rationale: A Potential Tropical Cyclone Advisory with high formation probability during this period would indicate active tropical development late in the peak season, potentially leading to additional named storms. Since the ultimate question concerns whether total named storms will remain below 12, and only 6 storms have been named as of October 1st, any additional tropical development in early October increases the likelihood of reaching or exceeding 12 named storms for the season. This serves as an early indicator of whether the season will remain relatively quiet or become more active late in the year.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: NOAA NHC must issue a Potential Tropical Cyclone Advisory (product MIATCPAT1-5) for an Atlantic Basin system between Oct 1-11, 2025, with at least 50% TC formation chance within 48 hours. This is a distinct product from the Tropical Weather Outlook - it's issued only when a pre-TC system threatens land. Observable evidence: explicit text of MIATCPAT advisory on NHC website.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'NOAA NHC Potential Tropical Cyclone Advisory Atlantic October 2025' - to find explicit MIATCPAT advisories; 2) 'Tropical Storm Jerry formation AL95 Invest 95L advisory October 6 7 2025' - to find Jerry's formation details; 3) 'NHC MIATCPAT1 advisory October Atlantic 2025' - to find specific product; 4) 'Potential Tropical Cyclone advisory NHC Jerry October 2025 MIATCPAT' - to find specific product references
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Invest 95L/AL95 had 50% 48-hr development chance on Oct 6 per multiple sources (WKMG, Orlando Sentinel, Newsweek, Breakingbelizenews). (2) Tropical Storm Jerry formed Oct 7 at 11am ET from Invest 95L 'directly' without passing through tropical depression stage. (3) Gainesville Sun article notes NHC may issue advisories before a storm forms if near land. REJECTED: No source explicitly confirms a MIATCPAT advisory product was issued - only Tropical Weather Outlook entries are documented in search results.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution requires the specific MIATCPAT product type, not just a system with 50%+ development probability in the Tropical Weather Outlook. The MIATCPAT is issued when an unorganized system threatens land before becoming a TC. Sources confirm Jerry formed far from land (~1,300 miles east of northern Leeward Islands) when first advisory was issued at 11am Oct 7 - this was a regular TC advisory (MIATCEAT for Tropical Storm Jerry), not a MIATCPAT. Gainesville Sun: 'NHC may issue advisories even before a storm forms if it poses a threat near land' - but no source explicitly states such an advisory was issued for this system.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Cannot extract a reliable timestamp for a MIATCPAT advisory issuance because no source explicitly confirms such a product was issued. The 50% 48-hour probability was documented on October 6, 2025 (WKMG article, Orlando Sentinel, Newsweek, Breakingbelizenews), but this refers to the Tropical Weather Outlook, not a MIATCPAT advisory.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying MIATCPAT occurrence found. The system (Invest 95L) progressed from 40% on Oct 5 to 50% on Oct 6 to 70-80% on Oct 7 before becoming Jerry directly. No evidence of a MIATCPAT product being issued at any point.

subquestions.question: Will the FDIC Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF) reserve ratio fall below 1.75% as reported in any quarterly report published between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12?
subquestions.background_information:
The FDIC Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF) is the primary backstop for bank failures, with its reserve ratio indicating the fund's capacity to cover insured deposits. A declining ratio suggests increased stress on the banking system. The FDIC is required by law to maintain a minimum reserve ratio of 2%, but the agency has been rebuilding the fund since it fell below this level during the pandemic. Recent FDIC reports indicate the DIF is approaching its target ratio, with a projected return to 2% by end of 2025. However, if the ratio were to fall significantly below current levels during the monitoring period, it could signal emerging stress in the banking sector that might precede bank failures. Current DIF reserve ratio stands at approximately 2.0% as of Q3 2025.

- https://www.fdic.gov/news/press-releases/2025/pr25068.html
- https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance-fund/
- https://pymnts.com/banking/2025/fdic-deposit-insurance-fund-nears-legal-target-ratio/

The ratio will be determined using the 'Reserve Ratio' figure as reported in the official FDIC publication. If multiple reports are published during this period, the first report showing a ratio below 1.75% will trigger resolution. If no such report is published by 2026-01-12 23:59:59 UTC, the question resolves NO. subquestions.rationale: A significant decline in the DIF reserve ratio below 1.75% would indicate emerging stress in the banking system that could precede bank failures. This provides an early warning indicator for the ultimate question about bank failures by March 31, 2026, as fund depletion often correlates with increased bank stress.

question: Will ChatGPT reach 1b monthly active users in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ChatGPT reaches 1 billion monthly active users (MAUs) during by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PMET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The primary resolution source will be official information from OpenAI, however a consensus of reputable sources including, major analytics firms (e.g. Similarweb, Sensor Tower), investor or regulatory disclosures, or reputable media may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will ChatGPT's weekly active users grow by at least 10% between August 2025 and September 2025?
subquestions.background_information: ChatGPT has demonstrated rapid growth, reaching approximately 700 million weekly active users as of early August 2025 according to OpenAI executives. This represents a 4x increase from the previous year. To reach 1 billion monthly active users by December 2025, ChatGPT would need to maintain strong growth momentum. A 10% monthly growth rate in weekly users would indicate continued expansion that could support reaching the ultimate target. Weekly active user growth is a leading indicator for monthly active user growth, as increased weekly engagement typically translates to higher monthly user counts. Current weekly user count is approximately 700M (as of early August 2025).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if official OpenAI reporting or consensus among reputable analytics firms (Similarweb, Sensor Tower) shows that ChatGPT's weekly active user count increased by at least 10% between the week of August 4-10, 2025 and the week of September 1-7, 2025. The comparison must use comparable measurement periods (both weekly counts). If no official data is published by October 1, 2025, but multiple reputable analytics firms (Similarweb, Sensor Tower) show consensus on ≥10% growth, that consensus will be used. This question resolves No if growth is less than 10% or if user count decreases. The resolution will be determined using data published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Primary source: OpenAI official communications (https://openai.com/blog). Secondary sources: Similarweb (https://www.similarweb.com/), Sensor Tower (https://sensortower.com/).
subquestions.rationale: Weekly active user growth is a leading indicator for monthly active user growth. If ChatGPT cannot maintain at least 10% monthly growth during this critical period following the GPT-5 launch, it suggests diminishing growth momentum that would make reaching 1B MAUs by year-end less likely. This subquestion provides an early signal about whether user adoption is accelerating or decelerating post-major-update.

evidence.step1_decompose: Requires explicit week-specific data: (1) ChatGPT WAU for week of Aug 4-10, 2025; (2) ChatGPT WAU for week of Sep 1-7, 2025; (3) verified ≥10% growth between those two comparable weekly periods; sourced from OpenAI official communications OR consensus from Similarweb/Sensor Tower; published Sep 1 – Oct 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'ChatGPT weekly active users growth August September 2025'; (2) 'OpenAI ChatGPT user statistics 2025'; (3) 'ChatGPT weekly users 700 million August 2025 specific week count'; (4) 'Similarweb Sensor Tower ChatGPT traffic analytics August September 2025'; (5) 'ChatGPT weekly users week August 4-10 September 1-7 2025 comparison'; (6) 'OpenAI blog ChatGPT active users report September 2025'. All intended to find precise, dated, week-level user count data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: All found articles cite a general '700 million weekly active users' figure attributed to OpenAI (as of approximately July 2025). No article provides: (a) specific WAU counts for the individual weeks of Aug 4-10 or Sep 1-7, (b) week-over-week comparison between those two periods, or (c) Similarweb/Sensor Tower analytics showing growth between those specific weeks. The OpenAI NBER paper released Sept 15 covers usage trends up to July 2025 but provides only trend-level data, not specific weekly comparisons. The Drum article (Sep 29) notes '700 million weekly users... four times the number from last year' and '200 million new users in last six months' but does not provide the precise weekly comparison required.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No source explicitly provides the required week-specific comparison. Available data from OpenAI's September 15, 2025 NBER study [Ars Technica](https://arstechnica.com/ai/2025/09/seven-things-we-learned-from-openais-first-study-on-chatgpt-usage/) and [Search Engine Land](https://searchengineland.com/openai-staffing-chatgpt-ad-platform-462554) only cite '700 million WAU as of August 2025' as an aggregate figure — not a specific weekly count. Similarweb data found only covers referral traffic patterns, not WAU comparisons between specific weeks. No Sensor Tower data found at all for this period.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event (week-specific WAU comparison showing ≥10% growth) found, so no timestamp can be extracted.
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checked all major sources. The 700 million WAU figure is widely cited but as an aggregate milestone, not a week-specific measurement. One source (The Paradox of AI, Medium) even frames 700 million as a 'projection' for August 2025, suggesting the actual weekly measurements are not granularly tracked or reported publicly. Similarweb's data found in the window relates to referral traffic, not WAU. No Sensor Tower data specific to ChatGPT WAU comparisons was found. No contradictory evidence (e.g., a confirmed decline) was found either — the data is simply absent at the required granularity.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria require explicit, verifiable data comparing ChatGPT's WAU for the specific weeks of Aug 4-10 and Sep 1-7, 2025, from official OpenAI communications or consensus from Similarweb/Sensor Tower. No such data was published in the required window. The only WAU data available is an aggregate '700 million' milestone figure that is not broken down into specific weekly comparisons. This fails Evidence Requirements #1 (direct match to criteria), #2 (explicitly stated), and #4 (reliable timestamp). Therefore: resolvable=false.
